The CEO and the management team are always available to anyone who has a suggestion, strategy, improvement or who simply wants to give some feedback. 82

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The Reluctant CEO “The desire to be a politician should bar you for life from ever becoming one
searchIndex.text: Whatever your position. Whatever your age or years of experience. Whatever your idea. It can be a little chaotic at times but that is the price of decentralized growth. As we all know, success doesn’t come easy. So, how far are you willing to go? Product testing in the early days usually meant loading assorted parts and components into a small car late at night and heading off to remote areas of the country to test out equipment. Late nights and rural areas were chosen to minimize the damage if testing turned out to be unsuccessful. Often testing equipment in extreme heat or torrential rain . Lots of sleepless nights and plenty of failures and flops. And yet, Phally and his team recalls this time fondly. The time when VP.Start demonstrated unflinchingly why they had given their company the moniker of a “very powerful” start. It was at this time that the company slogan was created as well. Innovation through Technology. From the very beginning, Phally wanted to make it clear that innovation and technology are not the same thing . Both are mission critical and one, technology, is the result of the other, innovation. That’s why it must be “innovation through technology” and never “technology through innovation.” If innovation does not come first, it will never come at all. In the VP.Start mindset, technology is something that you can build and 83 upgrade and customize and optimize . It is constantly changing. A company can imitate the technology of others and other companies can copy yours as well. Technology leads to competition. It is the domain of engineers and technicians and skilled specialists. VP.Start has no intention of knocking technology but VP.Start was not founded to be a product-driven tech engineering or manufacturing company . Nothing wrong with those kinds of companies. But they are not VP.Start! Innovation is creative thinking, outside the box ideas. It is a series of groundbreaking ideas that transform and revolutionize, that challenge the norms of conventional wisdom. Building a product like the DRC is technology and manufacturing, testing and quality control, sales and marketing, engineering. On the other hand, seeing that the key to modernizing the electric grid is harnessing and leveraging the existing, aging infrastructure, recognizing that this crumbling infrastructure can be part of the solution as much as it is part of the problem, that is innovation . Technology can come from researching other companies’ products, following the latest news and keeping abreast of the most recent trends in the tech world. 84

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The Reluctant CEO “The desire to be a politician should bar you for life from ever becoming one
searchIndex.text: It can also be as simple as updating or upgrading your own products. It can come from any number of sources. But technology is, by definition, derivative . Again, to be clear, this is not to belittle technology or engineering. But from the SIMA Journey perspective, it is not the optimizers and customizers who change the world; it is the thinkers and dreamers and innovators . True innovation leads to new technologies. New technologies comes from true innovation. Always. Technology is the realm of the followers while innovation is the kingdom of the lead actors. To restate the obvious, I must emphasize again, there is nothing wrong with being a follower. VP.Start appreciates deeply the skilled team of engineers who bring their innovations to reality. At the same time, while Phally may be many things, he certainly is not a follower . VP.Start has amazing technology, to be sure, but it is all through and as a result of innovation. Innovation through technology . In his speeches, especially to high school and university students, Phally focuses a lot of his attention on creative thinking and innovation. He puts it this way. “Technology without innovation is little more than toys on the playground. By the same token, innovation without technology is mere daydreaming and science f iction. 85 But when innovation leads to technology, a revolution is unleashed to transform the world. That is the lofty objective that VP.Start aspires to. Do you dare allow yourself to be a leader, an innovator, a creator, a thinker, a founder? ” Phally boldly poses the same question to you. He insists that everyone is an innovator by nature. Innovation is the lifeblood of the universe and everyone is born into this world with the DNA of innovation. “DNA” to Phally means “Dreaming New Advancements”, by the way. So, are you ready to take up your birthright and become the innovator that you are? Are you ready to be radically authentic? Are you prepared for the challenge of dedicating your life to your dreams without reservation? Are you willing to have the confidence to believe in yourself, the way the universe believes in you? Are you ready to start your journey of “innovation through technology”? 86

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Story The Growing Pains of VP
searchIndex.text: Chapter 6 The SIMA Story The Growing Pains of VP.Start “Unfortunately, resilience matters in success. I don’t know how to teach it to you except for I hope suffering happens to you.” -Jensen Huang, CEO of NVidia Why are times of growth often more challenging than times of failure? How do you overcome the bottleneck of your own success? With the implementation of the DRC technologies into the electric grid, with the providing of SCADA technology to the EDC utility branches throughout Cambodia and with the increasing partnering with the EDC and other electric licensees, for the first time in its brief existence, VP.Start began to experience a degree of success. 87 Beyond mere survival. VP.Start started to move from its very powerful start to the next stage of its growth. VP.Start began hiring new employees, establishing a more permanent headquarters, the Sen Sok Valley Campus, and improving the DRC through various iterations. Each of these steps were opportunities and potential pitfalls at the same time. As with many companies in the early stages, rapid growth did not always play out smoothly. Why is it so hard to transition the corporate culture as your business grows? One challenge that many startups face is the corporate culture transition from the small, close-knit group of friends and family members who started the business to a burgeoning team of skilled and more specialized experts. This problem was further exacerbated by Phally’s insistence that staff were free to depart VP.Start whenever so inclined. No coercion to stay. No pressure to stay. No encouragement to stay beyond the excitement of innovation itself. If the thrill of being on the cutting edge of the sustainability revolution was not enough to hold your loyalty to VP.Start, If the desire to make a massive difference in the future of Cambodia was not enough to keep your focus on the prize, it was probably inevitable and even preferable that you leave anyway. Leave and make room for others who were more aligned with the vision. To paraphrase the lyrics of Juice Newton, “There’ll be no strings to bind your hands, Not if love of innovation can’t bind your heart.” 88

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Story The Growing Pains of VP
searchIndex.text: In such a freewheeling and open-minded atmosphere, even small disputes and disagreements might be a cause for a valuable team member with a difficult to replace skill set and level of expertise to decide to up and leave. And to take others along with him or her. And to speak ill of the company once they had left. And that is exactly what happened. More than a few times . How do you clean up the mess after key team members abruptly leave? How do you make your workplace a place that employess want to stay at? One lesson that Phally and the new management team of VP.Start had to learn the hard way, was the mission critical nature of damage control . As a wide-eyed true believer in innovation and the solutions that VP.Start were creating, it was hard for Phally to imagine that anyone would ever want to leave the company. Especially, over such minor issues as working conditions, schedules, promotions and salaries. Of course, to many team members, these were hardly minor issues. When you are “all in” as the management team definitely was, you are tempted to think that everyone else is as all in as you are. As long as VP.Start was striving for a sustainable future , the management team seemed to think, All other matters would pale in importance. That, VP.Start learned, was a seriously erroneous perspective. How do we avoid the fallacy that since we care so much about our vision and dreams, everyone else must feel the same as we do? 89 Word began to be spread that Phally might be hard to work for , salaries might be less than desired, schedules might be harder than hoped for, working conditions might be less than ideal and so on. These innuendos may have been exaggerated and overblown but it would be hard to deny that there was some element of truth in the background. For someone like CEO Phally, who cared nothing about money, fame, prestige, awards or positions, the trappings of business success that most others sought after, how could he be made to understand that others did not always share his detachment from attachments? What are some of the challenges of moving to a new location and upgrading your facilities? The inauguration of the Sen Sok Valley Campus was another major step forward for VP.Start. But this undeniable milestone, too, was not without its own challenges . First of all, at this point in time, the moniker, “campus”, might have been more aspirational than actual . Positive thinking, yes! A bit of a stretch, yes to that, too! The “campus” was a small area of warehouses and workshops in the Sen Sok district of Phnom Penh, a growing but still somewhat gritty suburb. Just off of a main street but facing on to on a dirt road. 90

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Story The Growing Pains of VP
searchIndex.text: Surrounded by shops peddling snacks and meals for day laborers. Sen Sok was a district slowly and noticeably on the rise but at this point, still struggling to escape from its humble beginnings. In its own way, it was a very fitting place for VP.Start to take its first stand in the business world. Furthermore, there is no valley in Sen Sok to justify the name Sen Sok Valley Campus. The “valley” was added by VP.Start to compare itself to Silicon Valley. Bold, audacious and visionary but also a little bit over the top! As a matter of fact, there was no valley and truthfully, no campus, at this point, either. At least, not in the normal meaning of the word. There were some rented spaces in a corrugated compound, hints of potential growth but still ramshackle and unrefined…… Why is upgrading a product often more challenging than inventing the product in the first place? The development of the DRC through its various iterations, unsurprisingly, was also not without its challenges and issues. The original DRC concept was a remote control system to monitor grid data, to collect the data for grid function improvement and to pinpoint anomalies and flaws, to reduce outages or to stop them before they happened. Radically simple, radically cost-effective, radically groundbreaking. Plug and play, easy to install, 91 intuitive to use and adaptable to the existing infrastructure. However, this last point, which was a key aspect of the affordability of the grid modernization solutions of VP.Start, was also the source of a major potential dilemma. The electric grid in Cambodia was made up of infrastructure imported from various providers from all over the world. Complicated and somewhat haphazard. Different protocols, different parameters, different specifications. The original DRC solution would need to be modified to meet the various needs of each piece of infrastructure, depending on the company that provided this equipment. In other words, the DRC would have to be modified over and over again. Furthermore, at this point, these modifications would need to be carried out at the “campus”, a campus with limited testing facilities, limited research and development, limited quality control, a limited production line and a significantly limited, if growing, team of technical experts. The revenue required to upgrade these facilities needed to come from selling the products. But simultaneously, the products could not be developed without upgraded facilities. Outside investment was interested but not ready to commit. A serious bottleneck was forming that threatened growth and success. 92

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Story The Growing Pains of VP
searchIndex.text: How do you create an innovative business in a conventional world? How do you break the traditional rules of business and take bold risks without being seen as “risky” and “out of control” by investors and stakeholders? Additionally, while Phally and the VP.Start management team were determined to upset the apple cart of traditional grid modernization, they had to deal with the struggles and challenges of stabilizing and expanding their business at the same time. Let’s be honest, dear readers . Investors tend to prefer safe investments, especially when investing in a developing country like Cambodia. Banks tend to prefer companies that follow the traditional business growth model. Government ministries tend to select and support firms that stay within established patterns and conventional frameworks. VP.Start refused to play it safe. And, at times, they paid the price. Former US President Theodore Roosevelt once said, “Believe you can and you’re halfway there.” While these encouraging words may be true, this certainly does not mean that each step will be easy or that you may not feel like giving up at times. But Phally refused to bend, to change, to give up his perspective. “ Yes, you will feel like giving up. Sure, you will get discouraged. 93 Undoubtedly, you will want to quit. Not might. Not could. You will. After all, if you never feel like giving up, it means that you are not accomplishing anything important. The frustration, the doubt, the discouragement, the feeling of accomplishing nothing, learning nothing, knowing nothing, these feelings are natural for anyone that has a growth mindset. They are universal. Accept the frustration, welcome the disappointment, embrace the failures, admit the feelings of despair and discouragement but don’t let them consume you . Let these feelings be your fuel to achieve personal and professional exponential growth. The moment you stop feeling these feelings, you have stopped growing. Nature presents us with only two choices: grow or die.” “When you feel like you know nothing and have accomplished nothing and can do nothing, you are in good company. All of the great creative minds, Socrates and Aristotle, Confucius and Einstein, Steve Jobs and Oscar Wilde, Even Buddha himself, and, indeed, all the great innovators and thinkers of our world felt the same way . The path to enlightenment is the path of self-disillusionment. If you believe in your ability and rest on your laurels, you will cease to grow. 94

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: If you look at the vastness of the universe and the power of nature And if you dare to dream, Nothing will be impossible for you.” Do you see your dilemmas and difficulties and predicaments as opportunities? What are the challenges that you are FORTUNATE enough to face in your personal life? In your career? In your company’s development? Are you accomplishing something so significant that at times you feel doubt and discouragement? Are you ready to turn that into the fuel that rockets you forward? 95 Chapter 7 The SIMA Story VP.Start Begins to Raise its Voice “The first principle is that you must not fool yourself and you are the easiest person to fool.” -Richard Feynman, Professor and Nobel Laureate Why do successful achievements often take us by surprise? As grid modernization proceeded across Cambodia, a funny thing happened. A simultaneously both unexpected and completely expected development. The DRC technology in its ever improving and expanding iterations and the SCADA system, the network collecting and displaying the DRC data, started to dramatically improve electric grid reliability in Cambodia. In a very short period of years, outages had been reduced dramatically, energy waste had been trimmed, processes had been streamlined and, most importantly and most noticeably to the utilities and electricity consumers of Cambodia, the grid had become more dependable . Coverage had been expanded and extended to even more remote areas and, so by the same token, the quality of electric service became more equitable. Businesses were increasingly able to plan and develop products at full capacity, universities were able to accelerate research and establish connections with academic institutions in other countries, families were able to live tangibly more comfortable lives, healthcare became more effective and dependable, especially in remote regions, 96

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: construction work became smoother and quicker and so on and so on. In other words, since the electric grid is at the foundation of almost all aspects of modern life , modernizing the electric grid led to significant knock-on improvements in virtually every facet of quality of life. Why is grid modernization so mission critical and foundational to success? What are the key developments that would be foundational to your success? As the grid became more energy efficient , it also became more favorable to the adoption and increase of renewable energy usage. Furthermore, it became more affordable for customers. For the first time, there was starting to be the stirring of interest in VP.Start’s technologies outside of Cambodia as well. Visitors began arriving from ASEAN member nations, as well as, India, Japan, China, Taiwan and even US universities, such as the University of Louisville. This growth coincided with a major expansion of the Sen Sok Valley Campus. What are the rewards and affirmations that you seek after? VP.Start, at this time, began to receive awards, international certifications, increased government and utility contracts. VP.Start began to forge connections with investors, potential collaborative partners, and leaders of academia and government ministries. But as always, Phally was not very concerned about the connections or impressed with the awards garnered. He was respectful and he appreciated the acclaim but 97 he was not that excited about the people he met or the awards VP.Start got. The only reward that mattered, in his view, was being yourself, a better version of yourself. He felt could learn as much from making a connection with a street vendor or a tuk tuk driver as from a government minister or a famous professor. As a matter of fact, he would say that he could probably learn more from a street vendor or tuk tuk driver than the others because they have never been customised and compromised by society, academia, government or industry. They are true to themselves. Be that as it may, VP.Start was making a “very powerful” start, moving forward aggressively, developing new products, meeting new customers and chasing the dream of a reliable and affordable electric grid for all Cambodians in all parts of the country. It was an amazing turn of events, a spectacular, nearly miraculous, transition from a company without anything going for it except powerful ideas to turn into a burgeoning success story, a veritable “out of nowhere” success story , a company growing from the ground up, from scratch , rapid fire, exponentially. This growth would have surely shocked and awed anyone else except Phally but for him, the only question had never been whether VP.Start would succeed or not, 98

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: but why was success taking so long? He knew that VP.Start had the answers in-house and in hand , to grid modernization in a plug and play format with the DRC technology and the SCADA system, a system that could often be installed in fifteen minutes or less and that used existing infrastructure to keep costs at less than one-hundredth of traditional and conventional grid modernization strategies. With home grown innovations like these already being deployed, Phally knew that it was just a matter of time before these innovations would become mainstream and VP.Start would become a major player. Confidence has never been an issue for Phally. His frustration was that success was not forthcoming immediately . What was the bottleneck? Branding? Advertising? Market research? As important as all of these certainly are, CEO Phally realised that the real problem didn’t lie in any of these areas. VP.Start needed a voice , a powerful voice to match their very powerful start. A voice full of passion and energy, a voice replete with wisdom and storytelling, with philosophy and the power of persuasion. VP.Start needed a mesmerizing, captivating, enthralling voice. And Phally knew full well that that voice would have to come from Phally, 99 himself. Technology could be developed and tested by others , innovations could be implemented by others , DRC and SCADA systems and RPM Grids could be optimized by others , plans could be made by others , projects could be inaugurated and organized by others , but at the end of the day, Phally was going to have be the one to raise a powerful, articulate, positive voice on behalf of VP.Start. What do you care enough to RAISE YOUR VOICE about? A conventional voice would never do. Never be sufficient. Never be adequate. How could VP.Start tell the world that it was an innovative firm, prepared to break the rules, embrace nonconformity, take risks, go completely outside the comfort zone and challenge all traditional norms and conventional approaches , indeed, how could VP.Start dare to claim that, unless it had an revolutionary and unconventional voice? If you believe in yourself, follow your dreams, refuse to concede and become yourself, You will have amazing innovation and undeniable success. Are you expecting success or will it take you by surprise? 100

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: “Until you spread your wings, you’ll have no idea how far you can fly!” -Napoleon When it is time to take the plunge, are you prepared to jump? Or will you be left behind? As VP.Start started to grow and gain more success in business, Phally started to face three new predicaments, challenges that he had never had to navigate before, obstacles that were actually golden opportunities disguised as difficulties . First of all, if the grid could be modernized and made data-driven and that data could be harnessed for simulations and applications, was that the final destination? Or were there more innovative solutions still to be built on the foundation of a reliable energy source? Secondly, since VP.Start had been able to deploy grid ecosolutions that were already starting to work powerfully for Cambodia, why wouldn’t they work in other countries, as well, especially developing countries that were faced with similar grid issues? Finally, and perhaps most critically, how was VP.Start ever going to become the company that it must become without Phally developing a powerful, persuasive voice in English that was, Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP.Start Begins to Spread Its Wings 103 as he likes to say, “beyond native speaker level”? This was not a criticism of the Khmer language, per se, but a clear recognition that on the global stage, English was mission critical. Not just good and proper English, correct and fluent English, not even native speaker English. After all, there were already hundreds of millions of native speakers all over the world. Merely matching their ability was never going to be good enough for Phally. One the first question, as it became increasingly clear to Phally and the VP.Start management team that grid modernization based on the DRC technology was assured to be a success in Cambodia in conjunction with the Cambodian utility, EDC, a new question arose in their minds. Is that enough? Have we already arrived at the end of the journey? Surely not. So, what is the next step once the grid has become modernized, smart and intelligent? Where do we go next? The VP.Start team began to see that grid modernization was just getting the ball rolling, if you will. Laying the foundation. Taking the first step. After all, until you have a reliable source of electricity, how can you even consider attracting meaningful external investment? How can you even try to incorporate more renewables into the power system? How can you even start to move towards energy independence? How can you even imagine the education sector beginning to leverage the power of WiFi and the internet, 104

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: machine learning and the advancements of AI, if they can’t depend on their source of electricity? How can you even hope for industry to grow and expand when deadlines are missed and product development is delayed, testing is made unreliable and pilot projects fail due to the lack of a dependable energy source? How can you even dream of families living a comfortable and convenient life when appliances are undependable, air conditioning is exorbitantly unafforable and electric lighting is unstable and unreliable? Consider, try, start, imagine, hope, dream. All of these verbs were waiting on reliable electricity to make them operable. As the VP.Start team had come to see, everything depended on electricity and a ample, reliable supply thereof. But if a lack of reliable electricity hampers and hinders, damages and ruins everything, then, what does having a dependable supply of energy bring to the table? What benefits accrue from having the solid foundation of a sustainable grid? Allow me to answer that: Once you have successfully modernized and smartened the grid, made it data-driven and dependable, affordable and equitable across the spectrum, and made power outages infrequent and by harnessing the DRC technology, easy to spot and solve remotely and instantly when they do happen, Why do we need to stop there? Now that you have a solid foundation to build on, why not start building skyscrapers of innovative ideas ? 105 What are the real-world problems that you face personally? What do your ideas and innovation do to alleviate these issues? As we know but occasionally seem to forget, it is pretty nearly impossible to solve a problem until you know clearly and exactly what the problem is. Fortunately, Phally and the VP.Start team were not just innovators and researchers. They didn’t live in a fictional world of affluence and comfort. They were also ordinary electricity consumers just like everyone else. They similarly experienced the same hardships and inconveniences when power was down as everyone else did. They faced the same challenges in garnering investment and meeting deadlines and testing products. They also faced the same inconveniences in their personal home lives that came from dealing with unreliable energy sources. This deep familiarity with the real-world problems of a third world country like Cambodia is what especially empowered them to get off the fence and make an assault on these problems proactively and relentlessly. In other words, they pushed grid modernization as if their lives depended on it, because, in a sense, their lives did. What are the benefits and drawbacks of urban life in your city? How can we augment the benefits while mitigating the drawbacks? In the same way, Phally and his team were urban dwellers, living in the beautiful, challenging, glorious and frustrating city of Phnom Penh , a city with its own unique set of colonial charm, riverfront beauty and suburban sprawl. 106

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: Phnom Penh is a rapidly growing capital city, a beacon for radical urbanization , in a country that is still largely rural and agricultural for the most part. Phnom Penh is increasingly a city of skyscrapers and towering apartment buildings, of old alleys and lanes juxtaposed with modern highways and major roads, a city with a modern core area around the royal palace along the Tonle Sap riverfront that is full of trendy bars and international restaurants and high end hotels as well as backpacker establishments. A second layer of Phnom Penh spreads out from the riverfront area with some exclusive neighborhoods and gated communities and boutique shops spreading out in a semi-circle from the central area. As you get further away from the royal palace-oriented center, however, you soon start to get into working class neighborhoods, pothole covered roads, and less than well-maintained infrastructure. In some areas, to be brutally honest, Phnom Penh is little more than shanty towns with open sewers and dwellings cobbled together from reused materials on the edges of polluted canals . How do we handle the mixed blessing that is urbanization? Phnom Penh, not surprisingly, has the best education and job opportunities in Cambodia by far. Salaries are higher and workplaces are better, cleaner and safer. But it is certainly not always a completely rosy picture, not for the majority of city dwellers. 107 Traffic for instance can be horrific in the suburbs. Morning rush hour and especially evening rush hour traffic can easily turn a 15 minute ride into 90 minutes or 2 hours of torture and wasted time. Public transportation, to the extent that it exists at all, is a fleet of imported city buses which if anything, add to the extreme traffic congestion. How much productivity is lost due to time wasted in commuting? Waste services are also rudimentary in many areas, schedules are undependable and the quality is unreliable. This is said, not to show disrespect to the valiant workers who take on this thankless task. We have the utmost respect for the work that they do but the reality is that it is insufficient. This often leads to unsanitary conditions, health issues, safety concerns and unpleasant odors and uncomfortable urban living, especially in the outlying areas. Not surprisingly, this also takes a toll on valuable tourism income. Littering is also a serious problem that is, to some extent, a side effect of unreliable waste management. How can health and safety be maintained in such sub-optimal conditions? As is the case in a lot of rapidly growing cities, car parking is yet another major problem , especially in the city center. Due to lack of legitimate, authorized parking spaces in Phnom Penh, motorists often choose to park on the sidewalk, at the roadside or in illegal spots like in front of bus stops or hospitals. Needless to say, this makes the already unpleasant traffic situation 108

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: even more congested and inefficient. Building management in apartment complexes is another critical urban life comfort issue. We want to live in buildings that have reliable elevators , dependable security systems , effective water and electric power delivery, reliable smoke alarm systems and convenient parking. Each one of these is a challenge in a developing country like ours that lacks infrastructure and cutting edge architectural know how. Phally and his VP.Start team members have had the unpleasant experience of water running out mid-shower, of elevators breaking down in tall buildings and of parking issues that simply won’t go away. As urban dwellers and lovers of Phnom Penh, Phally and the VP.Start team seek boldly innovative solutions to some of these pitfalls that they themselves also face. The challenges of urban life in a developing country are huge and growing. But… “But” seems to be the most commonly used word in Phally’s vocabulary. “There is this intractable problem but… ” “This seems like an impossible challenge but… ” “We don’t have the resources to accomplish this plan but… ” “But” is a word that indicates refusal to accept defeat. “But” is a word that says that despite all the evidence to the contrary, there must be a way to make this work. And VP.Start will find that way! As VP.Start was achieving the early stages of a more reliable, sustainable, 109 affordable and equitable smart grid as a foundation, it was time for another “but”. A big “but”! Urban life is not always convenient, comfortable, safe, healthy or affordable. I might add, this is hardly a situation unique to Cambodian cities like Phnom Penh. It is rare indeed to find a city that does not suffer from at least some of these challenges. To CEO Phally, these daunting challenges of the urban experience looked like opportunities. Golden opportunities. After all, the bigger the problem, the larger the solution that needs to be created. Phally looked directly at these daunting urban problems and decided that VP.Start would take those problems head on . VP.Start would make solutions, big solutions, transformative solutions, global solutions. Nothing more and nothing less! VP.Start was going to have to create solutions for Smart cities . After all, the ultimate goal of VP.Start had never been just grid modernization. They were moving towards an overarching sustainability system. There could be no true sustainability unless there were sustainable, liveable cities. Think about it like this: What good is a reliable electric grid if it doesn’t improve the lives of users? What good are smart cities without smart citizens? What good are smart homes without smart homeowners? 110

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: Another challenge that Phally and the VP.Start team faced personally on a regular basis was trying to live a comfortable, cost-effective and safe home life. There was a definite need for home automation. Greater efficiency in home electric usage. Greater cost savings and less waste. Greater dependability and safety. A sustainability revolution. Specifically, electricity in Cambodia, while getting more affordable, was still far from cheap. In this situation, the last thing that Phally and his associates could afford to do was waste money and waste electricity with inefficient devices. There was a world to change and so little time to change it. Inefficient, wasteful, unsafe, unhealthy, uncomfortable homes were simply unacceptable. This challenge, the challenge of smart homes, led the SIMA Journey of VP.Start in yet a new direction, The direction of the Internet of Things and IoT devices. Phally knew that he, like most hardworking people, didn’t have enough time to sit around and monitor his devices on a constant basis just to make sure that he wasn’t wasting electricity. A commodity, electricity, that Cambodia could ill-afford to waste. He didn’t have the time or the inclination to constantly check his appliances to ascertain and verify that cost-savings were being maximized. 111 Phally needed devices that managed and monitored themselves and only subsequently reported to him, as necessary . IoT devices that could make adjustments independently based on data-driven insights that were self-collected and acted on. Phally needed devices and appliances that worked for him , not the other way around. This was the seed that sprouted the SIMA Home Initiatives concept. And once again, as Phally tended to think, if it could be done right , why couldn’t it be done big ? The “CEO Phally strategy”: Find a successful and affordable approach to home automation, office automation, business automation, hospital automation, every kind of automation , and keep expanding the plan, increasing the savings, improving energy independence. “If at first you don’t succeed, it was probably because the plan was not big enough.” So you have the wisdom to solve a million problems, But do you have the wisdom to solve them all with only ONE solution? This, logically, led to the yet another stage of the SIMA Journey. So, yes, we are developing an intelligent grid with plug and play technology and using existing infrastructure for cost-savings. So, yes, we are building a reliable urban framework on the foundation of that now reliable electric grid. So, yes, we are expanding the power of data-driven technology that 112

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: has become possible thanks to a more dependable and equitable grid. So, yes, we are pushing that power out into home automation by means of IoT devices and data acquisition. But, in spite of all these new “missions” of VP.Start, Phally and his “clan” couldn’t help but feel that something was still missing . He needed something to bring it all together into one framework. One integrated system, one network. A Universal Connectivity Network. One app to bring grid modernization, intelligent cities, home automation and AI capabilities under one giant umbrella. Just as Phally had been nicknamed the “alien” by his classmates, this universal app would be called AlienCheck. Just for a moment, Stop and think about the courage, the chutzpah, the boldness bordering on madness, required for a young, growing company like VP.Start to even consider attempting to create a universal app. Simply creating any app, let alone an app with chat features, an IoT device connectivity app, an AI chatbot app, an app to monitor the electric grid, an e-commerce app, an internet banking app, an app to monitor and improve urban life, an app to facilitate home automation And then combining all these features into one UNIVERSAL app, 113 was such an epic task that even some team members thought it was crazy. To create even one of these apps was a very daunting challenge. To try to create them all, simultaneously, under one UCN (Universal Connectivity Network) was such a herculean task that it almost required a suspension of reality to even consider it. And yet, Phally and his team not only considered it, they insisted on it . Without an overarching framework to tie everything together, It couldn’t really be called a sustainability system ! Are you willing to be “crazy” for your dreams? Fortunately, Phally was and is, more that willing to suspend reality for a while if reality threatens to get in the ways of his plans and dreams. He has never minded being called “crazy” or considered foolish. If Phally ever worried about such things, VP.Start would have never started at all, let alone, very powerfully. Others could say why this is impossible or that is unachievable, talk about the improbability of even accomplishing a sliver of what Phally was setting out to do. Phally would hear out all the naysayers and doubters, with all their logical and reasonable doubts, and then he would just accomplish, just achieve, just succeed, just perform. This has always been the crazy miracle of VP.Start. Somewhere beyond the world of logic and reason, Phally would determine that something needed to be done and then he and his team would be arrogant and foolish enough to do it. When you innovatively solve the problems that trouble you personally, 114

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: Why not share these solutions with the world? Do you dare to try to make the world a better place? Another core aspect of the VP.Start perspective and the “missions” of VP.Start is how the solutions start at the very personal level , spread to the local level, rapidly become national and regional solutions and then eventually move on to the global stage . As mentioned before, grid modernization, intelligent cities, data-driven IoT devices and creating a universal connectivity app, were at their core, solutions to daily life problems of ordinary Cambodians. Ordinary Cambodians… like Phally and his management team. The entire team. The grind of traffic jams, the frustration of undependable electricity, the discomfort and health issues of poor waste management, the lost money from their pockets due to inefficient appliances and electric use, these were not “academic” research topics divorced from daily reality. These were real world problems for which VP.Start began to craft real world solutions . When your business ideas begin to grow, is it time to consolidate your successes? To rest on your laurels? To count your money when you’re sitting at the table? Or is it time to press your advantage and go for broke? 115 As the solutions began to take shape, to take hold and succeed, they started to become adopted as local solutions , at first in a piecemeal fashion, by local business and local communities and local branches of the EDC. With each new pilot project like the SIMA City Initiatives in TaKhmao town, a suburb of Phnom Penh in neighboring Kandal Province, with each new company that started adopting VP.Start automation solutions and with each new successful integration of DRC technology into existing EDC infrastructure, word was starting to spread and continuing to spread. VP.Start was starting to make a difference at the local level . True national recognition was not far behind. Especially, thanks to the well-established and still growing working relationship with the EDC and its branches all over Cambodia, VP.Start was starting to become a flagship company in grid modernization for Cambodia. The deeper point was not missed or lost on VP.Start. If you succeed locally, why not go national? If you succeed nationally, why not go international? What if the best way to follow up success is more and more success, more accelerated, more escalated, more exponential success? After all, if local solutions could be scaled up nationally, and if people in other countries were facing similar difficulties as those 116

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Story VP
searchIndex.text: of Cambodia, countries across ASEAN, South Asia and indeed throughout the developing world, why wouldn’t it make sense to scale up what VP.Start was doing internationally? Which, of course, is exactly what started happening, be it through pilot projects in India and Malaysia, visiting students from the US and the Philippines, pitching conferences in Taiwan and Germany, collaborative meetings in China, and with Japanese, Singaporean and Korean investors. Phally was quickly becoming a regular fixture at Phnom Penh international airport. For the first time, VP.Start was beginning to have a nascent international reputation, presence and branding. Two of the three big challenges were already being met head on. The first challenge had been, what to do with the reliable power that accrued from a grid that had become more dependable, more affordable, more equitable and more efficient, not to mention, more data-driven,. What kind of architecture was VP.Start going to build on that foundation? As we have already seen in detail above, 117 a variety of missions and initiatives were inaugurated. The second challenge had been, as these initiatives became more established, substantiated and verified through successful implementation and deployment experiences, which aspects of the overarching SIMA Journey were primed to be expanded and scaled up to the global level ? As we have just seen, VP.Start dealt with the question aggressively and proactively. But a third challenge still remained , perhaps the most daunting challenge of the three. For VP.Start to succeed in the long term, it would not be enough to have amazing ecosolutions and missions, or even not be enough to spread them out on the global stage. VP.Start’s success or failure to gain permanent success, would come down to a critical factor, a core issue that could not be ignored or overlooked. VP.Start need to have a powerful, persuasive, positive and particular voice! You have amazing ideas, groundbreaking solutions, innovative plans. There is no doubt about that. It is your birthright as a human, the gift of nature. And furthermore, your ideas belong on the global stage, transforming the world. BUT, do you have the voice, The Powerful, Persuasive, 118

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Story An Ordinary Voice or a SIMA Voice? “I like hearing myself talk
searchIndex.text: Positive and Particular Voice To bring your dreams to fruition? Chapter 9 The SIMA Story An Ordinary Voice or a SIMA Voice? “I like hearing myself talk. I often have long conversations by myself, and I am so clever that sometimes I don’t understand a word of what I am saying.” -Oscar Wilde, author and humorist How often do you talk to yourself ? When you do talk to yourself, do you listen? The time had come for VP.Start to raise a SIMA voice. There really was no choice. VP.Start had the innovative solutions. They were developing a local branding and name recognition. They had solutions that needed to go global . That were suited to go global . They were starting to have supporters, stakeholders and to get 119 positive word of mouth. But this word of mouth was in Khmer. No disrespect intended to a beautiful language with an ancient pedigree. An ancient language, a historically significant language, but hardly a global business language. VP.Start was going to need to raise its SIMA voice, and raise it loudly and proudly in English. How do you plan to learn how to raise your voice? In English? One solution to this situation might be to bring in English-speaking outsourced consultants. International spokespeople. Public speakers or speaking coaches from abroad. There was a key, inescapable problem with this approach. Outsiders cannot bring the powerful inside story of VP.Start to life. VP.Start was and is a proudly Cambodian company. This is not about racism or discrimination on the part of VP.Start; it is about giving talented young Khmer students and graduates greater opportunities. Think about this: If the voice of the company was not Cambodian, If the voice came from some overseas speakers, How could VP.Start focus attention on its home-grown solutions , created in-house by Cambodian engineers and tech professionals who graduated from the Cambodian education system? Before you raise your voice, do you know what you want to say? If you don’t know what you want to say, 120

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Story An Ordinary Voice or a SIMA Voice? “I like hearing myself talk
searchIndex.text: How can you avoid having an ORDINARY voice ? How could VP.Start successfully make the case for its “MADE IN CAMBODIA, MADE FOR THE WORLD” solutions? How could VP.Start reinforce its position that its solutions and innovations Are NOT imported from abroad or copied from other companies? How do you raise your voice with originality and authenticity? Getting quality English speakers was not the biggest issue, by any means. VP.Start’s amazing innovations came from the CEO and Founder Phally. Other team members could talk about specifications and testing regimens, About compliance and technical parameters, About all the critical details that made up the ecosolutions of VP.Start, But they could not give the big picture sustainability system view . They could not give the overarching data-driven AI-infused digitized view, The philosophical underpinnings that brought everything together. And if the team that knew VP.Start so well could hardly do that, how could outside consultants do that? If you don’t raise your voice, who will? If you don’t raise it now, when? The team could sell products and promote services but VP.Start had never been focused on that. They might be able to help customers to start to understand VP.Start’s products, but the goal was never that but always, To let customers feel, believe in and remember VP.Start. Deep technical understanding by customers was neither required nor encouraged. 121 My wife informed me recently that she wants an Apple iPhone. I asked her why she preferred this phone to other options. She didn’t give me specifications or functions or technical information. She said, “I believe in Apple products. I feel like they are high quality.” That is the vibe that VP.Start is seeking as well. But that could only come from a powerful and persuasive big picture voice And that voice has to come from the Founder. Phally was going to have to improve his English ability. Why do we need to improve our communication skills to the true world-class level? We are talking about Phally so Let’s be clear. For this task, Fluent speaker, second language speaker, nearly native speaker, functionally native speaker: these were not going to be sufficient. The goal was simple and simply difficult: world-class communicator. The SIMA Voice. At this time, VP.Start made its first steps towards having an online presence, as well. Building a website from scratch. Developing a Facebook following. Sometimes in Khmer, sometimes in English, sometimes both. In these early stages, everything was pretty rudimentary. It was definitely a case of on the job training. 122

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Story An Ordinary Voice or a SIMA Voice? “I like hearing myself talk
searchIndex.text: But, if you have the VP.Start mindset of creativity and positivity, And are naive enough or arrogant enough to believe in yourself, the impossible might just be a little less impossible than you think. What is your online footprint and why is it distinctive? If you cannot show your innovative nature in your online presence, who will believe it offline? Especially on Facebook, this was a time to document every meeting, every visit to utility offices in the provinces, every visitor to the campus, both domestic and international. Not for branding, not for promotion, just for practicing raising the SIMA Voice. A strange and new phenomenon had begun; gradually the number of Facebook post viewers was increasing and these viewers were increasingly industry leaders, regional tech players, government ministers and university professors. Not that Phally particularly cared about the number or positions of his viewership. Remember this: For a powerful SIMA Voice, Sometimes what you choose NOT to say is just as important as what you choose to say. VP.Start decided NOT to use Facebook posts to focus on products and services. After all, who wants to read advertising and sales pitches masquerading 123 as legitimate posts? Furthermore, VP.Start determined NOT to use Facebook posts for self-promotion. Awards gained, sales targets reached, profits accrued, customers acquired, these were not topic for Facebook posts. When you have your chance to speak to the world, your 15 minutes of fame, what do you feel compelled to say? Facebook was the place to tell the SIMA Journey. The Story of VP.Start, The Ideology of VP.Start, The Methodology of VP.Start and The Amazing Innovations of VP.Start. To raise up the SIMA Voice . From the earliest days, the focus was largely and intentionally on Ideology. What were the guiding principles of VP.Start? Why did Phally decide to found the company in the first place? What was the difference between innovation and technology? Between being yourself and being a follower, a copy, an echo? What does true sustainability mean? The theory was simple. Some people may want to know about the latest products. A few people may even want to know about the specifications and technical details. On the other hand, everyone wants to know how to live more sustainably, how to work more creatively, 124

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Story An Ordinary Voice or a SIMA Voice? “I like hearing myself talk
searchIndex.text: how to manage their lives more effectively, how to become the best possible version of themselves. In other words, The SIMA Voice must take the principles of grid modernization and data-driven technology, of digital twins and AI-infusion, of data acquisition and digitization, and use philosophy and common sense and powerful quotes to make these concepts meaningful to lay people. The culmination of this strategy was a recurring Facebook post article that Phally created: “From Cambodia With Love” A couple of examples will suffice to give you the concept: From Cambodia With Love (Part 13) Thoughts on a Business Trip in Vietnam “We cannot direct the wind, but we can adjust our sails.” -Dolly Parton The wind blows. And then it stops. It changes directions. The “tech warrior” knows that wind is energy, energy that can push you forward or slow you down. The wise man doesn’t try to fight against the wind. The wiser man lets the wind lead him forward. The wisest man of all tries to harness the wind and use Big Data to predict what direction and what time it will blow. The old song says that “the answer is blowing in the wind.” Are you ready to catch the next big wind? 125 And, one more….. From Cambodia With Love Part 20 How do you feel when you think about the future? Are you excited or afraid? Some people feel afraid when they think about the future. They think that technology will leave them behind. They believe that innovation can be dangerous. Often, they are especially afraid of AI. They hear stories that AI will take over the world, taking away human freedom and authority. However, the “tech warrior” is not afraid of the future. He understands these feelings, of course. Technology must be handled wisely and harnessed to benefit everyone equally. VP.Start promises not just to bring “innovation through technology “ but to implement it carefully, safely and sustainably. The future is coming, whether we are ready or not. VP.Start wants to help us be ready to greet a future without fear. Each entry start with either a quote or a thought-provoking question. We are then faced with a challenge and we are informed what 1) the ordinary person and 2) the tech warrior would do to handle that situation. This is never meant as a put down of the “ordinary” response or arrogant praise of “the tech warrior”. It is simply a unique way for CEO Phally to show the uniqueness of the SIMA philosophy . 126

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Story An Ordinary Voice or a SIMA Voice? “I like hearing myself talk
searchIndex.text: At the end, there is a question or statement to push the reader into action. These post ultimately reached 100 editions and became quite popular. There were internal calls at VP.Start at times to make these posts less philosophical and more commercial and product-oriented, but Phally refused to do so. The goal was never product promotion, advertising, sales and marketing or even company branding and name recognition. The sole goal was to express VP.Start’s unique ideology to Cambodia and the wider world . This inclusiveness and lack of sales pressure made the series unique and ubiquitous, soon being passed around in ever widening circles. Just the kind of counter-intuitive approach that VP.Start always embraces. If you could meet anyone, pitch your idea to anyone, chat with anyone, Who would you choose to meet? VP.Start also started raising their voice by ramping up conference and meetings. Meetings with utilities. Meetings with customers. Meetings with stakeholders and supporters. Meetings with potential investors. 127 Meetings with educators and school administrators. Meetings with government ministers. Meetings with international organizations. Meetings with students. Why so many meetings? Not to promote a product, nor to secure brand loyalty. Not to publicize a service, neither to build up a customer base. Not to garner investment or to build ROI or attract support or earn a profit. Not to leverage that powerful SIMA voice for any of aspirations that companies normally leverage a powerful voice for. The purpose was much simpler and much more complex . Much more conventional and yet simultaneously innovative and unique. VP.Start had something to say, and had to say it. A message of sustainability to change the world. A message of the hope of innovation through technology. A message of the SIMA Journey. Silence was not an option. 128

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Story Difficulties Along the SIMA Journey “I took the (road) less traveled by, and that has made all the difference
searchIndex.text: Chapter 10 The SIMA Story Difficulties Along the SIMA Journey “I took the (road) less traveled by, and that has made all the difference.” -Robert Frost, poet When you make the decision to be yourself in all your uniqueness, Are you prepared to deal with those who may not approve? By this point, VP.Start has been experiencing continuous, if somewhat haphazard, off and on growth. By embracing the strategy of not being strategic, by choosing to be idea-driven rather than product-driven, by opting to adopt an innovation-driven rather than profit-driven business model and by insisting on a corporate culture of radical decentralization, VP.Start had certainly selected “the road less traveled.” While this approach impressed outsiders greatly and stoked interest in VP.Start, Some insiders were less enthused. While CEOPhally ignored awards and eschewed honors, keeping his focus squarely on the Big Picture solutions of the sustainability system, There were some team members who didn’t appreciate his responsibility-over-profits approach. There were those who felt that a company should be focused on promoting products, selling services, cornering markets, 129 making government connections and above all, garnering massive profits. In the normal business world, these were hardly radical ideas. But CEO Phally adamantly and steadfastly refused to allow VP.Start to be a mere normal business. Do you choose or refuse to do business as normal? Why do you choose the road that you choose? Normal businesses sell products, but innovative businesses tell stories. Normal businesses garner ROI, but innovative businesses make a difference. Normal businesses work for traction, market share, increased profitability. VP.Start was working to change the world and make it more sustainable. Not surprisingly, not all team members were not on board with this attitude. A group of VP.Start employees, referred to by CEO Phally, as “invaders, slanderers, toxic, ungrateful people”, decided to see if they could start their own company, have success and make profits on their own. Unfortunately, they decided to take code, product details, specifications and Some of the VP.Start technical staff with them. They thought that they could copy the success and imitate the products of VP.Start without the burden of an innovative spirit or sense of responsibility. Why do we often learn more from failures and problems than from successes? 130

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Story Difficulties Along the SIMA Journey “I took the (road) less traveled by, and that has made all the difference
searchIndex.text: CEO Phally learned 3 valuable if painful lessons from this setback. First, innovation cannot be stolen . Products can be copied, services can be imitated , business plans can be mimicked. But innovative ideas and creativity are impossible to echo or steal. How can the non-innovative person expand the innovative ideas of another? Who do you trust and how much do you trust them? Second, VP.Start learned a vital lesson about trust. “Trust but verify.” CEO Phally loved each team member, including those that chose to betray his trust, but he also learned that unlimited trust and unfettered access leads to problems. Cybersecurity is not just designed to protect us from outside malicious and nefarious actors ; a similar scrutiny, sadly, must be applied to the internal team . People tend to do what they think is in their personal best interest rather than what is in the best interest of the team. If we assume by default that people will always behave properly, we are certain to be disappointed. But finding the right balance of “trust” and “verify” is never easy. Perhaps, the VP.Start management was so convinced, of the power of their ideas, the persuasive power of innovation through technology, that they forgot that some people operate profit-driven rather than idea-driven lives. While everyone has the opportunity to be an innovator, 131 some choose the less challenging, materialism-driven life of the follower, not the lead actor. Third, CEO Phally discovered the truth of the famous quote, “Whatever doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.” While the loss of valuable staff, some with difficult to replace skills and experience, the loss of intellectual property, which would take time to recover from, and the loss of trust, perhaps the hardest blow of all for a “family” like VP.Start, While all of these setbacks slowed down VP.Start for a while, these dilemmas were unable to seriously damage the growth trajectory of VP.Start. What problems and failures have made you stronger? As a matter of fact, the departure of those team members who didn’t share the unique VP.Start perspective, meant that those who remained had actively chosen to align themselves with this radical way of doing business, for a brighter future for our country and our world. As a result, the familial atmosphere of the team became stronger than ever. In that way, while the setbacks caused frustration and difficulties, in the long run, they were beneficial and made VP.Start stronger. Or maybe, to put in a more CEO Phally ideological framework, We cannot always control what happens to us, BUT We can control how we respond to less than favorable outcomes. How do you react to those who disappoint, harm or betray you? What does your reaction tell you about yourself ? 132

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Story Difficulties Along the SIMA Journey “I took the (road) less traveled by, and that has made all the difference
searchIndex.text: The “slanderers” left VP.Start and tried to start their own business, make their own products, accumulate their own customers and garner their own profits. At times, they spoke ill of VP.Start and tried unsuccessfuly to cast doubts on the effectiveness of very products that they had helped to develop and market. Under the circumstances, you might expect that the VP.Start team would hold a grudge or even take legal action. And since they are humans, not angels, they did hold a grudge at times. They did consider legal action, as well. CEO Phally, himself, was not above having moments of anger with those who had shown themselves to be ungrateful and dishonest. And yet, those moments never last very long. VP.Start’s core vision is to make a brighter, better future for Cambodia with a more reliable grid and a more sustainable, greener and more energy independent power system. No time to dwell on bitter feelings and bad memories. One further aspect of this sustainability system encompasses creating better paying, higher quality job opportunities for Khmer young people. The VP.Start team is clear and united that if the ungrateful “rivals” and “rebels” are able to create new jobs for qualified students and recent graduates, we would be happy and unhesitating to wish them success. The good of the country comes first. In fact, at the end of the day, 133 Phally hopes that they achieve their dreams and find what they seek. Still, and without bitterness or malice, Phally has determined unflinchingly that they will never be allowed to return to the fold of VP.Start. This is not based on anger or pettiness or jealousy. The former team members made a conscious, intentional decision to reject the VP.Start ideology and methodology in pursuit of greater financial rewards. They are not to be criticized for this, but their decision must be respected and bear consequences. They made a choice and in CEO Phally’s view that is the one choice that cannot be undone . Mistakes can be forgiven, of course, errors can be handled, to be sure, and failures can be learned from, without a doubt but the decision to reject innovation and leave the SIMA Journey is final and irreversible. Have you ever felt betrayed in a business or other context? How did you handle the feelings? Are you so dedicated to your goals that these setbacks cannot derail your journey? Are there lines that cannot be crossed and decisions that are irreversible for you? Hard times will come, Challenges will appear. You may feel discouraged or disparaged or dismayed. HOW WILL YOU RESPOND? 134

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey to the Global Stage “To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom
searchIndex.text: Chapter 11 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey to the Global Stage “To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom.” -Bertrand Russell, philosopher and professor at the University of Cambridge The artist, Picasso, once drew a portrait of a customer in less than a minute. He asked the customer to pay him $10M for the picture. The customer refused saying that it only took him 30 seconds to draw that picture. Picasso responded that in fact, it took him 40 years to draw that picture. In the same way, you could say that VP.Start decision to go to the global stage started when Phally was 5 years old, dreaming about Cambodia becoming another Singapore, a place that he could barely imagine. In other words, the seed of going to the global stage was there from the very beginning . What dream is guiding you? What are you aiming for? What is your ultimate destination? How sure are you of that objective? How long has that goal been your aim? The dream for VP.Start was, and always has been, and will always be, one and the same. 135 Yes, grid modernization. But that stepping stone is just in order to create a more reliable source of energy. A stronger economy, a more vibrant education, a more comfortable life. Yes, the SIMA Smart Grid. The data-driven dynamic digital AI-infused Smart Grid. But that is not the goal, either. That is one step further on the path. Yes, SIMA Smart cities are essential. Smart cities for smart citizens. Data-driven green waste management. IoT device-based traffic management and smart street lighting. Smart building management and parking management connected online. Weather forecasting. EV charging station expansion. DER seamless integration. Safe and secure water management. Augmented Disaster preparation infrastructure. Each component is a valuable part of improving outcomes for city dwellers. And yet this, too, is not the destination. Yes, Smart Home automation is mission critical. More efficient appliances. More cost-saving gadgets. Safer devices that can be monitored remotely. More peace of mind, less waste, more energy efficiency. Each IoT-infused home appliance and each automated piece of office equipment is a positive step in the right direction. A step forward but this, too, is not the ultimate objective. 136

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey to the Global Stage “To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom
searchIndex.text: Yes, the Universal Connectivity app , bringing all of these aspect of the VP.Start vision, all these parts of the SIMA Journey, together in one platform. Connecting AI to IoT device management, connecting chat features to the energy management system, connecting e-commerce to internet banking to smart cities and homes, connecting seamlessly, powerfully, efficiently, universally. How far are you prepared to go to bring your dreams to fruition? We are finally getting close to the SIMA destination but we have still not yet arrived. Moving past Big Data and cloud computing and AI capabilities and digitization, We are able to arrive at the objective that has motivated VP.Start before it even existed. Sustainability. Overarching sustainability. A comprehensive sustainability system. A sustainable future. A sustainable WORLD. This is the crazy, impossible, extreme, revolutionary destination of the SIMA Journey. And the VP.Start team is crazy enough and arrogant enough to believe that simple people with big ideas and unbridled ambition can change the world. “A small campus but big ideas. A small team but big dreams. 137 A small country but a big heart.” Or a John Lennon put it in the song, “Imagine”: “ You may say that I’m a dreamer, but I’m not the only one. I hope some day you will join us and the world will live as one.” A sustainable future necessitates a sustainable world. And If VP.Start is serious in its pursuit of a sustainable world, by definition, they must “go to the global stage.” Nothing more and nothing less! Do you believe that your ideas can change the world? Your ideas may or may not change the world, but I can guarantee without hesitation that your unexpressed ideas will never change anything. VP.Start had been cultivating connections to the world, as mentioned before, but the time had come to move from cultivation to harvesting. 5 initial locations to extend and expand the SIMA Journey outward came into focus. India, the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia and Lao PDR. Each potential market presented challenges and obstacles But as we know, VP.Start “translates” obstacles into opportunities, challenges into chances. How do you turn extreme challenges into amazing opportunities? How do you view the challenges that inevitably come? The Philippine market is particularly challenging for market access in the energy sector. For starters, the Philippines features three mostly interconnected but 138

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey to the Global Stage “To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom
searchIndex.text: distinct grids , which in and of itself is a major logistics challenge. Furthermore, the Philippines is an archipelago ranging from densely populated and fairly large islands to small, isolated and sparsely inhabited ones, which leads to a wide spectrum of electric coverage and service depending on the location, from extensive to minimal to completely non-existent. Add to that, the Philippines regularly faces extreme weather events at a level and frequency that few other countries in the world experience: tsunamis, extreme heat waves, torrential rains and flooding with related landslides. Beyond all of these challenges, there are active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes . The cherry on top is rampant and runaway urbanization which puts a severe strain on the functioning urban grid capacity. Haha, did I mention that the Philippines is a challenging energy sector? VP.Start is able to say that their ecosolutions are a perfect fit for the Philippine market because they are: easy to install, easy to use, easy to afford, easy to adapt and if necessary, easy to replace. Installing expensive grid infrastructure that a tsunami or volcano may suddenly take out is neither wise nor cost-effective. 139 On the other hand, data-driven solutions that are predictive can minimize the negative effects of extreme weather events. Installing expensive grid infrastructure to support islands of minimal population is impractical. On the other hand, taking advantage of existing infrastructure and building a grid architecture with AI-capabilities to seamlessly integrate DERs into the power system is proactive and sensible. Installing expensive grid equipment to try to keep up with explosive urbanization and exponential growth in demand is fiscally unfeasible. On the other hand, leveraging the power of digitization and data simulation to reduce bottlenecks, and doing it at cost, is reasonable and doable. You might say that VP.Start’s grid modernization solutions and strategies were created just for a place like the Philippines, a developing country with a myriad of challenges. You might say that and if you say that, you would be right! Indonesia and its market are in some ways similar to that of the Philippines but with these problems exacerbated to the extreme degree. The Philippines struggles with rapid urbanization. Indonesia faces the same challenge with one of the largest populations in the world. The Philippines is a widespread archipelago of islands. Indonesia is the largest grouping of islands in the world. Covering the greatest distance. more or less, stretching from the vicinity of India to that of Australia. composed of islands with different cultures, religions, languages, 140

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey to the Global Stage “To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom
searchIndex.text: histories, customs and very different levels of economic development from affluent Java and tourist powered Bali to undeveloped and primitive islands like West Jaya and North Maluku. Great distances geographically, culturally and economically. Once again, this variation among the islands means that grid modernization must be very adaptable . Fortunately, one of the strengths of the DRC series, the flagship modernization products of VP.Start, is their adaptability. Cambodia itself is a hodgepodge of infrastructures made by different companies, put together in an inconsistent fashion, due to the challenges of recovering from near total economic collapse during the war period. Hence, the DRC has more than 20 iterations and the number is constantly rising, each iteration dedicated to a distinct infrastructural architecture, maintaining the core grid modernization concepts but adapting to to the varied circumstances, bringing the disparate parts into one unified whole. In other words, exactly what Indonesia needs. If money were no object, do you think it would be wise to spend money as if it were no object? The Malaysian market is in many ways an outlier among the VP.Start global push. Malaysia is a stable, economically vibrant, rapidly developing and harmonious country. They have considerable resources to expend for grid modernization. 141 Why would they want to consider the modernization solutions of VP.Start? Let me suggest a pragmatic reason. To state the obvious, rich people and rich countries tend to get that way and stay that way by allocating their resources wisely. Just because you are able to afford a more expensive, luxury car, does NOT necessarily mean that a luxury car is the wisest option. As we all sadly know, we live in a world of geopolitical instability and sudden conflict. We also live in a world of unprecedented economic shocks . A wise country chooses the solutions that meet their needs at the lowest cost. A wise country prepares for the unpredictable future carefully. VP.Start ultimately intends its solutions to serve developed and “rich” countries in addition to those that are developing, “poor” and struggling . This initiative to access the Malaysian market is the first step in that direction. The Indian market is a special case indeed. It is often said that “India is not a country, India is a world” . Each region and often each village has its own culture, religious traditions and language. More than 20% of the world’s population live in India, so needless to point out, it is one of the world’s largest markets. One of the world’s most complicated energy sectors , as well. There is one national level dispatch center that manages the 5 regional level grids which in turn break up into more than 30 state level grid authorities . Each state level grid has its own compliance standards, its own unique regulatory framework and 142

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey to the Global Stage “To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom
searchIndex.text: its own distinct governing bodies. Success in one state does not guarantee access to others. Entering the market must be done on the state and local level and built up piece by piece, constantly adapting to the varied and heterogeneous geographical, legal and economic situations of each Indian state. How can a relatively small company like VP.Start dare to even envision entering such a massive market? As we have seen before, the VP.Start philosophy is simple: You cannot change the world by being quiet and shy and modest. You need aggressiveness and boldness and at times, arrogance. You need to be so convinced of the power of your ideas that the ridiculously impossible suddenly sounds easy. CEO Phally and the team are convinced of exactly that. It is not that the Indian market is so big and so complex and so unfathomable; it is that the SIMA Journey is so powerful and so essential and so undeniable . India is BIG. The SIMA Journey is BIGGER! In some ways, the market dearest to the heart of VP.Start is the nearest one, that of the Lao PDR (Laos). 143 First of all, Laos is a neighbor of Cambodia. Culturally similar , religiously similar , historically similar . Similar food, similar wedding practices, similar thinking, similar backgrounds. Both Cambodia and Laos experienced French colonization together. Both countries experienced the Cold War, the Vietnam War and the communist takeovers. Both experienced nearly crushing war experiences leaving both countries largely destroyed. Both countries suffered and still suffer frequent conflicts with bigger neighboring countries. Both are rebuilding their economies and electric grids. The EDL, the main utility of Laos, faces a major challenge, as well. Very limited population, spread out in remote and often mountainous villages, very limited urbanization and still a largely rural and underindustrialized economy and a much larger geographic area for the electric grid to cover than Cambodia. But Laos does have its advantages as well, namely great hydroelectric power resources . The Laotian energy grid is a very green one, in that sense. The ecosolutions of VP.Start can help connect those resources to the grid. Efficiently. 144

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey Past, Present and Future “The best way to predict the future is to create it
searchIndex.text: Without waste. Without losses. Using the power of data-driven technology. The power of AI. The power of digitization. The power of IoT-based monitoring systems. The power of innovation through technology that VP.Start brings to the table. VP.Start is already working on pilot projects in Laos with the EDL. The first steps. Small steps. Small steps that will soon turn into strides . Onto the global stage. At the end of the day, “going to the the global stage” is not about garnering more profits, although considerable profits and ROI will undoubtedly accrue . Neither is it about building up the reputation and name recognition, the branding, of VP.Start, even though this too will certainly be a result. The motivation is about building a better, brighter, healthier, safer, more equitable and more peaceful world. A more sustainable world. Is there really any other goal worth pursuing? Beyond turning a profit and building a brand and promoting your products, What are your motivations? Why do you work so hard to do what you do? As Phally likes to put it: “When you know why you live, you will know how to live and what living is!” 145 Chapter 12 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey Past, Present and Future “The best way to predict the future is to create it.” -Peter Drucker, management consultant For obvious reasons, the Story section of our book has focused mostly on the past, the development, the challenges, the victories, the failures. The resilience of VP.Start and its dedication to the SIMA Journey.
