Similarly, when you think about your “story”, you probably think of your past, your experiences, and your memories, both positive and negative. That is legitimate, but… Your story is more than just history. VP.Start’s story is more than just retelling the past. The past is just the guide to the present and the future. As some have put it, the past is made up of memories, not always accurate, and the future is made up of predictions, not always correct. All we have is now! 146

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey Past, Present and Future “The best way to predict the future is to create it
searchIndex.text: How much time do we spend regretting things that have never happened or worrying about things that never will happen? Focus on now and so much stress drifts away! VP.Start is now a company of more than 100 team members. More than 10,000 DRC solutions have been installed across Cambodia. VP.Start is working in tandem with universities across Cambodia and around the world. VP.Start is liaising with government ministries and officials while keeping independence. VP.Start is cooperating with various industrial leaders, attending and leading out various forums, participating in ASEAN and international conferences, submitting proposals for grants, cultivating partners and supporters and investors, forging a very loyal customer base, ramping up production with OEM collaboration, developing new products, expanding new missions, publicizing their UCN app, and entering global markets. That is a lot of action! VP.Start is a highly profitable company changing the face and image of Cambodia. Outstanding results, yes! Amazing advancements, yes! Wonderful successes, yes! Does this guarantee a bright future? NO! 147 VP.Start values its past but it does not believe in dwelling on the past. Resting on your laurels is not a recipe for success, but for disaster. VP.Start is looking to the future with the newly built SIMA Journey Hub, a conference center addition to the Sen Sok Valley Campus. In addition to hosting meetings with government dignitaries, investment bankers, utility officials, resident ambassadors, university administrators and industry leaders, this is also the home of the SIMA Journey Workshop , a weekly meeting open to the public to spread the good news about the latest trends in innovation through technology. Raising their voices and letting the world know! The goal is to turn Cambodia and VP.Start, specifically, into a hub of innovation. Other countries may have taken the lead in manufacturing and engineering and technological skill but Cambodia is primed to take the lead in innovative and creative ideas. Again, you may find this far-fetched. But the VP.Start team is completely dedicated to bring this idea to fruition. The VP.Start “Story” has reached a transformational inflection point. VP.Start is moving from a local company to a regional one, with eyes on the prize of becoming an international one. VP.Start is moving from a small, unknown company to a well-known local player with an increasing degree of name recognition at the regional level. VP.Start has, in a short time, increased its yearly revenue from nearly nothing to considerable resources with a view towards further exponential growth. 148

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey Past, Present and Future “The best way to predict the future is to create it
searchIndex.text: Above all else, VP.Start is committed to its journey and to building a sustainable world, or at the very least, setting the wheels in motion for others to follow up on. You, too, have a story to bring to the world. Everyone does. This story informs how you view the world, how you view your life, how you envision the future, how you understand what it means to become yourself. Your story when internalized, leads you to your ideology, which is the next step in the SIMA Journey. 149 150 148

searchIndex.text: “A sign of wisdom is believing that you are limitless, because you are.” -Maxine Lagace, philosopher What do you believe about yourself ? What limits have you chosen to put on yourself ? What do you believe that you cannot achieve, can never accomplish? Most people are convinced that there are many things that can not do. Most companies feel this way, as well. They pull up short of their dreams, believing that their story shows their limitations. But a big part of every story is how you interpret that story . Do your failures mean that you are a failure? Do your mistakes mean that you are a mistake? Or do they show you the way forward? If you look at your story and you have a negative ideology, let me be so bold as to tell you that you are interpreting your story incorrectly . CEO Phally’s story is not without hardships and troubles, as we have seen. The SIMA Journey of VP.Start similarly faced many obstacles, errors and disheartening moments. 155 Days of darkness, of difficulties, of disappointments, of disasters, of defeats. However, VP.Start chose to see that as a call to action. After all, you never fail if you do nothing . But when you try to accomplish something, failures and defeats are inevitable . In fact, the higher the goal that you seek to reach, the greater those failures will seem to be. In other words, troubles, frustrations and out and out failures mean that we are on the right track. How are you interpreting your story? What ideology are you forging out of your life experiences? What outcomes are accruing from the ideology that you have adopted? Let’s look at the data and let it drive us. Let’s look at the results and see if any changes need to be made. Sadly, some people and some companies have amazing stories, incredible stories but they allow a negative mindset and a pessimistic ideology diminish their power. VP.Start adamantly refuses to allow that negative mindset and defeatist ideology to take hold. Believe in your dreams, believe in your story, believe in yourself, believe in your belief. How about you? Are you ready to look at your ideology with open eyes? 156

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 The SIMA Story The SIMA Journey Past, Present and Future “The best way to predict the future is to create it
Chapter 1 The SIMA Ideology Innovation through Technology “Innovation is the ability to see change as an opportunity, not a threat
searchIndex.text: Chapter 1 The SIMA Ideology Innovation through Technology “Innovation is the ability to see change as an opportunity, not a threat.” -Steve Jobs Change will come. There is no way to avoid change. No way to escape transformation. However, will we be on the innovative, cutting edge of change? Or will we be left behind? As someone said, if you are not driving the car of change, that car is running you over. How do you feel about change? How do we come to see change as an opportunity? The most basic ideological framework of VP.Start is a simple but powerful one: Innovation through Technology. This is the slogan and motto of the company but more importantly, this is the mindset that drives VP.Start forward. And yet, it is a deceptive simple idea that few people really understand. First off, technology and innovation are not the same thing. Let me say that again, technology and innovation are not the same thing, any more than an artist and a house painter are the same thing. Any more than a classical composer and a high school drummer are the same thing. 159 A classical composer hears the melody in his imagination and creates music out of silence. A drummer is high school band has one task: follow the musical score. No creativity, no imagination. Just follow the notes written on the page. Success or failure is determined by how well you follow what has been written for you. The composers success or failure comes from how well he or she creates something out of nothing. Similarly, a house painter’s job is to paint the house according to the exact specifications of the home owner. The home owner determines the colors for each wall and ceiling and the house painter follows that design. A great house painter is a great follower , not to criticize house painters in the least. But creativity is not only unnecessary, it is forbidden. On the other hand, altogether, an artist faces a blank paper and lets his imagination guide her or him. The artist “sees” what is not there and brings it into existence. Creation. A house painter, a drummer and an engineer are all similarly on the technology side of the ledger. Again, we are not speaking ill of their skills. The ability to follow instruction precisely is not easy and is worthy of respect. Yet, on the contrary, the classical composer and the world-class artist come from the innovation side of things. 160

searchIndex.title: Chapter 1 The SIMA Ideology Innovation through Technology “Innovation is the ability to see change as an opportunity, not a threat
searchIndex.text: They bring into existence new things that did not exist before, except in their minds. Innovators turn imaginative dreams into tangible reality. That is why Innovation must always come before Technology. That is also why success requires both of them in tandem. What are your innovative ideas? Are you putting them first? Are you using your skills to bring your dreams into reality? Are you contented to be a follower? (No shame in that) Or, do you insist on being a lead actor? There are several groups. In the first group , some people and some companies try to achieve success with technology, but without innovation . Perhaps they believe that with enough technical skills and experience and expertise, innovation will come automatically. It will NOT. They build products that people don’t really need , set up marketing campaigns to convince people that they need what they don’t really need , and they battle competitors who also produce very similar products that no one really needs . They make profits, but incrementally , They grow their business, but very slowly , They change the world, not even a little . They do not achieve sustainability. After all, that was never the goal in the first place. On the flip side, there is also a second group , those companies and people, 161 fewer in number than the first group, who have innovative ideas but no skills or inclination to bring them to reality. The dreamers of dreams, the thinkers of thoughts, the imaginers of imagination. But NEVER the accomplishers, the achievers, the doers. If you have innovation but you don’t pair it with technological skills and abilities, You might as well go back to sleep and continue your dreaming. Are you a thinker? Or a doer? Or both? Or neither? There is a third group , rarer still, but existing nonetheless, those corporations and individuals who have both innovation and technology , but try to put technology first. They try to create prototypes and products, services and subscriptions, and THEN, make them innovative. This is an impossible task . After you crack the egg, can you put it back together? Innovation is the idea that drives technology, the action. If you act first and think later, what usually happens? Have you ever said something and then stopped and thought, why did I say that? I know I have many times. After saying it, you realized that those words would make the other person, the listener, unhappy and should not have been said. 162

searchIndex.title: Chapter 1 The SIMA Ideology Innovation through Technology “Innovation is the ability to see change as an opportunity, not a threat
searchIndex.text: I am pretty sure we have all had that experience. But can you take back what has already been said or already been done? The act of saying (or doing) is like technology. When we put words or action before thinking, will we have a positive outcome? Let me give an example. Some entrepreneur decides to start an AI service provider. After all, she has heard that now is the time to get into the AI business. So thinks the entrepreneur. So she comes up with a company name, hires a great and highly qualified AI team, gains international investment, builds an impressive headquarters and launches a successful IPO. Sounds good, doesn’t it? Now if she could only think of what to do, what goal to pursue, what innovation to bring to the table. She has all the technology that she needs but she put it before innovation. She leaped before she looked. Do you usually think before you act? Or do you act before you think? There is a fourth group , a very small group, indeed. This is the group that has both innovation and technology and puts technology first. They are innovation-driven , idea-driven, creative thinking-driven companies and people. They practice Innovation through Technology. VP.Start is a proud member of this last group. At the core of VP.Start’s ideology are ideas. 163 Amazing ideas. Ridiculous ideas. Outstanding ideas. Impossible ideas. Powerful ideas. Incredible ideas. Crazy, crazy ideas! Our ideas are a natural outcome of our story. In VP.Start’s case, the idea of ideas is sustainability. A sustainable future. A sustainable world. Coming from an unstable and unsustainable past in Cambodia. and creating a stable, peaceful, successful and sustainable Cambodia and the larger world. That is the dream, the vision, the goal, the innovation. Next Phally set about hiring a team and gathering skill sets and human resources and establishing a hub to flesh out these ideas, to hone them into specific missions with tangible deadlines and measurable results. Not Innovation and Technology, Not Innovation or Technology, Not Innovation without Technology, Not Technology through Innovation, But…. Innovation through Technology 164

searchIndex.title: Chapter 2 The SIMA Ideology Remember the Big Picture “If you want to make the world a better place, take a look at yourself and make a change
searchIndex.text: Chapter 2 The SIMA Ideology Remember the Big Picture “If you want to make the world a better place, take a look at yourself and make a change.” -Michael Jackson from “Man in the Mirror” The ideology of VP.Start includes caring about others . What point is creating a sustainable world, SIMA Smart cities, homes and offices And a reliable, affordable and energy independent power system, If you don’t care about the people who will use those solutions? Once again, compassionate corporate culture comes from the VP.Start Story. CEO Phally remembers family and friends who supported him from his very birth, even going so far as to take him to various other mothers in the village for breastfeeding when his own mother was ill. People who have experienced suffering themselves tend to be unwilling to let others suffer . They see the big picture. They see beyond prof it statements and market research and balance sheets and contracts . They see what really matters. They see compassion. Compassion is the soul of VP.Start, the cornerstone of all its ideology and vision. Without compassion, there can be no SIMA Journey. How do you respond when others are in trouble? 165 Is a spirit of helping others a core part of your corporate culture or just a sideshow? It is impossible to consider the VP.Start philosophy without talking about charitable work. During the border conflict with Thailand that occurred in 2025, many hundreds of thousands of Cambodians were displaced (many Thais were displaced, also). The evacuees were forced to live in ramshackle tent cities or on the grounds of Buddhist pagodas. The elderly and the infirm struggled, at times, to get the healthcare and medications that they needed. Tragically, young children were unable to attend schools. Pregnant women and women with small babies were hard pressed to make sure that they were able to get adequate nutrition for their newest members. The refugees in general were suffering from overcrowded and sometimes unsanitary conditions with insufficient food and water and a critical lack of medical and educational resources. Of course, the government was doing its best to help the victims. And yet, some in the camps also were affected by depression and extreme loneliness. Despite the fact that in Phnom Penh conditions were safe and the war seemed very far away, the VP.Start team and CEO Phally saw this situation and felt that this was a challenge that the SIMA Journey needed to take up. What good, after all, is a sustainable future that leaves some people out? Furthermore, merely giving donations to a charity 166

searchIndex.title: Chapter 2 The SIMA Ideology Remember the Big Picture “If you want to make the world a better place, take a look at yourself and make a change
searchIndex.text: and letting them handle the logistics would not be sufficient. VP.Start needed to go into action, visit the refugee camps, meet the displaced people, serve their needs and take action to help them directly . CEO Phally believed that just as important as meeting their material needs, VP.Start needed to show the evacuees that they had not been forgotten , that people all over the country were concerned for their welfare and that Cambodians everywhere were all “one country, one family.” Of equal importance, the VP.Start team didn’t see this as “taking a break” from the SIMA Journey, or “putting the journey on hold” for a while, while they pursued a valiant but unrelated charitable goal. Caring for others, compassion and charity are actually at the very heart of what VP.Start does. There is no SIMA Journey without concern for the welfare of others. To put in a more tech business context, VP.Start has various core missions that form the backbone of its business plan: SIMA Smart Grid Modernization, SIMA Smart City Initiatives, SIMA Smart Home Initiatives and the UCN (Universal Connectivity Network), the app known as AlienCheck. Each one of these missions serves as an innovative solution to a challenging set of problems but they are much more than just solutions, 167 more than mere products for profits. They are acts of compassion, above all else. What, after all, is the purpose of modernizing the electric grid of Cambodia and then of other nations, especially developing ones? Is it to gain investment, to turn a nice profit, to burnish the brand reputation of VP.Start, to earn credentials and honors and awards? These are all fine accomplishments, in their own right, but from the SIMA Journey perspective, none of these could be the motivation for true innovation. As the VP.Start team saw the frustration of students unable to do research on the Internet due to an unreliable electric supply, they felt frustrated . As they saw factories unable to meet their quotas due to frequent outages, they felt disappointed. As they saw clever industrial leaders unable to finish projects on time or meet deadlines or release new products in a timely fashion, they felt deeply moved and saddened. As they saw families unable to live comfortably because the cost of electricity was too high for them to run an air conditioner or heat water or use lights, they felt compassion. “Compassion”, “caring” and “concern” may not be words that we usually associate with the tech industry and cutting edge innovation but for the SIMA Journey to a sustainable world 168

searchIndex.title: Chapter 2 The SIMA Ideology Remember the Big Picture “If you want to make the world a better place, take a look at yourself and make a change
searchIndex.text: it is a massive mistake to leave compassion out of the equation. VP.Start is not in the business of selling products or promoting services; it is in the business of creating solutions for people in need. Why? Because they genuinely care about their neighbors and their neighbors’ problems. Similarly, the smart city initiatives are innovative solutions to improve street lighting, traffic management, parking and building management, waste collection and other aspects of the urban experience. While grounded in data acquisition and application and implementation of sophisticated systems of sensors and digital monitoring systems with continuous upgrading based on the data, they are so much more than the latest in IoT technological prowess . They are answers to actual human needs, the problems and sufferings of urban citizens, answers that stem from the compassion that VP.Start’s team of engineers feels for their fellow citizens. In much the same way, the smart home automation approaches of VP.Start, are not merely technological strategies to improve appliance usage for greater cost efficiency and less energy waste, although they certainly achieve these goals, as well. These home and office automation and IoT initiatives are based on the fact that families are struggling to pay their electric bills, that, at times, the EDC is struggling to meet their energy needs without relying on excessive energy imports and that nature and the environment are struggling to put up with the wasted energy that makes our world less green and sustainable. 169 VP.Start sees the family trying to make ends meet despite high electricity bills and their hearts go out to them. The team sees the utilities working their hardest to meet energy demand and wants to help in any way they can. CEO Phally and his clan feel the vital importance of connecting with and protecting nature, not because it is good business or good marketing or good branding. Simply because it is good. How often do you do things “simply” because they are the right things to do? The UCN is a profoundly game changing app that combines: Chat and conversation features, AI capabilities, IoT device management and Smart city updates in one convenient app location. It is a groundbreaking, outside the box technological transformation that opens up new possibilities in sustainable connectivity. But in addition to all of that, AlienCheck is a much needed answer to a problem. We have and we need to have too many apps currently. We need separate social media apps, AI apps, IoT device apps and so on. This makes managing and monitoring all these different apps, both challenging and inconvenient. It leads some people to abandon the process in frustration and others feeling stressed out trying to stay on top of a myriad of varied apps. CEO Phally and the VP.Start family saw this situation and felt compassion on people overwhelmed 170

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Ideology Idea Driven, not Product-Driven “The two greatest days of your life are the day you were born and they day you f ind out what your purpose is
searchIndex.text: by too many overlapping apps and the confusion that it bred. But compassion that doesn’t lead to a solution is just romantic, dramatic feelings that don’t really accomplish anything. Think of it like this: Innovation is the engine of progress but compassion is the key that starts the engine running. Or perhaps, as Phally likes to say, “ compassion is the key that unlocks us.” Once unlocked, we can dare to be ourselves, the best version of ourselves, and become the innovators that nature always intended us to be, Innovators that care about others because they know that in reality, we are all part of the same bigger picture, whether we are wealthy tech moguls or refugees languishing in uncomfortable camps. Please remember that in the SIMA philosophy, innovation is the default situation. Innovation is not surprising or unexpected. Lack of innovation is. Innovation is the natural state of man , since man is a part of nature and nature is innovative. Compassion is the natural attitude of people who realize that we are all part of something bigger than ourselves, bigger than our families, bigger than our countries and ethnicities, bigger than our languages and religions and cultural biases. Compassion is the de facto state of a world citizen. It is the only prerequisite to innovation. Everything else can be learned later. 171 Compassion and kindness are the big picture. VP.Start is laser-focused on them. Why do we need to remember that we are a part of the bigger picture, the universe? Why do we need to make compassionate corporate culture central to everything we do? Are you ready to put aside profits and self-promotion and make helping other your goal? If you do so, get ready for the world to change! Chapter 3 The SIMA Ideology Idea Driven, not Product-Driven “The two greatest days of your life are the day you were born and they day you f ind out what your purpose is.” -Shannon Kaiser, author and self-love teacher If this is true for people, it is equally true for companies. The two most important days for every company are the day that the company was founded and the day that the company discovered why it was founded . Hopefully, both happy events come on the same day, but all to often, there is a big gap in time between these two days. Have you discovered your purpose yet? Are you living according to that purpose? 172

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Ideology Idea Driven, not Product-Driven “The two greatest days of your life are the day you were born and they day you f ind out what your purpose is
searchIndex.text: VP.Start knew its purpose on its first day. On its founding day. As a matter of fact, CEO Phally knew the purpose of VP.Start long, long before there was any company. Make the grid reliable, make the future sustainable, spread it to the world. Simple. In other words, from the very beginning, VP.Start was driven by ideas. That is the reason that they were able to make a Very Powerful Start. Dreams, ideas and goals came first. Products and solutions and services came later. So, why does it matter which comes first? Every company requires some customization. It is simply inevitable. Either you customize your products to meet your ideas or you customize your ideas to meet your products. If you do the former , you will keep modifying your product in line with your goals until those goals are achieved. In that case, you will have a crystal clear vision and your entire team will know 173 that vision and buy into it. If you do the latter , you will keep changing your ideas and goals to keep up with your products. In that case , you will have confusion and uncertainty. Your team will not know which road to take. But, let’s be completely frank. Acquiring the “idea-driven” mindset is not always an easy task. Conventional companies focus on products and profits, services and subscriptions, customers and competitors. You cannot break that mindset and replace it with the “idea-driven” mindset overnight. For instance, As mentioned before, VP.Start, like most companies, put effort into establishing a website. Like most corporate websites, it listed products and their features, services and their benefits, successful case studies and satisfied customers. Pretty typical corporate website. But that is the problem. How can an atypical company have a typical website? How can a revolutionary company have a conventional, traditional website? How can an “idea-driven” company have a “product-driven” website? Don’t get the wrong idea. This is not to attack the website designers. They did an outstanding job of creating a conventional, professional website. 174

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Ideology Idea Driven, not Product-Driven “The two greatest days of your life are the day you were born and they day you f ind out what your purpose is
searchIndex.text: Unfortunately, VP.Start needs an innovative, “idea-driven” website. Dramatic changes had to be made. People come to website to see if they can trust a company. How does the company make them feel ? What does the company make them believe ? After visiting the website, what do they remember about the company? Feel. Believe. Remember. The FBR principle. A good website never tries to make you understand. A good website makes you FBR. “What are the products that we sell? At VP.Start, our ideas are the products.” Again, don’t get the wrong idea. VP.Start has amazing products and creative services. They are proud of their home-grown solutions and their “Made For the World” innovations. And yes, of course, VP.Start sells these products, promotes these services, markets their solutions and strives to garner profits. So, is an “idea-driven” company like VP.Start really any different from a traditional company? YES! The mindset maters. The mindset changes everything. Companies that are product-driven are made up of salespeople, marketers, advertisers and promoters. They try to convince you to buy a product whether you really need it or not. 175 They are strategic thinkers, seeking to leverage customers for their company’s financial gain. Let’s be honest. If you are like me at all, you are not a big fan of salespeople. You avoid advertisements and ignore commercials. You despise the manipulation. You especially dislike paid promoters like singers and sports figures and social media influencers who promote and champion a product that they have never used and have scarcely ever heard of. Some companies are worse and some are better, but most are variations on this situation. The “idea-driven” company is totally different. They present a problem to be solved and suggest their innovative solution. VP.Start does not tell you to buy their DRC products but asks if you want a more reliable grid. VP.Start never pressures you to buy home automation IoT gadgets. They explain why they created them, how they can be beneficial And then they leave the decision up to the individual consumer . VP.Start, for example, expresses the philosophy, problem solving and ideology that gave birth to AlienCheck and encourage those who share their views to download. If so inclined. “VP.Start sells its ideas. VP.Start’s ideas sell its products.” Let’s look at another example. We have already talked about the weekly SIMA Journey Hub Conferences held at VP.Start. 176

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Ideology Idea Driven, not Product-Driven “The two greatest days of your life are the day you were born and they day you f ind out what your purpose is
searchIndex.text: Each week a new topic, a new audience, a new opportunity. Early on, topics were suggested such as “The DRC: The Power of Innovation” and “VP.Start’s Grid Solutions.” If such topics were adopted, the weekly forum would be little more than advertising and marketing. And the audience would recognize that and dwindle away. What are people interested in? The products and services of VP.Start? NO! People are interested in themselves. They want to know what technology and innovation means to them personally. They want to see if VP.Start cares about them. They don’t want to understand technology. They want to FBR (feel-believe-remember). Subsequently, the topics were changed to “The Impact of AI Data Centers”, “Tech Jobs of the Future”, “Renewable Energy for a Renewable Future” and so on. Not product promotion. Not services promotion. Idea promotion! Let’s be clear on one more point. You cannot be “idea-driven” unless you have positive thinking. Founding, maintaining and even working for an “idea-driven” company like VP.Start is risky. Undeniably, inescapably, irrefutably risky. Think about this: 177 Even if your product is no good, even worthless garbage, with effective marketing and strategic advertising, you still may be able to make a profit. Even if your services are useless and pointless, if you promote and publicize them cleverly, you may still be able to keep your company in the black. But if you are an “idea-driven” company and your ideas are inadequate and subpar, no amount of ingenious marketing or fantastic promotion is going to save you . Your company will live or die on the power of its ideas, and nothing else. If you have less than absolute confidence in your ideas, your company will be “idea-driven” into the ground. VP.Start has that confidence in their ideas, bordering on arrogance. They are ready to put all their eggs in one basket, the basket of ideas. How about you? Do you believe in what you believe enough to risk everything to make those ideas succeed? If you have less than absolute assurance of the power of your ideas, You are probably better off making and selling a product. Being a follower. Being an echo. Being a marketer. But only those who dare to take the risk, get the chance to experience the reward. The choice is yours. Are you ready to stop selling your products and start selling your ideas? Are you ready to be “idea-driven”? 178

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion
searchIndex.text: 179 Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion.” -W. Edwards Deming, Data Theorist How do you make a decision? What do you base that decision on? VP.Start like any other organization, has to make decisions. Lots of decisions every day. Some decisions are minor like when to schedule a meeting or where to have a dinner with customers. Other decisions are critical and potential deal breakers, such as which foreign markets to enter first or whether or not to collaborate with a certain OEM. But at its core, all decisions have to be based on something. They must either be based on data, or they must be based on something other than data. Needless to say, it is not always easy to get the data that is necessary to make wise decisions. Sometimes we must act with insufficient data, based on feelings, emotions or even guesses. Even in the 4 th Industrial Revolution as AI chatbots become ubiquitous, there is still no one who lives a completely data-driven lifestyle and there is no company that is perfectly data-driven, either. While this is true, 180

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion
searchIndex.text: VP.Start has made the decision to adopt the data-driven mindset. Yes, let’s be clear. Data-driven is a powerful technology but long before data-driven technology, there was the data-driven mindset. In fact, there can be no data-driven technology without a data-driven ideology. What does it mean to have a data-driven mindset and ideology? First, it means that we make decisions based on facts. Second, it means that we are always looking to upgrade. Finally , it means that every result, good or bad, is checked to see if it could be better. These are core beliefs, key pillars, the very soul of VP.Start. Are you ready to make decisions based on the facts and the data? Are you ready to constantly, ruthlessly, relentlessly upgrade those decisions? Are you willing to accept the frustration of always wanting to be better? How can VP.Start achieve grid modernization, smart cities, smart homes? First and foremost, they have to know the details, the facts, the data of the current situation. You cannot solve a problem that you do not really understand. How can VP.Start carry out extensive grid modernization with the DRC and other products unless they know clearly and accurately the faults of the current situation? 181 Common sense, isn’t it? At each step of grid modernization, with each installation of new DRC solutions, with each new SCADA system, with each new RPM grid, there is a new chance to judge those problems even more clearly and accurately. You might be surprised, as VP.Start was on many occasions, that problems that were considered and solutions that were implemented did NOT hold up in the data. How do you respond to data that does not match your assumptions and suppositions? Do you throw away your assumptions or do you throw away the data? For one example, you might be forgiven for thinking that the main or even only purpose for the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is to store solar energy from daylight hours and shift them to nighttime use. Most energy and technology companies view the BESS in this way. Fortunately, VP.Start is not like other companies. They follow the data. Yes, renewables integration and solar energy storage and shifting are roles for theBESS to be sure and one of the ways that the BESS plays a crucial role in the overall sustainability system that VP.Start promotes . But not the only way. Not even the main way. In fact, the data gathered on the BESS shows a quite different picture than conventional wisdom might suggest. In fact, in terms of data results, 182

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion
searchIndex.text: solar energy integration is just a small part of the function of the BESS. Much more critical functions according to data analysis include backing up the grid to prevent blackouts and outages when there is a major grid disruption. Furthermore, balancing second-by-second grid fluctuations are another essential function of the BESS. In other words, the main function and importance of the BESS lies NOT in energy shifting and renewables integration, BUT in ameliorating grid stability. If a company created renewable integration solutions without this data-based understanding of the BESS, there is a very good chance these solutions will not produce the desired outcomes. This is an example where the data points to a deeper purpose that might be lost if we merely focused on our opinions, hunches and estimations. Another common trope in grid modernization is that the only way to solve grid congestion, is to build more transmission wires and infrastructure. Most companies in the energy sector follow this logic. Not surprisingly, building more infrastructure and new transmission lines is expensive, time consuming, environmentally-unfriendly and diff icult to achieve within budget constraints . Once again, VP.Start adamantly refuses to follow accepted wisdom. What does the data say? Data-driven technology points to new technologies, Grid Enhancing Technologies , 183 that allow more efficient and effective use of existing wires and infrastructure, to maximize capacity WITHOUT building new infrastructure . For example, instead of basing load capacity of worst-case scenario weather conditions, data-driven dynamic digital solutions can base load capacity on real-time, constantly updated weather conditions. Similarly, data-driven solutions can reroute power flows instantly and automatically to avoid congested bottlenecks in the power system. These are exactly the kinds of approaches that VP.Start implements. Because VP.Start refuses to follow assumptions and feelings; VP.Start unflinchingly follows the data. Another widespread assumption is that Smart meters lead to significant energy savings and electricity bill reductions. Most companies market their Smart meters and home automation products in this fashion, often leaving customers disappointed with the results. How about VP.Start? The data shows that merely installing IoT devices has only a minimal, negligible effect on energy saving and cost reduction . In many cases, the data shows that there is not benefit to the customer at all. Why? The customers don’t know how to use the devices properly or pay no attention to them at all. Data shows that fewer Than 10% of IoT device customers actually understand their purpose. VP.Start provides regular training, customer service, workshops and tutorials on effective IoT device usage. As a result, there is massive growth in effectiveness of use and customer satisfaction. 184

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion
searchIndex.text: If you didn’t follow the data, this trend might escape your view. But, have no fear, VP.Start follows the data. On a similar note, one of the flagship solutions of VP.Start is the Universal Connectivity Network app, AlienCheck, as has been mentioned before. VP.Start encourages people to download AlienCheck and use it to monitor their IoT devices, connect with conversational features and AI capabilities and much, much more. But data paints a much bigger and clearer picture . The number of people who actually download AlienCheck is certainly valuable data, but it is merely the beginning. How frequently, how effectively and how wisely people are using AlienCheck, these are some key pieces of data that can help VP.Start make sure that AlienCheck is serving its purpose. Does VP.Start need more online videos to show people how to make effective use of the app? Does the app itself need to be transformed to be more intuitive? Does something as basic as the color scheme or font need to be changed to make it more user-friendly? Are customers finding the AlienCheck experience satisfactory? If not, why not? 185 These questions can only be answered with data. And this accumulation of data leads us naturally to the second point of contention. Constant, continuous, relentless, endless upgrading. The data-driven ideology is never satisfied, always seeking better, more effective, more efficient. Good enough is never good enough. Sufficient and adequate are always insufficient and inadequate. If handled unwisely, the data-driven mindset adopted by VP.Start can be unsettling and frustrating. Let me share a personal example to illustrate my point. Once I attended a camp in Japan as a counselor. At the end of the week-long camp, all of the counselors were called together for a meeting. I thought that overall, while not perfect, of course, the camp had been a success. The campers had enjoyed themselves, the experience had been a good one. But the meeting started without congratulations on a job well done or appreciation for successes. Would you rather be satisfied or would you rather be better? I would learn later that this kind of meeting in Japan was called “Hansei-kai” (reflection or self-criticism meeting) and that it was common practice in Japan. Every possible way to make improvements was discussed and 186

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion
searchIndex.text: every problem and foible was dissected in extreme detail. As a non-Japanese person new to the experience, I found it very frustrating and irritating. We had just finished what I considered to be a great camp and we now nitpicking every minor flaw and fault endlessly. In a sense, the data-driven philosophy is similar to this. We are never satisfied with our results because the data always tells us that things could be better. CEO Phally himself often speaks of his frustration, frequently after an experience that most people would consider a resounding success. Good return on investment? Not good enough. Improved energy efficiency? Not improved enough. Better English speech making? Not nearly enough. The Grid is still not smart enough, Not digital enough, Not dynamic enough, Not extended enough, Not renewable enough, Not affordable enough, Not reliable enough. Each success and each milestone reminds VP.Start that: the sustainable world has not yet been obtained , the final destination has not yet been reached , the SIMA Journey has not yet been completed . If VP.Start allowed emotions to overrule their judgment, this could lead to depression and despondence and ultimately to giving up in despair. But VP.Start refuses to give up because they are led not by feelings and 187 emotions, but by data. The third stage of the data-driven mindset and the data-driven lifestyle is the hardest of all. Data shows simultaneously the impossibility of the task AND the way to achieve that task. Without this crazy mindset, there is no point in following the data-driven ideology at all. After each result, we must compare it with the data to see the ways in which that result was sub-optimal. As mentioned with the camp example above, this is especially uncomfortable when we feel we have had a signature success. At those special moments, the last thing that most people want to think about what went wrong and how to make things better. It is much easier to seek better results when we feel our early results were clearly unacceptable. It is not at all easy to seek better results when our results were undeniably good, but could still be even better. As an example, I have had a chance to attend several events where CEO Phally was the keynote speaker. For instance, there was a major conference in downtown Phnom Penh where Phally delivered a major address on the topic of the power of innovative technology. The audience featured university students, 188

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Ideology Data-Driven, not Feelings-Driven “Without data, you are just another person with an opinion
searchIndex.text: government officials, visiting international dignitaries and tech industry leaders. It was a big opportunity to promote and bring forward the SIMA Journey. Unfortunately, the slides used in the speech were too complicated and contained too much information. Also, it was one of the first times for Phally to give a major speech in English before such a distinguished crowd and by his own account, he got flustered and lost his place in the speech a few times. Furthermore, he didn’t make as much of a connection with the audience as he had hoped and in the end, he was disappointed with the results. The data-driven mindset was perfect for this occasion as there was much to upgrade. Simpler and fewer slides. More audience participation. Better voice control at the speech opening and a more compelling conclusion. Less dependence on prepared notes and slides and more spontaneity. More frequent speech making in English in less consequential and high-pressure forums. A few months later, Phally gave a speech at a European Chamber of Commerce, Cambodia (EuroCham) function on the topic of EV adoption, a topic which is not exactly a specialty of VP.Start. And yet, this time, the speech was smoother, the conclusion was stronger, 189 the connection with the audience was deeper, the slides were fewer, simpler and there was no confusion, the EV adoption topic was seamlessly weaved into the larger sustainability system framework and the SIMA Journey, and the speech was, while not perfect, a resounding success. It is at this point that the data-driven ideology becomes crystal clear. Far from resting on his laurels over a clearly much better speech, he was still unsatisfied . Always unsatisf ied. CEO Phally felt that The introduction could have been more gripping. A wider variety of English vocabulary could have been employed. He could have moved more on the stage instead of standing rather immobile. The data-driven ideology states that success is only temporary. The only permanent thing is upgrading. This is how the Big Data revolution as envisioned and implemented by VP.Start works. Using solutions like the DRC, VP.Start accumulates data from the grid, IoT devices, AlienCheck and Smart City and home automation sensors. This data is cleansed, stored in a retrievable form and the acquisition continues. Next off, this data is put into a myriad of simulation scenarios including digital twins, to find the best possible usage of the data to improve grid, smart city, smart home and AlienCheck functions and operations. When the best solution is discovered from the data, 190

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Ideology Break the Rules “Know the rules well, so you can break them effectively
searchIndex.text: these data-based solutions are applied to the sustainability system of VP.Start to maximize efficiency, reduce waste and increase savings. Is this the end of the process? NO! This is just the beginning. These outcomes of data application become new data to be collected, analyzed, simulated and applied. Improved. Upgraded. Endlessly. Let’s be honest. The data-driven ideology is not always comfortable and satisfying. In fact, it can be quite frustrating and irritating and off-putting. But the best answers can only be found and achieved in this way. So my question to use is a simple one: Is good enough good enough for you? Or do you insist on following the data-driven ideology for endless improvement? The SIMA Journey belongs to those who choose the pain and joy of continuous growth. 191 Chapter 5 The SIMA Ideology Break the Rules “Know the rules well, so you can break them effectively.” -Dalai Lama, Tibetan Buddhist leader Do you know the rules? Are you ready to break them for your ideas? VP.Start is a leading company in the 4 th Industrial Revolution, sometimes called the Revolution of Data. A revolution is more than just novelty or unusual ideas or even innovation. A true revolution MUST break the rules of the past. There is no such thing as a traditional, conventional revolution. When you meet CEO Phally for the first time, you will probably notice something about him before he says anything or does anything. Take a moment to look at his photo. You will most likely notice, as so many visitors to VP.Start have, his long, full, somewhat curly hair. In Cambodia, it is very rare, indeed, to see anyone with a hairstyle like this, especially a CEO. If Phally worked for a “regular” company, he would almost surely have to cut his hair in a more conventional style. Fortunately, when you are the CEO, you get some special permissions. So let me ask you: Is a hairstyle really important? Yes and No. 192

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Ideology Break the Rules “Know the rules well, so you can break them effectively
searchIndex.text: Of course, a hairstyle says nothing about a company’s plans or footprint or ideas or projects. You can’t learn much at all from a haircut. And yet, this is not completely true, either. Why does Phally wear his hair in an unconventional way? To make a statement? No. To confound expectations? No, nothing complicated like that. He wears his hair that way because he likes it that way. Simple. Yet, this encapsulates the “break the rules” ideology. Some people might not approve. Some people might criticize. Some people might laugh. Some people might approve. An innovator with a “break the rules” mindset doesn’t really care what others think. “If I like it, I do it. If I don’t, I don’t. If I break the rules, written or unwritten, I don’t really care one way or the other.” Are you prepped to “change the game”? Do you even know what the “game” is? For a very long time, rugby had been a popular sport. Running with a ball, passing it backwards or sideways and moving up and down the field to score points. Football (soccer) was also popular and many rugby teams chose to move the ball without using their hands, relying merely on kicking the ball. However in one rugby football game, in 1880, 193 the coach of Yale University encouraged his players to pick up the ball with their hands and pass the ball forward, which was directly against the rules of the sport. Nevertheless, the idea became popular quickly and soon “forward passing” became a key element of a new sport, American football. This was literally a “game changing” innovation . VP.Start has a similar spirit of experimentation and revolutionary change . Are you ready to break the rules if you think that it benefits your customers? Even if these changes make your personal success and your companies profits harder to achieve? Case in point, in the 3 rd Industrial Revolution, the so-called Digital Revolution , social media was a key player in the sweeping changes. When VP.Start invented AlienCheck, many observers, even in the internal team, foresaw another social media app to go alongside Telegram and Messenger and Whatsapp and others. If that were true, if AlienCheck were just another social media app, that would not be revolutionary at all. No rules would be broken. AlienCheck would be a follower, not a leader. But that is not the case. Not at all. VP.Start designed AlienCheck to break all the rules of social media. After all, AlienCheck is NOT a 3 rd Industrial Revolution social media app. 194

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Ideology Break the Rules “Know the rules well, so you can break them effectively
searchIndex.text: AlienCheck is a 4 th Industrial Revolution data-driven sustainability app. Social media makes a profit by gathering as many users as possible , persuading these users to frequent the app as often as possible , convincing users to stay on the app as long as possible , and ultimately encouraging them to buy products recommended by the app tailored to the users’ algorithmic preferences. As many have put it, social media users and their data are the products . Social media companies leverage the data of users to make massive profits. Hence, social media moguls are always among the richest people in the world even though ostensibly they give away their products for free. VP.Start took a good look at this rule of the social media business and determined to break it. After all, these social media rules were not designed to benefit the customers in the first place. The AlienCheck developers thought: What if instead of gathering the maximum number of users, we only tried to add users who would benefit from the app? What if , instead of leveraging the users and their data, we created an app designed to allow users to leverage their own data? What if , instead of trying to maximize the frequency of user access to our app, whether they were really gaining something from the access or not, we tried to keep access to the bare minimum of usefulness? What if , instead of trying to keep users on the app as long as possible with recommendations and addictive algorithms, we attempted to make the app as efficient as possible to keep “on app” time minimal? 195 What if , we created an app that was not social media at all, and furthermore, was not designed to promote advertising and sales and marketing, but took user productivity and sustainability as its goal? What if , in one app, we created a universal connectivity network? The AlienCheck programmers and developers were imbued with the VP.Start ideology, the “know the rules, so you can break the rules” mentality. They decided that in order to benefit the users, they were willing to break every rule of traditional social media apps. What rules need to be broken in order for you to become who you were meant to be? What rules need to be broken to make your innovations succeed and your dreams come true? Another “break the rules” approach of VP.Start was in the interface of AlienCheck with home automation IoT devices. A common problem across IoT apps and platforms was that they tended to only allow access to IoT gadgets aligned with that company. After all, why would you create an IoT framework app that would help customers use your competitors products? It seems like bad business practice. It seems like bad business practice UNLESS you are a revolutionary company that breaks the rules. From the beginning, VP.Start was determined to make the AlienCheck app platform interoperable 196

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Ideology Break the Rules “Know the rules well, so you can break them effectively
searchIndex.text: with all IoT devices and home automations solutions whether they were produced by VP.Start or not. Interoperability makes AlienCheck more intuitive to use and more fruitful and advantageous for users. Would this mean that AlienCheck users might be more inclined to use home automation gadgets and appliances produced by competitors? Yes. But remember, according to the SIMA Ideology, true innovators have no real competitors . Instead of competitors weakening the market share of VP.Start’s home automation smart meters, these competitors would actually be strengthening the value of AlienCheck , intentionally or otherwise. How could AlienCheck call itself a Universal Connectivity Network if it limited itself to VP.Start products and services? How could such a limited app be part of the overarching sustainability system? Are you prepared to accept the ridicule that sometimes accompanies breaking the rules? When you start breaking the rules, as VP.Start consistently does, the feedback will not always be positive . When the pioneers of aviation started making the first attempt at manned flight and airplanes, they were mocked, ridiculed and criticized as fools. According to a famous critique of the day, “ If God had wanted man to fly, he would have given man wings. ” Those pioneers and innovators ignored the ridicule and broke the rules. 197 Every time you get on an airplane, you are recognizing the value of breaking the rules. You are honoring the revolutionaries who were not stopped by the “impossibility” of human flight. When the first astronauts stepped on the moon, they were walking in the footsteps of these “crazy” dreamers. Are you willing to speak “truth to power” in order to break the rules? When VP.Start went to the banking system with their radical approaches and rule breaking disposition, not so surprisingly, they were not always welcomed with open arms. Even though, many financiers and bankers respected the ideas and innovations, these ideas seemed a bit too risky, too radical, too revolutionary. Bank after bank would ultimately refuse to finance VP.Start projects because VP.Start didn’t follow the established, conventional procedures. Where was the starting capital? The collateral? The assets? Phally responded that their assets were their ideas, their collateral was their innovation . Sadly, banks fell back on regulatory frameworks and traditional practices and time-tested approaches. The banks were not ready to break their rules for the company that broke the rules. At the same time, VP.Start was completely unwilling to customize itself to make its plans and projects more appetizing to the banks. Once you make a commitment to breaking the rules, “unbreaking” those rules will destroy your entire business plan and 198

Phally: We cannot change our culture to fit your rules. We would become just another engineering services company. Chapter 6 The SIMA Ideology The Three Aspects of Powerful Thinking “Failure is not the end, it’s an opportunity to learn and grow.” -Jensen Huang, CEO of NVidia Who are your role models in thinking? Do you learn more from your failures or from your successes? CEO Phally, as a young student, as we mentioned in the Story Section, had no desire to be the top student in the class or to get the best grade on the test. He was never drawn to the top students, the studious and the clever. He was naturally attracted to the least successful students, the laziest, weakest, least motivated students. Not with a condescending attitude or even with a desire to change them. He just wanted to figure out, 200

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Ideology The Three Aspects of Powerful Thinking “Failure is not the end, it’s an opportunity to learn and grow
searchIndex.text: to diagnose their reason for lack of interest, lack of energy, lack of academic growth. For the young Phally, while academic success meant nothing and academic awards meant even less, there was no greater joy than thinking. It struck Phally as peculiar, an almost unfathomable mystery, that some students, in fact, many students, found thinking and learning distasteful and unpleasant. Phally was not so much an evangelist trying to convince these students of the value of thinking. He was examining and evaluating these students, largely unconsciously, to try to figure out why thinking and learning were so valuable and enjoyable to himself. Not surprisingly, coming from this background, VP.Start values thinking. In this regard, there is nothing so out of the ordinary from other companies. But from the perspective of the SIMA Ideology, there is a big difference between the way most people and companies think and powerful thinking. Truly powerful thinking. Powerful thinking requires three aspect working together, according to the SIMA perspective. Logical thinking, creative thinking AND positive thinking. If you are lacking in any of these areas, you can never really be called a “thinker” and 201 you definitely cannot become a world-class innovator. The stereotypical “engineer” or “tech guy” is strong on logic, moderately creative and almost completely lacking positive thinking skills. This is an oversimplification and overgeneralization, of course, but perhaps, it is not without some basis in reality. After all, engineering relies on the logical skills of mathematics and physics, solving complex equations and explaining operations down to the minutest details. Coding and programming are also logic-based by definition. Similarly, one potential problem of artificial intelligence is that it is by its very nature highly logical but lacking in creativity and, of course, completely bereft of true positive thinking. In that sense, according to the SIMA Ideology, AI is unable to “truly” think. When someone is strong on logic and weak in the other two areas of intelligence , they tend to act as “teachers” or “professors”, sages on the stage, talking down to customers and potential investors from a position of superior knowledge. They can easily become condescending. From a personal example, I recall one math teacher that I knew in my school days who would frequently berate students who didn’t learn and understand complex math concepts after the first explanation. He would say to the class, he had understood it easily, so they should be able to understand it easily as well. He was a highly logical teacher with almost no creative or positive thinking. 202

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Ideology The Three Aspects of Powerful Thinking “Failure is not the end, it’s an opportunity to learn and grow
searchIndex.text: As you might well imagine, he was not very popular with his students. On the other hand, there is the legendary physics professor from California, Richard Feynman, who could explain the most complicated and arcane physics concepts in simple layman’s terms, due to amazingly creative storytelling skills. Professor Feynman was a very logical man, as well, undeniably, but he allowed creativity and positivity to guide his teaching. He was, from the SIMA point of view, a true thinker and a world-class innovator and communicator. Some people have creative thinking but lack logic and positivity. These people are the proverbial “starving artists”. They have creative ideas but lack the logic to explain their ideas or the empathy to make people care about their ideas. These kind of “innovators” tend to irritate people with their “odd behavior”. People quite often don’t think of them as creative but as simply strange. Then there are those that have positive thinking but lack logic and creativity . They are the eternal optimists who always believe that tomorrow will be a better day. Unfortunately, they don’t do anything to make tomorrow better . They probably have a lot of friends because they are positive and fun to be around but in the end, they accomplish very little because they have no creative strategies or logical plans to help them go forward. In business, the “logical thinking only” people are irritating and overbearing and tend to drive customers, potential investors and collaborators away. The “creative thinking only” crowd are considered strange and peculiar 203 and they are unable to explain why their often great ideas are great. The “positive thinking only” folks make customers and supporters feel good and happy but in the end, they cannot lead these stakeholders to make a decision to support their company. VP.Start insists that all employees must be powerful thinkers, deploying all three of the thinking skills. You can think about it this way. If you lack logical thinking, how can you give a clear presentation of your business plans and goals? If you lack creative thinking, how can you create a business plan that is not just a sad imitation of the business plan of other companies? If you lack positive thinking, how can you get stakeholders excited about your ideas and plans, ideas that you yourself don’t seem to be very excited about? On the other hand, when you are a powerful thinker, you are a game changer, a world beater and a lead actor. Your creative thinking gives you amazing innovations and solutions that have never been thought of before. This means that you have no competitors, a completely blue sea situation. Your logical thinking means that you can explain your ideas clearly, concisely and effectively and persuade people of the value of your vision. Your positive thinking means that you are enthusiastic about your ideas and you share that enthusiasm with everyone you meet. It doesn’t matter if the other person is a high government official with policy proposals, 204

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Ideology The Three Aspects of Powerful Thinking “Failure is not the end, it’s an opportunity to learn and grow
searchIndex.text: the CEO of a unicorn suggesting a merger or a new customer with a “stupid” question. (Of course, there are no stupid questions but I think you know what I mean.) All of them get the same infectious enthusiasm because positive thinkers don’t know how to give out negativity. Think about nature for a moment. Animals need to be logical. If I, as an animal, see a bigger predator, and I know that that predator is stronger than me and likely to eat me, I will run away as fast as I can, because logic tells me that this is the wise approach. Otherwise I might be eaten. If I, as an animal, need to cross a river to access a food source but I cannot swim or if the river current is too strong, I must find a creative way to get to the other side. Otherwise I might starve to death . And, if I, as an animal, head out into the natural world, I must do it without fear or hesitation, convinced that I will succeed in getting food and raising my young. Without positivity , why would I take the risk of having offspring? I must have positivity and believe in myself. Otherwise I might never find a mate. Powerful thinking is key part of nature and nature informs all the practices of every wise tech company, including VP.Start. Finally, powerful thinking is not always easy. Not at all. 205 As CEO Phally would say, “Thinking is a choice.” Are there times when it seems easier to abandon logical, creative and positive thinking? How do we maintain our commitment to powerful thinking? There are days when there may be team problems, power outages, cyber attacks, weather disruptions, lower profits than expected, contract cancellations and other discouraging developments. It would be easy to become negative and pessimistic. Do you allow negative thinking to creep in and do you CHOOSE to be a positive thinker? There are times when it seems easier to just follow the ideas of other companies or rehash your own ideas from the past, rather than taking the time and effort to create new solutions. Do you allow yourself to copy others and imitate the past or do you CHOOSE to prioritize creative thinking? There are moment when following logical procedures is a lot of trouble and hassle. It would be much easier to cut corners and not follow all the proper processes. We might even think that probably no one would ever notice. We might even be right. So, do we accept the easy and lazy way or do we CHOOSE to emphasize logical thinking? The choice belongs to everyone and at times, we all make the wrong choices. Needless to say, the VP.Start team is not immune to these mistake 206

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Ideology The Three Aspects of Powerful Thinking “Failure is not the end, it’s an opportunity to learn and grow
searchIndex.text: and errors. But at its core, when VP.Start is true to its beliefs and ideology, the clan succeeds or fails because the team chooses to be powerful thinkers or they don’t. The success of the past suggests that VP.Start has learned well the value of the triple helix of powerful thinking . But yesterday’s success does not guarantee success tomorrow . The team must rededicate itself to choosing powerful thinking every day . Having powerful thinking does not ensure that you will be a world-class communicator BUT you will not be a world-class communicator without positive thinking, creative thinking and logical thinking . CEO Phally would like to pose a question to all of you, dear readers. Have you made your choice? And, have you made your choice again TODAY? 207 208 206

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control. That’s simply not true. You can improve the control of events instead of the control of people. The more people you have proactively working to create favorable events - the more control you have, by def inition.” -Wilbur Creech, US Military Thinker and General As we stated in the last chapter, VP.Start values powerful thinking. The SIMA Journey necessitates powerful thinking combining creativity, logic and positivity. Decentralization takes powerful thinking to the next logical step. For example, if you work for VP.Start, you almost certainly have a solid skill set, expertise, experience and areas of technical prowess. Yet, to state the quite obvious, you also have deficiencies and limitations in some areas. You may be an incredible coder or software developer but know little about marketing strategies. Or, you may be a world-class engineer but have very limited public speaking abilities. In terms of creativity, You may be an outside of the box thinker with revolutionary ideas in your domain, Be it sales or business development or communication. 209 But it is highly unlikely that you will be breathtakingly innovative across ALL domains . Even a highly positive team member can face moments of discouragement and doubt . Do you value your team and their ideas over your own? Do you believe that they can bring things to the table that you cannot? Decentralization comes from the philosophical perspective that our logic is better than my logic, our creativity exceeds my creativity and our positivity outweighs and surpasses my creativity. If you want truly powerful thinking at the corporate level, you need to give everyone a voice and a seat at the table. Corporate powerful thinking is a powerhouse that individual powerful thinking can never match. However, c orporate powerful thinking requires decentralization to exist and thrive. You might think that decentralization would belong in the Methodology Section of this book, rather than the Ideology Section. CEO Phally would not agree. As he likes to put it, “ Decentralization is a mindset before it is corporate governance architecture.” Think about it in this way, if you would: A company can build a decentralized management model, forge agile teams, remove corporate titles and 210

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: flatten the entire company hierarchy. But decentralized management will never succeed in a company that does not have a decentralized mindset . Are you willing to take the risk of having a decentralized mindset? There are some core beliefs that inform the SIMA decentralized mindset: 1) Creativity can never be taught or managed; it can only be nurtured and fostered. 2) Centralized corporate governance can maintain a company or optimize a product but it can never be transformative. 3) CEOs and management teams are optional but understanding of and commitment to a shared vision are not. 4) A decentralized company does not seek qualified, highly skilled employees. It seeks staff members that are creative, positive and above all else, passionate. 5) If you have a limited, closed mindset, how can you expect unlimited, universal outcomes? 6) The best CEO is not the one who leads from the front but the one who gradually disappears. There are some contentious and controversial claims here, so let’s look at them one by one. 1) Creativity can never be taught or managed; it can only be nurtured and fostered. This is the basis on which SIMA decentralized management is built. A successful company does not provide lectures and lessons and workshops on creativity as if it is a subject to be mastered like a programming language. If creativity and innovative thinking could be taught, centralized management might be a wise idea . The most creative person would be the leader and 211 she or he would impart their creativity to the team members, correcting their errors and enhancing their innovative skills. But creativity is not like that at all. Creativity comes from inside of each one of us. From becoming ourselves. From ceasing to be a follower. Any attempt to manage or manipulate this process will instantly destroy all creativity . That would be like a company demanding creative solutions and then laying out the detailed parameters of what those solutions must look like. If we follow those parameters to the letter without exception, we are trying to create outside the box solutions inside the box . A decentralized company allows team members to experiment, to learn and grow, to try outlandish ideas and even, to fail spectacularly. Failures are noted as learning experiences on the road to innovation. Only in a company with this kind of decentralized, nurturing atmosphere, can creativity dare to grow. If you ask me to be creative, but punish me when I fail, I will avoid failure and ignore my creativity. Are you ready to allow to yourself to try new things and to fail spectacularly? As mentioned before, VP.Start has inaugurated a weekly Friday conference, open to all, called the SIMA Journey Conference. This conference is a chance to discuss and examine 212

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: some of the latest trends in cutting edge technology but it is also an opportunity for a wide variety of team members to speak publicly. They create their own presentations, design their own slides and do their own research. Some speeches are excellent. Some are less so. All of them are valuable. Team members get a chance to raise their voices, hone their speaking skills and feel valued by their company, which they are! 2) Centralized corporate governance can maintain a company or optimize a product but it can never be transformative. Steve Jobs founded Apple and imbued it with revolutionary ideas and innovative principles. After his death, he was replaced by Tim Cook, who maintained and managed the company. This is not at all a criticism of Tim Cook, since Apple became much more profitable and successful under Tim Cook than it was under Steve Jobs. The point is that Steve Jobs was a transformative leader who built a company that people FBR (feel, believe and remember). Tim Cook was never a transformative leader nor did he ever intend to be one. He was an amazing manager, a powerful product optimizer and a great team builder. 213 Maybe we can think of it like this: In Hindu theology, there are the three central deities: Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Brahma is the creator , the force of creativity and transformation. Vishnu is the preserver , the one who maintains and manages and upholds. Shiva is the destroyer , the one who clears away the past so Brahma can create anew. Companies can be compared to this pattern: Founders and innovators like CEO Phally are the Brahma figures, creating a new company and new ideas out of nothing. This is like the stage of decentralized management. Vishnu is the maintainer, the optimizer, the preserver and protector. This is the post-founder stage of a company, similar to centralized management. Finally, inevitably, Shiva arrives with disruption and destruction. But this destruction is not negative. It is an opportunity to return to the creative roots and start over again. In the SIMA ideological view, that is the difference between centralized and decentralized management, as well. If you want t o improve your products, enhance your services, maintain and extend your market share and make continued incremental growth, centralized management might be the best choice for you. On the other hand, if you want a revolution, 214

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: an exponential explosion, a transformation, you must opt for decentralized management . Are you seeking optimization or transformation? Are you seeking incremental or exponential growth? Whichever one you are seeking is probably what you will find! Again, to be crystal clear, there is absolutely nothing wrong with a well-managed business, growing gradually but consistently. But, this is not the model that VP.Start selected. They decided to change the world more sustainably . More radically. More explosively. They decided to go for radical transformation. Decentralized management is an inevitable part of that decision. 3) CEOs and management teams are optional but understanding of and commitment to a shared vision are not. According to the SIMA ideology of decentralization, titles and positions are relatively insignificant. A great idea is a great idea whether developed by a CEO or a brand new team member. Are you willing to minimize your position to maximize teamwork and cooperation? When CEOs and dignitaries from other companies and government bodies visit VP.Start, they are often surprised to be met by a delegation of ordinary team members. This is not disrespect. Or laziness on the part of the management team. 215 This is decentralization. The CEO makes a conscientious effort not to cover events and meetings that could be covered just as effectively or even more effectively by others. Occasionally, the VP.Start team members themselves are surprised to be put in charge of international delegations like the recent ones to Malaysia and Singapore for product compliance. While positions, titles and corporate governance hierarchy may be optional, if decentralization is attempted without a clear understanding of the destination and the vision of the the company, this can quickly lead to utter chaos. Consider this: If we get in a car, and half the passengers want to go to Siem Reap to see Angkor Wat and the other half want to go to Sihanoukville, to swim and relax on the beach, and if we take turns at driving, changing the driver at fixed intervals, where will we end up? Probably not at Siem Reap or Sihanoukville, I dare say. If everyone share the same destination, sharing the driving makes life easier for everyone. If there are multiple, competing destinations, sharing the driving leads to anger, arguments and chaos. Not exactly what companies hope for. That’s why many companies support decentralization in theory but reject it in practice . VP.Start recognizes the potential for decentralization to descend into confusion and complication. 216

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: But they feel that the answer is not to give up on decentralization but instead, to make sure that everyone is on the same page, on the same journey, following the same vision, to the same goals. One of the purposes that this book is hoping to accomplish is to lay out the SIMA Journey in a written form so team members can stay on track or get back on track even in a highly decentralized corporate culture. Are you willing to abandon your personal views at times to stay aligned with the corporate vision?
