A highly creative and innovative company like VP.Start CAN survive without a centralized management structure but it won’t last a day UNLESS EVERY team member knows the company vision and aligns themselves with it. 4) A decentralized company does not seek qualified, highly skilled employees. It seeks staff members that are creative, positive and above all else, passionate. This is an idea that you could easily misinterpret because this part of the SIMA decentralized management philosophy might be the most counterintuitive of all . To state the extremely obvious, most companies look for highly qualified and suitably experienced candidates with direct knowledge, background and skills and expertise for the position on offer. To do otherwise, to most observers, would seem foolhardy and ridiculous. But VP.Start is never afraid of looking foolhardy or ridiculous. Their theory is that skills and abilities can be developed later, 217 experience and expertise can be honed on the job and knowledge can be expanded fairly easily. Conversely, creativity can not be learned or taught . It is a decision to be yourself. To dare to be yourself. To ignore what others think about you. Creativity cannot be forced on someone but without it, a candidate is simply unsuitable for VP.Start. Similarly, positive thinking is something that a person must develop and choose by themselves. Those who lack positive thinking will find working in VP.Start an uncomfortable experience indeed. The VP.Start team spends all their time outside of the comfort zone, testing their boundaries and pushing their limits. If that is not a place or a circumstance that you would choose to be in, you will be unhappy at VP.Start and before too long, you will leave. But even more than the attributes of creative thinking and positive thinking, a successful VP.Start candidate must be passionate about the VP.Start vision. Without passionate belief in the importance of achieving the goals of a sustainable world, there is no way that candidates and a new team members will be able to put up with the demanding schedule and meet the challenging deadlines. What are you desperately, deeply passionate about? What are you so dedicated to that you are truly “all in”? In this context, CEO Phally often talks about “optional” team members. These are people who work at VP.Start but they are not “all in.” They are often very talented and skilled. As a result, they are open to other opportunities with better pay and benefits. 218

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: They always keep one eye open for other opportunities. Nothing wrong with this, of course, but it indicates less than total passion for the vision. Or, in the opposite vein, some candidates come to VP.Start because all other options have already failed. As a last resort. Either way, they do not have an absolute commitment to the VP.Start vision. At some point, it is highly likely that they will leave. Recently, I heard the story of two highly qualified candidates that were rejected by the VP.Start hiring team. Both were graduates of international universities with very solid reputations in tech. Both had a high level of skills in their respective fields and considerable experience. Both were very fluent in English and ready to help VP.Start on its push to the global stage. But each one had their own fatal flaw. The first one was a highly creative and talented candidate who had tried one more than one occasion to start his own business and had failed. A bit of red flag. This indicated probable limitations to positive thinking and passion. But that alone would not derail a candidate. The real issue was that he had come to VP.Start as a kind of last option after everything else had fallen apart. That sealed his rejection. VP.Start and the SIMA Journey cannot be your last choice. It must be your ONLY choice. 219 All or nothing. The other candidate was quite the opposite. He had had an outstanding career and he saw the potential of working with VP.Start as a great, golden opportunity. Unfortunately, rather than embracing the VP.Start vision or even making the effort to understand it, he wanted to make changes to bring it more in line with conventional business strategies. Inside the box thinking. Inside the comfort zone, “normal ” practices. In other words, he was not positive about VP.Start corporate culture, he was not passionate about accomplishing the SIMA Journey and especially the SIMA Ideology and he looked down on the company as in need of more conventional, traditional thinking. Many companies would be excited to hire a quality candidate like him but for an idea-driven company like VP.Start, he was not a good fit. CEO Phally often says that his current job is “his last job.” This is not a morbid prophecy of impending death It merely means that he has no intention of doing anything else for the rest of his life. VP.Start looks for employees with that same mindset. Mindset over skill set. Are you willing to adopt a “this is my last job” mindset? 5) If you have a limited, closed mindset, how can you expect unlimited, universal outcomes? Decentralized management is undeniably a risky philosophy . It could lead to confusion, chaos and even corporate catastrophe. 220

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: It is certainly much easier to adopt a conventional, centralized approach. The CEO and management team can make all the decisions, chair all the meetings, lead all the projects, welcome all the visitors, give all the speeches, control the company completely. Everyone speaks from the same script, follows the same rules and all decisions are made in the classic “waterfall” style. Top down. Follow the chain of command. Obey the rules of the hierarchy. For a conventional company, centralized management may work just fine. As a matter of fact, for a manufacturing company or an engineering company or any product-driven company, centralized management may be the ideal. But NOT for VP.Start. VP.Start is not selling a product. VP.Start is not building a brand. VP.Start is not promoting services. VP.Start is not marketing and publicizing and announcing to gain greater traction or profitability. VP.Start wants to change the world . Make it more greenable. More reliable. More sustainable. Radically different desired outcomes require radically different approaches. 221 For instance, at one pitching conference, Phally was pulled aside after a speech by the hosts of the event and told to stop talking about “changing the world.” Too bold. Too aggressive. Too arrogant. Furthermore, he was told to stop asking for $100M in investment support. Stick to $1M, he was told. $100M is too massive. Too radical. Too excessive. What do you think that Phally’s reaction was? Phally responded that it was only arrogant to say that you were going to change the world, if you couldn’t do it. If you could change the world and you had the ideas to do so and the passion to do so, where was the arrogance? If you have earth shattering ideas, why not say so? And why ask for only a small amount of support when you are trying to change the world? Such a small ask would mean that you didn’t really intend to change the world at all. Decentralization is the only option for people who are not satisfied to be conventional and want to spark a revolution. They know that there are no incredible outcomes without taking incredible risks. 222

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Ideology Radical Decentralization “Many people think that decentralization means loss of control
searchIndex.text: 6) The best CEO is not the one who leads from the front but the one who gradually disappears. CEO Phally is a wise and firm believer in the idea of impermanence. We have no guarantee of tomorrow, no promise of next year or of even 5 minutes from now, for that matter. Therefore, a wise CEO is ALWAYS preparing his team for corporate life without him. If the CEO becomes indispensable, this guarantees catastrophe down the road. Directly related to this concept is the further idea of living in the present. NOW. Accomplish everything that you can today because you may not have any future beyond today. Oddly, this is not a sad realization or a cruel expression of the universe, but it is a comfort to innovators like Phally. There is no longer any need to worry endlessly about the things that we cannot control. Most of things that we fear never happen anyway. Be in the now, live in the now, love life without limits and gladly accept the reality that “this too shall pass.” Of course, at the beginning of a corporate lifespan, it falls to the Founder and the CEO to establish the vision, nurture the culture and inculcate it into each team member. At the earliest stages of company development, the CEO must be a leader at almost all times, 223 in all meetings, in all decisions. But this is not the optimal situation and it is not sustainable over the long haul. As soon as possible, CEO Phally began downsizing himself and downloading responsibilities and opportunities onto the team. He became a master of delegation. He still remained the voice of the company, the face of the company, and the arbiter of the the most important, big picture decisions. But the everyday decisions were left to the team. The CEOs main job had transformed into monitoring whether the team was maintaining fidelity to the core vision of the SIMA Journey or not. In actual practice, CEO Phally has been gradually disappearing, spending more time in meditation at the pagoda, spending more time improving his communications skills, spending more time “with himself ” as he puts it. His ultimate goal is to become completely unnecessary and one day to simply walk away. Hopefully no one will notice that he is gone. You may find this radical decentralization ideology to be extreme. And, to be fair, it would be inaccurate to claim that it has already been fully implemented. Some parts may never be implemented to the most radical extent. Be that as it may, CEO Phally believes that emphasizing and envisioning decentralization is in some ways as mission critical as full 224

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Ideology Love Everyone But Don’t Care About Anyone “People who are not interested in people, are the most interesting people
searchIndex.text: implementation. The SIMA Decentralization Mindset. How far the SIMA decentralization program takes them, still remains to be seen. True decentralization is risky, radical, revolutionary. Are you ready to take the risk, adopt the radical and revolutionary mindset? Are you ready to walk the walk and not just talk the talk? 225 Chapter 8 The SIMA Ideology Love Everyone But Don’t Care About Anyone “People who are not interested in people, are the most interesting people.” -CEO Phally On the surface, this quote may seem like a contradiction. Love everyone but don’t care about anyone? And in a way, it is. But sometimes it takes grappling with a contradiction to get us to the next level in our thinking. Do you love others? Or do you merely want to sell them your product? If you do love others, do you care about what they think about you? If we like flowers, we may choose to cut them and put them in a vase. But not if we love flowers. But if we love flowers, we will never cut them. We will let them grow and watch them grow from a distance . If you love people, you will let them grow and leave them alone. Phally loves his team and indeed everyone else as well. But he is not interested in them. He lets them grow in their own way at their own pace. Let’s think about an example to try to fathom this concept: Phally had just returned from a business trip to Germany. On the off days, he went sightseeing in Potsdam between conferences 226

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Ideology Love Everyone But Don’t Care About Anyone “People who are not interested in people, are the most interesting people
searchIndex.text: in Berlin. He ate German food. He saw the Brandenberg Gate. And yet on his return to Cambodia, he had little to say about his trip. How was the food? OK. How was the sightseeing, the culture? Nothing special. How was Germany? Not too bad, I guess. When pressed about his experiences, he said that people are basically the same everywhere. Same old, same old. You might think that this means that Phally is not interested in the world, or at the very least, not interested in travel, but nothing could be further from the truth. He loves roaming the world but he is uninterested in the world . He is interested in providing sustainable solutions to the world. Not for the profits or the prestige or the power . Just because people need these solutions. Who needs these ecosolutions? People who Phally and the team love…. but are not at all interested in. Are you interested in people enough to customize yourself and your ideas to try to please others? Phally is not interested in people. Not at all. To tell the truth, he is not very good at remembering names and even faces. At a recent business party, he introduced himself to a stranger. 227 The “stranger” pointed out that this was not the first time that they had met. In fact, he had known Phally for more than 10 years. Each time they met , Phally had acted as if they were meeting for the first time. Phally freely admitted to that “stranger” that he might not recognize him the next time, either. That might seem distant and cold to you but actually such an understanding is not quite right. Phally loves people and cares about people but he is not interested in them . But, what does this mean in practice? Think about it like this, if you will: VP.Start wants to provide services and solutions that genuinely help people. Therefore, it is anathema to their corporate ethos to try to use marketing to sell someone something that they don’t really need. If the VP.Start team explains the advantages of their solutions but for whatever reason, they don’t resonate with the potential customer or the customer sees no need to implement these solutions, VP.Start is more than happy to let them walk away. No high pressure sales. Ever. In that sense, they definitely care about people and care about making better outcomes for people, even if that outcome is to decide not to become a customer. In other words, as Phally likes to put it, “We love people but we don’t care about people and what they want.” What that also means is that VP.Start is unwilling to customize its products and services 228

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Ideology Love Everyone But Don’t Care About Anyone “People who are not interested in people, are the most interesting people
searchIndex.text: to make customers happy and satisfied because in the words of Steve Jobs, often quoted by Phally, “ the customer doesn’t know what they want until we tell them. ” VP.Start offers their solutions. Customers can choose to take them or leave them . Implement them or reject them . Either one is fine to VP.Start. What the customer cannot do is change them. Do you have principles and perspectives and rules that you will not change, no matter what the customer might tell you that they want? Do you think that it is wise business practice to have some unchangeable guidelines? This may well seem to be an arrogant, cocky, overconfident attitude. Perhaps, to some extent, it is exactly that. But let’s say that you go to the doctor when you don’t feel well. You ask the doctor for his solutions and remedies to your ailments. Do you try to customize or modify the medicine that the doctor gives you? Do you dispute the diagnosis or treatment plan? Do you decide to take the doctor’s advice that you like and ignore the part that you don’t care for? That is not what you do if you are wise. So, does that mean that doctors are arrogant? No. Doctors want to help us based on their advanced knowledge, skills and experience. Knowledge, skills and experience that we patients do not have. Of course, we can choose to walk away and ignore the doctor’s suggestions. Conversely, we can also, needless to say, choose to follow the doctor’s advice. 229 But what we cannot do is try to make the doctor change her or his advice to meet our needs or requests. We cannot write our own prescriptions. A wise doctor would never allow that. Take it or leave it but don’t try to change it. In a similar way, all are welcome to accept or reject VP.Start’s solutions, implement them or ignore them, but you do not have the option of changing them . On this point, VP.Start is adamant . Does it matter to you who your customer is? Should it matter? Would you be more likely to customise and alter your ideas for a rich, powerful, well-connected potential customer? Furthermore, in that sense, to VP.Start, it really makes no difference who you are. You may be an important government official, a well-respected professor or academician, a wealthy business tycoon or mogul or an influential overseas investor or just an average consumer or individual customer. For VP.Start, your position, title, influence, power and wealth matter not at all. VP.Start changes its vision for no one. In a positive sense, this means that VP.Start respects everyone equally. So, clearly VP.Start does not “care” about people, in the usual meaning of the word. This may seem like a strange business model but actually, it seems to work. Why? Because VP.Start may not care about people, but they definitely love people. 230

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Ideology Love Everyone But Don’t Care About Anyone “People who are not interested in people, are the most interesting people
searchIndex.text: And people seem to recognize that, at the deepest level . VP.Start may not be even remotely interested in people and what they think they want, but they are deeply interested in making their world a better place to live in through the power of innovation and data-driven technology. Do you care what others think about you? Do you build your self-worth on the positive or negative evaluations of others? Add to the SIMA ideology one more ingredient: CEO Phally does not care if you love him or hate him . He has experienced long-time teammates and supporters who told him how much they loved him, his ideas, his solutions and the entire SIMA Journey. A short time later, these erstwhile “lovers” were slandering VP.Start, stealing their proprietary secrets and codes, luring away other team members surreptitiously and spreading lies about the innovative solutions of VP.Start. Phally is not bitter. As we will see in the next chapter, people come and people go. Phally is not bitter but he is wiser than he was. He knows that you should never let praise get you too high or a discouraging word get you too low. In other words, love others, yes, but care about them and what they say, no, not in the least! Can a company go to the global stage, the world market, and succeed with this approach? That, of course, remains to be seen 231 but I suspect we will all know the answer to that question in fairly short order. Whether they win or lose with this approach, despite all odds, VP.Start has decided to go all in on this strategy, believing that in the long run, people want a company who loves them and makes products and services to express that “love” for the users, more than people want a company that caters to their whims and temporary wishes. Let me ask you a question, dear reader, How much do you care what others think about you and your innovations? Are you willing or unwilling to customize those innovative solutions to make them more profitable in the short term? Or, do you imbibe the VP.Start ideology, if you will, and refuse to customize your ideas, your products and yourselves? Make your choice and test your theory. Let’s see what happens a few years down the road! 232

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Ideology People Come and People Go “As people come and go, appreciate the role that they play in your story
searchIndex.text: Chapter 9 The SIMA Ideology People Come and People Go “As people come and go, appreciate the role that they play in your story. Each one contributes a chapter to your life.” -Author unknown At VP.Start, we are always talking about the SIMA Journey . Not the SIMA Project. Not the SIMA Strategy. Not the SIMA Plan. The word “Journey” is very important. What does the word “journey” indicate? A journey is a long-term development over time. A journey is sometimes arduous and includes overcoming obstacles along the way. A journey is full of surprises and adventure, the unexpected. And…. A journey is a movement that people can join or leave at any time. Have you found your journey yet? People come and people go. This is true both inside VP.Start and among the supporters of VP.Start externally, as well. Some people come for a season and leave amicably when times change. Others leave in anger or disappointment when the journey goes in a way that they do not agree with or approve of. 233 Ronald Wayne was the least known member of the trio that started Apple, along with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak. But he was not insignificant. Mr. Wayne created the Apple logo and wrote the first partnership agreement. He provided the very first funding to support Apple. He had a 10% equity stake in the corporation. But he decided to leave Apple after only 12 days because he was worried that Jobs was accumulating too much debt. He didn’t like the f inancial direction of the journey so he left. His 10% stake would be worth 100s of billions of US dollars currently if he had stayed with the company. Instead he sold the 10% share back to Apple for $800 . What will you do when the company vision and journey start to differ from your own personal perspective? Jef Raskin was the 31 st employee of Apple and he founded the Macintosh (Mac) Computer division at Apple, which ultimately became the most powerful and most profitable division. He was widely considered to be a brilliant computer programmer and designer. His radical dream was to build “an affordable all-in-one computer” for ordinary consumers. (At this time, personal computers were rare. Most computers were used by large businesses and educational institutions.) Unfortunately, Jobs and Raskin had radically different visions for the Mac computer, with Jobs wanting a sophisticated and more expensive mouse-based interface but Raskin pushing for a simpler, cheaper text-based keyboard interface. When the management team sided with Jobs and his approaches, Raskin left in anger. 234

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Ideology People Come and People Go “As people come and go, appreciate the role that they play in your story
searchIndex.text: When you are overruled and your ideas disregarded, how do you handle the rejection? One more. Steve Wozniak, the co-founder of Apple, designed the Apple 1 and Apple 2 computers which were in the early days, by far, the most popular products made by Apple. However, Jobs convinced the management of Apple to decrease funding for the Apple computer division and to increase funding for the newly founded Mac computer division. Jobs also mobilized a massive marketing campaign that completely excluded the Apple computer division. Frustrated, Wozniak soon left Apple to start a new company, CL9, which developed the first programmable remote control. When your journey is blocked, do you start a new one? When your dreams are not fulfilled, do you give up or try again elsewhere? Three different powerful members of the Apple Journey. Three different problems but the same final outcome. One was worried about finances and left of his own accord. Another left in bitterness when his plans and goals were overruled. The last one left when his innovations were gradually surpassed by other products in the company, neither bitter nor completely happy, but ready to follow his own journey as it separated from the Apple Journey. I mention these three Apple employees because they serve as a template for what has happened in the SIMA Journey as well. And every other innovative journey in history, I suspect. 235 There were those who left VP.Start and the SIMA Journey because they grew concerned about the radical, revolutionary approaches of VP.Start. Unconventional business practices. Low pressure sales. Limited efforts to build governmental contacts. Marketing by word of mouth, voice and powerful example. Refusal to leverage influencers and popular culture figures. Hiring people based on passion more than skills. An insistence on going to the global stage that some found premature. Conversely, some team members and outside supporters left because they felt that they could do a better job managing and marketing the technologies that VP.Start had created. As mentioned before in the Story section, some left in anger with the goal of establishing their own company based on the internal information that they took with them from VP.Start. Others chose to leave the SIMA Journey because they felt uncomfortable with the direction that the journey was taking. For example, some investors and consultants told CEO Phally to tone down his big picture thinking, reduce his requests for funding, build a local company with only very limited international aspirations and focus more resources on traditional marketing strategies. They urged him to stop talking about “world-class” and “earth shattering” and “game changing” soultions. They were concerned that the global market was not ready to accept a Cambodian tech company that dared to call its campus, the “Sen Sok Valley Campus” 236

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Ideology People Come and People Go “As people come and go, appreciate the role that they play in your story
searchIndex.text: as a rival to Silicon Valley and dared to call its new annex, a “Global Innovation Hub”. They wanted a quieter, more modest, more local, more incrementally growing journey. Not at all surprisingly, CEO Phally and the management team refused. If anything, the VP.Start team wanted to go faster, bigger, bolder, crazier, more disruptive, not less. If some people doubted Cambodian tech potential, that was their mistake, not the mistake of the VP.Start team. They knew what they could do and what they had already accomplished. These “take it slow” consultants also departed the journey. What do you do when “consultants” doubt your ideas, your plans, your abilities? How do you avoid discouragement? But as people left, more and more came , as well. During a very recent job hiring campaign to fill 5 positions, for example, VP.Start got more than 300 applications, some of them, for the first time, from outside of Cambodia, as well. Universities are lining up to sign MoUs with VP.Start because they want mentorships, training and research opportunities for their students. They want access to the SIMA Journey. Government ministers and official delegations like ones from the Cambodian Senate began to arrive at VP.Start more and more regularly , even though VP.Start never went out of its way to cultivate these contacts. 237 Business forums started seeking and inviting CEO Phally as a main speaker. Business leaders, government leaders, education leaders and leading students all wanted to participate in the SIMA Journey.. People come and people go. Simple. Not a very amazing observation. Rather obvious. But, the SIMA Ideology interprets this obvious situation in a counter intuitive way. Of course, when new people join the SIMA Journey, it makes the journey faster, stronger, wiser. And yet, when people leave the Journey, talented, qualified, amazing people depart, this makes the SIMA Journey even stronger . As a matter of fact, people leaving the Journey is often more empowering than people joining the Journey. Why? It likely sounds crazy that losing talented people and their experience, expertise and skills, knowledge and abilities, can be a plus, a positive. But you have to remember that for the SIMA Journey, the most important attribute required is passion. Team members who lack this passion are toxic. Not because they are malicious actors or nefarious workers, 238

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Ideology People Come and People Go “As people come and go, appreciate the role that they play in your story
searchIndex.text: but because a lack of passion can spread to others , like a disease. What is needed is passion! Not outstanding skills and talents. These can be learned. Not incredible experience and expertise. These can be acquired over time. Not vast, encyclopedic knowledge of technology. It will become obsolete tomorrow. You must have passion for the vision. You must have dedication to the SIMA Journey. Otherwise, you MUST go. Are you full of passion, addicted to your journey? If not, it is probably because you have not found your true journey yet. If you lack passionate love for the vision, you must go. Not because the VP.Start team hates you. Not at all. Because everyone has the right to find their own journey . If the SIMA Journey of VP.Start is not your journey, go find your own journey. No hard feelings. Warm wishes for your success. To reach a brighter tomorrow, we need many people on many journeys. If other journeys succeed and bring us closer to the sustainable world, this is a cause for celebration, even though this success may have come outside of the SIMA Journey framework. There is an engineer at VP.Start. 239 Let’s call him Dara. Dara is very dedicated and very talented. I recently had a chance to hear him speak on the power of IoT to change the future. Very passionate. Very lucid. Very detailed and knowledgeable. A year or so before, I was informed that Dara almost left VP.Start. Some of the “slanderers” who had left VP.Start a year or so prior tried to recruit him to join their company. Dara seriously considered the opportunity to take on a higher position in their organization, to promote his ideals with them, to follow a different journey. Conflicted and confused, he met with CEO Phally in private and expressed his thoughts. Since Dara was and is undoubtedly an important member of the VP.Start team with superior skills and advanced knowledge, you might expect that CEO Phally would try to convince him to stay. Phally did not. He said that Dara was welcome to stay if he felt like dedicating himself to the SIMA Journey. If he felt a different calling and a different journey, he could leave at any time with Phally’s blessing. If Dara wanted to start his own company and pursue his own journey in that way, Phally would do what he could to support that new journey. This was not at all what Dara was expecting to hear. 240

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Ideology: Celebrate your milestones……briefly “Remember to celebrate milestones as you prepare for the road ahead
searchIndex.text: Dara took some time to consider what journey he really wanted to pursue. A good salary. A higher position. A new company. New responsibilities. Ultimately he rejected those and decided that his journey was the SIMA Journey of VP.Start and he rededicated himself to remaining with the company and moving forwards toward the destination. But I can say with absolute confidence, that CEO Phally and the VP.Start would have proudly supported him whether he had stayed or had decided to started a new journey. In the end, no one stays together forever. Sometimes the paths split and the journeys separate. Other times, age becomes a factor that cannot be ignored. For whatever reason, impermanence is inevitable and unavoidable. The SIMA Journey continues even though at some point, we no longer are able to. Instead of feeling sad, looking at impermanence, we can choose to embrace it. Welcome it. Celebrate it. Long after we are long gone, the journey will go on and on. There is no greater joy than finding your journey, your calling. If you don’t feel that joy, may I suggest that you need to keep looking? When you find that journey, hold on tight and never let go! 241 Chapter 10 The SIMA Ideology: Celebrate your milestones……briefly “Remember to celebrate milestones as you prepare for the road ahead.” -Nelson Mandela Mr. Mandela captures the SIMA Ideology exactly in this quote. It is important to celebrate milestones and successes WHILE we are preparing for the next challenge. We never overlook the milestone but we also never stop preparing for the road ahead . Overlooking the milestones makes work a drudgery. Stopping preparations for the road ahead sets us up for failure. The celebrations and memorials give us energy and encouragement. But we can never focus on our milestones for very long. We overcome one obstacle in order to get to the next one. And the next one is usually bigger than the previous one. How do you feel about your work? Do you enjoy it? Or do you survive it? In your opinion, are our feelings important to our success and perseverance? Our resilience? How do we achieve the proper balance of remembering the past and preparing for the future? As you saw in the Story Section of this book, VP.Start has reached a number of major milestones. The first customers, the first breaking even, 242

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Ideology: Celebrate your milestones……briefly “Remember to celebrate milestones as you prepare for the road ahead
searchIndex.text: the first turning a profit, the first international visitors, the first pitching conference, the first contract with the EDC, the first university MoU, the new SIMA Journey Annex, selection for ASEAN meeting, selection as keynote company for Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Day, selection by EuroCham as speaker on the sustainable EV future, selection by GGGI (Global Green Growth Institute) as a grant recipient, selection for the smart grid modernization pilot project in Laos. The list of milestones could go on forever and we would still surely leave out a few of the milestones along the way. The point is not to boast of our achievements. The point is to recognize the importance of valuing each step on the SIMA Journey. The SIMA Journey, like any journey, is about the travel as much as the destination. But one other thing that CEO Phally promotes actively and unflinchingly is staying in the moment. Actually, failure to stay in the now means failure to continue making progress. Let me explain why. In a recent and fairly typical week for the CEO and management team, CEO Phally hosted a major conference on cybersecurity, held a strategy session with the management, researched funding and grant options for the pilot project in Laos, met visitors from the EDC including the Managing Director, 243 visited the offices of the ASEAN Secretary General for a meeting and pitching, organized training session for the newly established international liaison team, and then he was down to the airport for a two-day business trip to Laos to meet the management of the EDL (the utility of Lao PDR). After each event, of course, Phally takes a few moments to reflect , decompress and internalize any lessons learned. But then, quickly, it is time to move on to the next topic, meeting, event, conference. Spending too much time dwelling on failures or rejoicing over successes could be fatal to the the next project. Do you take the time to learn lessons, reflect and enjoy the moment? Do you do this quickly and promptly and move on rapidly to the next stage? If you wait for tomorrow, remember that, it is “always a day away.” That might sound hectic … and it definitely is. And yet, that is not the whole picture, by any means. If it were, VP.Start might be an intense, stressful, pressure packed workplace. And like all workplaces, at times, it certainly is. Deadlines to meet. Obstacles to overcome. Projects to complete. Products to produce and innovations to innovate. All in a timely fashion. 244

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Ideology: Celebrate your milestones……briefly “Remember to celebrate milestones as you prepare for the road ahead
searchIndex.text: Yet, if you visit VP.Start on a typical work day, you will almost certainly notice two things. Smiles. Plenty of smiles. And laughter. Genuine laughter. Lots and lots of laughter. VP.Start is a fun place to work. There is a corporate culture of joy that is hard to create and harder to maintain, but VP.Start has fostered and cultivated that atmosphere. How can a frequently busy, occasionally stressful, often challenging job also be usually fun and always enjoyable? It doesn’t happen by accident or coincidence. Creating a fun atmosphere requires conscientious effort. It is hard work to have fun , perhaps. Work hard. Play hard. Live hard. How do you do the hard work required to develop your ideas and build your innovations WHILE enjoying the journey with plenty of smiles and laughter? I saw one example that was very telling on a company trip to Siem Reap and Angkor Wat to celebrate 12 years of successful business operations. In the evening, the entire team went out to enjoy themselves in Siem Reap. Usually Phally does not take part in such activities. Not at all. It seems frivolous to him and he has little time for “playing” that does not advance the SIMA Journey. However he confided to me that he thought that it was mission critical for him to celebrate with the team on this particular evening even though that wasn’t really inside his comfort zone. 245 With intentionality. Drinking, singing, dancing, joking…. laughing . For CEO Phally, this was a sacrifice, a struggle, but he realized the value and significance of celebrating milestones , briefly but intensely. Taking a step forward. A stepping stone on the SIMA Journey. Are you ready to celebrate milestones “briefly but intensely”? If the celebration is too long, momentum can be lost. If the celebration is not intense, the purpose may not be met. We will talk later about the meditation and mindfulness training that VP.Start incorporates into its SIMA Methodology. At this point, let’s just say that meditation requires relaxation. True relaxation requires trust in your team members. To build that trust, in the mindfulness training, there were several games to build team work and cohesiveness . Silly games. Crazy games. After some team members managed to overcome their initial shyness, they were acting, jumping, running, moving, dancing, performing…. laughing. Of course, it is not always peace and harmony in a company. Not even in a happy company. Not all the time. There are disagreements and disputes. Occasionally, an idea must be rejected and 246

searchIndex.title: Chapter 10 The SIMA Ideology: Celebrate your milestones……briefly “Remember to celebrate milestones as you prepare for the road ahead
searchIndex.text: the originator of that idea is unlikely to be pleased. Bad news must be delivered . Criticism must be delivered . Faults must be pointed out . Failures must be pointed out. Inadequacies must be reprimanded. Laziness must be reprimanded. However, CEO Phally constantly maintains an attitude of humor that is infectious. He lightens the mood and breaks the tension. Humor spreads throughout the company as team members feel greenlighted to share their humorous sides as well. When you feel frustrated and unappreciated, when you face issues with your colleagues and coworkers, when they fail to understand and value your ideas and innovations, how do you maintain a positive attitude? How do you bring laughter into the picture for healing and growth? According to the Bible, “laughter and a happy heart are good like a medicine.” Whatever your religious perspective, I think you should be able to appreciate these words. Laughter brings us back to our original point: celebrate milestones, briefly. Briefly but intensely. Briefly but vibrantly. Briefly but with plenty of laughter. Briefly but with a big smile. Life is too short to ignore successes and milestones. 247 Please don’t forget. If we don’t enjoy today, we may not have tomorrow to enjoy. A wise company and a wise corporate culture finds the proper balance between staying in the present, remembering the past and focusing on the future. A corporate culture that takes the job seriously without the team taking themselves too seriously. Yes, of course, Dedication and commitment and sacrif ice and industriousness and proactivity. Covered with laughter and joy and love. A true innovator must find the balance between three competing desires. The desire to remember and honor the past. The desire to to focus and prepare for the future. The desire to stay in the present and live in the now. How do you intend to achieve the balance of these three contrasting factors? 248

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo.” -Albert Einstein “ What is the saddest story? ” Occasionally when the mood hits Phally, he likes to pose challenging questions to his audience. How would you answer, dear reader? “Is it the man with no ideas, no dreams, no vision, no innovation, nothing to drive him forward?” This is certainly a problematic situation, but it is not difficult to overcome. Learn to be yourself and those ideas, dreams and visions will come to you. That is the way of nature and no one can hold it back. Phally continues, “There is something much sadder than that . Try again.” “Is it the person with greatly imaginative and innovative ideas But no practical way to put these ideas to use?” Innovation, if it is true innovation, always finds a way to be useful and consequential. The most seemingly impractical innovations will eventually find their place in transforming our world and making it a better place to live. 249 Ridiculously fanciful flying machines eventually led to air travel and even space travel. “Well then,” Phally continues to challenge his audience, “how about the man who has great innovations, amazing vision, grandiose dreams to change the world but fails to bring these ideas to reality? This must be the saddest situation , right?” But no, this too could be rectified . Indeed, this situation happened and still happens all the time but it could be solved at a moment’s notice. “I suppose I could even live with unfulfilled dreams if people understood my dreams and chose to reject them for some valid or not so valid reason. I would be sorely disappointed but I would know that I had been true to myself.” “In that case, would the saddest story be that of the man who was unable to be true to himself, who lived in constant fear of what others would say and therefore customized himself to fit their expectations, losing his dreams and himself in the process?” This was the silver medal answer but it came up just a bit short of the gold medal . “I would say that the saddest man by far is: the man who has powerful vision, innovative dreams, creative thinking, 250

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: the man who refuses to be molded and modeled by society, the man who has ideas destined to change the world, the man who remains steadfastly true to the greatest version of himself, the man who has a visionary solution, both valid and worthy, BUT… the man who lacks a compelling voice to get his message out to the world. We talk a lot about Voice in this book. Having a Voice. Raising your Voice. Being a Voice. In the SIMA Journey, in your journey, there is probably nothing more critical than Voice . Many great ideas throughout history have been lost or tragically delayed because there was no one with a powerful and persuasive voice to bring that idea to the world.” The last statement, while perhaps not empirically verifiable, remains at the core of Phally’s view of the world and history. According to CEO Phally, Innovation has never been the exception ; it was and is the default mode for humanity. People are innovators by definition because innovation is the natural order of things and people are also a part of that order. 251 And yet, innovation has consistently lagged behind the progress that should have already been made long ago. Why? Because while people might be naturally-born innovators , they are definitely not naturally-born orators . In other words, For every 10,000 ground-breaking innovations happening every day, innovations custom-made to turn the world upside down, there might be but 1 or 2 persuasive speakers able to bring just a few of these ideas into fruition in the real world. The problem is not a lack of outstanding thinkers, but a lack of effective speakers. VP.Start’s motto is “Innovation through Technology” and what this means is that, innovation when it is not coupled with technology is mere daydreaming and science fiction. Technology is the logical methodology that brings creativity and innovative thinking out of the world of dreams and into our world. However, technology cannot move forward without a persuasive voice. What good is the greatest innovative technologies created by mankind if there is no voice to make them become known to mankind? Put differently, some ideas die because they lack the rigorous thought required to round them out into complete solutions. Other ideas die because they lack a realistic and cost-effective technological strategy to bring them to fruition. 252

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: But both of these predicaments can be overcome with additional time and effort. Overwhelmingly, ideas die, not because they are not plausible or logical or doable; they die because the person or group who hatched the idea lacked the mesmerizing voice needed to get that idea off the ground. The ideas and innovations die due to neglect , remaining dormant until someone else comes along to revive the idea, Someone who could provide the requisite powerful voice. Some innovative ideas, in Phally’s estimation, have died many a death already like Shakespeare’s cowards who “ die many times before their deaths. ” Some of these long deceased innovative ideas were still awaiting a voice that could revive them once more. Phally was determined that, yes, his innovative ideas could certainly die if they were unwise or impractical or unrealistic or financially nonviable. Phally could accept all those “deaths” as part and parcel of the “Fail fast, fail often, fail safely” mantra . However, on the contrary, Phally could not permit and would not allow, an idea of his to die because there was no world-class communicator to make sure that that idea did not. That was unacceptable. To Phally. 253 To nature. To the universe. When you have an amazing idea, how do you make sure that you have the voice to keep that idea alive? To keep innovation going and keep creativity alive , there must be a world-class communicator, a persuasive and mesmerizing voice, a powerful, positive and very unique voice. And at the end of the day, for VP.Start, that voice must come from the CEO and Founder . This is not about pride or arrogance, selfishness or a desire to take away the opportunity from anyone else to raise their voice. Of course, needless to say, every member of the VP.Start team and the greater VP.Start family of supporters and stakeholders, needs to have a powerful voice and possess a compelling message. Nonetheless, great ideas throughout history have been raised up by those unique voices that stood alone. Their ideas. Their voices. Their transformation. Do you dare to raise your voice? How dare you stay silent? For instance, when Einstein developed the theory of relativity, there were a number of scientists who did not go along with the theory. They even published a book critical of Einstein, 254

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: the infamous “100 Authors Against Einstein,” to dispute his theory of General Relativity. Einstein famously retorted, “ Why one hundred? If I were wrong, one would have been enough!” In other words a powerful and innovative idea raised up by a compelling voice can not be drowned out by 100s of critics whose voices lack the same credible authority. So, if communication is the key, how do you become a world-class communicator? If someone must have a persuasive, powerful, compelling, riveting voice, if this is the ultimate key to success , if this is the difference between life and death for innovation. how do you go about developing one? It is unlikely to be an easy goal to achieve. This question, became and in some ways, still remains the questions that will define the success or failure of the VP.Start experiment, the SIMA Journey, going forward. As Phally worked through some of the challenges of developing a powerful voice and presence to go along with it, he came up with some ground rules: The Six Commandments of the World-Class Communicator 1) There can be no powerful voice without powerful content. 2) There can be no powerful voice without passion. 255 3) There can be no powerful voice in another language if you lack it in your own language. 4) There can be no powerful voice from someone who is poor in listening skills. 5) There can be no powerful voice without empathy. 6) There can be no powerful voice without practice outside the comfort zone. Rule 1: There can be no powerful voice without powerful content There are many who speak smoothly and fluidly, who have mastered advanced grammar structures and sophisticated vocabulary, who are well-experienced in public speaking and who nonetheless are definitely not world-class communicators. Many of them are not even above average communicators. So, what’s the problem? They lack world-class content. They speak endlessly but they don’t really have anything to say . Anything worth saying . If you don’t have anything to say that MUST be said, that could not NOT be said, how could you possibly have a powerful voice? They use the buzzwords of technology without really knowing what they are discussing. They use quotes and passages from books, AI selections and clever phrasing and public speaking techniques but in fact, they have nothing to say. You will never become a world-class communicator unless you have incredible content . 256

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: The difference between meaningful, powerful, explosive content and repetition of jargon and buzz phrases is clear within seconds of a presentation. As a matter of fact, sometimes, it is clear even before the presentation has started. Do you have something to say? If not, the world-class communicator chooses silence. There is a burden on every speaker to show that they have something to say AND something to listen to. They must demonstrate this in the first 15 seconds of their speech. If they begin with introductions and greetings and traditional practices, they will have lost the audience before they have even gotten started. But perhaps this is just as well, since they didn’t really have anything to say anyway. When you stand up to pitch or make a speech, everything about you should tell the world that you have something to say , something that they need to hear . Before you even start to open your mouth, you have already captivated your audience. World-class communication must rest on the foundation of world-class content . To be otherwise, is to attempt to deceive the audience. It will not succeed. But why try to deceive the audience anyway? How much better it is for you and the audience, if you can give them something they need and give it to them in a way that is fresh, exciting and captivating! How will you capture your audience before you even open your mouth? 257 How will you use those first 15 seconds to show the audience that they absolutely need to listen to you? Rule 2: There can be no powerful voice without passion The second rule springs logically from the first. It is not enough just to have world-class content to share with your audience. You must feel passionate about delivering that content to your audience. If you are not thrilled beyond words to have this chance to express your innovative solutions to the audience, how can you blame the audience, if they are similarly uninspired and unmoved ? Simply put, an audience naturally tends to take on the characteristics of the speaker. A bored, listless, unenthused speaker creates a similarly unexcited audience reaction. A nervous speaker causes the audience to feel uncomfortable and to lack confidence in what is being told them. But when a speaker is consumed with passion for the topic they are discussing, how can the audience resist getting pulled in? We all know that a small flame indeed can start a massive forest fire . But passion cannot be manufactured . You have it or you don’t. If you don’t feel passionate about what you are speaking about, stop speaking and sit down . Think about and figure out why you should care and why your audience should care about what you are presenting. When, and only when, you catch that spark of passion, stand up again and complete your speech . To tell the truth, innovation, true innovation, 258

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: naturally generates passion. If there is no passion, it probably means that what seems to be innovation is in fact, just optimization of a pre-existing idea . When you drill into the ground and strike the oil of innovation, there is no way to hold back the emotion. Phally would defy any true innovator to be less than deeply passionate about their innovations. How do you feel about your innovations and creative solutions? Are you deeply passionate “beyond words” about your innovative ideas? How do you intend to make sure that your audience feels your passion and shares it? Rule 3: There can be no powerful voice in another language if you lack it in your own language A funny thing about voice is that contrary to what you might think, in the SIMA ideology, a powerful voice has little to do with language skills or ability. If you have a powerful voice, you can learn to have a powerful voice in English or Chinese or whatever languages you choose. Effort is required, of course, but it is within the realm of the achievable IF you have a powerful voice in your own language. This might seem counter-intuitive. We are all native speakers of our own language. Of course, we should have a clear and powerful voice in our own languages . But surprisingly, this is not always or even often, the case. 259 Phally has often pointed out that many Cambodians speak Khmer ineffectively and are not able to explain difficult concepts concisely and clearly. Needless to say, this applies to speakers of all languages. The problem is obviously not grammar or vocabulary when dealing with our own languages. The problem is logic and content and passion , as noted above. We can’t speak well in any language if we have nothing to say or if we care nothing about what we do say or if we cannot organize our thoughts around clear themes in a rational and logical progression. This is where so many speakers fall apart. When Phally determined to become a world-class communicator, he was convinced that to speak on the global stage, he would need to be a powerful speaker in English . This is not about disrespect of the Khmer language or overestimating English. It is just the nature of communication in the world today, for better or worse. Khmer is not going to take one very far in international business. And yet, as you might expect from Phally by this point, his first step to becoming a great communicator in English was anything but conventional. The first step was to master communication in Khmer. If he couldn’t be the most powerful, logical and passionate Khmer speaker in the room, if he couldn’t take control of the meeting and 260

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: make himself heard in Khmer, what chance did he stand in English in a meeting room full of native speakers? He threw himself into public speaking opportunities in Khmer. He also started learning English at this point but he kept a solid focus on becoming a world-class communicator in the sadly less than world-class business language of Khmer. In the Khmer speaking world, he became known as an effective and enchanting communicator. In Phally’s ideology, once he was able to become a powerful communicator in his own language , transferring those skills to English or any other languages as needed would be relatively easy. Are you effective at presenting your ideas in your own language? Learning another language for business is a great skill to acquire, But make sure that you are persuasive in your own language first! Rule 4:There can be no powerful voice from someone who is poor in listening skills Who is the best speaker? Phally would insist that the best speaker is the best listener , just as the best writer would be the best reader. Speaking and writing are production skills based on listening and reading. In Phally’s terminology, listening (and reading) are forms of data acquisition whereas speaking and writing are data simulation and application . The greatest data simulation and application will necessarily occur only where the best data is acquired and stored. Where data acquisition is limited or faulty or improperly stored, only very limited and poor quality data application is possible. It is important to note what active listening does and 261 does not mean in the SIMA Ideology. It does not mean only listening to interesting, captivating world-class communicators. After all, we are listening to grow, not to imitate . Therefore, we need to listen to everyone. The great speaker. The mediocre speaker. The unmitigated disaster of a speaker as well. It is all data that we need to acquire. Often, we can learn more about how to become a great speaker from listening to a very poor one , even if we are just learning from their cautionary example. Answering the question: Why is this speaker average or below average? While considering the weak points of a speaker, another aspect of the SIMA Ideology is that we can learn something from virtually everyone . As the saying goes, “Even a broken clock is right twice a day.” Even a very poor speaker might just have a successful approach every now and then. Similarly, even the greatest speakers are likely to miss a beat on occasion. These are the moments that only the most active listeners are in a position to take advantage of. Interestingly, we should note that when listening closely to others and finding what aspects of their speaking works or fails to connect, we often notice that we are making those same mistakes . Listening to recordings of 100s of our own speeches are unlikely to reveal these errors, 262

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: whereas we can often pick them up from just one speech of someone else . Perhaps, we are too close to ourselves to see the forest for the trees, as it were. Sometimes stepping back and seeing others can suddenly make everything clear. Are you the active listener to others that you want others to be to you? If your speaking skills are not what you’d hope, why not try listening more? Rule 5: There can be no powerful voice without empathy Another part of active listening is empathy. We don’t listen to a speaker just to evaluate, to judge, to critique. We must genuinely want to know what the speaker really wants to say . Otherwise, it is pointless to listen, however actively we might. By the same token, we must have empathy for our audience and share with them what they want to hear , not just what we want to say. On the surface, this might sound like customizing ourselves to satisfy the audience but actually, it is understanding the audience deeply and crafting our message to touch their understanding. We do not need to change our message in its essence, nor do we need to modify what we have to say; but we do need to give a message that is meaningful to the audience. Without empathy, this is impossible . According to the SIMA Ideology, most speakers have great messages and meaningful innovations but they don’t take the time to know their audience in a profound way. Therefore, the audience cannot clearly pick up on 263 why the message should be important to them. The truly great speakers don’t necessarily have any greater ideas or content than the average speakers but they understand the audience so deeply that they are able to format their message in a way that is digestible to the listeners. That is the key to making a complicated topic seem simple . Richard Feynman, the amazing professor, had an uncanny ability to take some of the most complicated and arcane topics of physics and make them seem as obvious as pure common sense. How did he do that? Was it because he had such a deep mastery of the content? Yes, of course, this played a crucial role. But even more importantly, Professor Feynman had a deep understanding of his audience and what they could and could not assimilate. He was able to fine tune his speaking to the exact level and requirements of the audience . His famous four step model of emphatic speaking was as follows: 1) Choose a concept that you want to learn. 2) Explain the concept to a child or a lay person with no background in the subject. 3) Identify gaps in your explanation that were difficult for the listener to understand. 4) Refine the explanation further. This is world-class empathy and the SIMA Ideology adopts a very similar approach . This calibration is absolutely critical. If you oversimplify and “dumb down” your speech too much, you show disrespect to the audience and 264

searchIndex.title: Chapter 11 SIMA Ideology Public Speakers HAVE a Voice, World-class Communicators ARE a Voice “Be a voice, not an echo
searchIndex.text: you can also introduce misconceptions or outright errors into the speech. If you raise the level of complexity beyond that which the audience can handle, a common error of tech speakers, the audience will likely be impressed , but confused and leave no wiser than they entered the proceedings. We must have masterful balance . But the only way to achieve that kind of calibration is to deeply know your audience. Empathy. But remember, you as a speaker may have never encountered this particular audience before . As a matter of fact, this exact combination of people, this specific audience may have never existed before right now. Furthermore, within this audience, there may be a wide variety of levels of expertise , meaning that some audience members will need near novice-level explanations while other may be able to handle much more sophisticated content and examples. Preparation is critical, obviously, but a speaker may sometimes need to try to evaluate all these factors and respond appropriately “on the fly” at times. If it sounds like an impossible task, that’s because it is. But as we know, “Only the impossible tasks are worth doing!” Do you have a deep understanding of and care for your audience? Before an audience decides if they like your ideas, they will decide if they like you. What is your audience likely to decide? Rule 6: There can be no powerful voice without practice outside the comfort zone. 265 Going on directly from rule 5, in the SIMA Ideology, truly world-class communication can only happen when we step outside the comfort zone . A great example of this is a panel discussion, a common occurrence at VP.Start. It is simply impossible to anticipate all the questions that might be asked. Therefore, by definition, answers are impromptu, generated on the spot. Does this create the risk that something inappropriate or inaccurate might be given in response to an unanticipated query? Yes! Does this open the door to unscripted and overly emotional answers? Yes . In other words, stepping outside your comfort zone forces you to be authentic . If you are inauthentic, it will be visible from the moon. Another aspect of forcing yourself outside of your comfort zone is forcing yourself to speak on topics about which you are not supremely confident. For Phally, a speech about grid modernization or data-driven technology is right up his alley. A speech on government-academia-industry collaboration or on the advantages and drawbacks of launching an IPO are speeches getting into topics well outside his area of comfort and expertise. Therefore, rather than avoiding these topics or leaving them to others, Phally insists on attending conferences and joining meetings where he will be forced to give speeches about and 266

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
searchIndex.text: answer impromptu audience questions about these very subjects. At times, I am not sure if this is a display of genius or of self-torture, but one thing is certain; Phally and VP.Start are all in. They may ultimately succeed or they may fail but they will definitely not go down without a fight. Are you willing to talk about any subject, even those that are outside your comfort zone? Will you seek out and embrace opportunities to delve into these less familiar areas? Do you grant yourself the grace to make mistakes and perform poorly as a stepping stone to better results down the road? If you dare, you will not regret it 267 Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself. Let everyone see the real, imperfect, flawed, quirky, weird, beautiful, magical person that you are.” -Mandy Hale, author of “The Single Woman” The most essential point of the SIMA Ideology is deceptively simple. So simple that a child can do it. Easily. And yet, often quite difficult for an adult to achieve. Be yourself. Let me say that again, Be yourself. One more time, all together now, “BE YOURSELF!” As Oscar Wilde has reportedly and famously stated, “Be yourself; everyone else is taken.” In a way, this concept encapsulates the entire SIMA Ideology in one phrase. If you are yourself , you are on the SIMA Journey, your SIMA Journey. If you are not yourself, you are on someone’s else journey, a journey to dissatisfaction. Today I was playing with my nephew. 5 months old. He is himself. You can believe me on this point. When he wants to cry, he cries. When he wants to laugh, he laughs. He touches whatever he wants to touch, makes whatever sound he wants to make. He doesn’t care if you are the Prime Minister or his older sister. 268

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
searchIndex.text: If he wants to grab your nose, he will grab your nose. He is himself 100%. Are you 50% yourself ? 70% yourself ? 85% yourself ? If you are not 100% yourself, you are still not yourself AT ALL! Something happens as a baby becomes a primary school student, then a high school student, then maybe a university student, then a worker, an adult. Something sad happens. Most people stop being themselves. They start to worry about making a mistake. They start to get embarrassed and shy. They start to care deeply about what others thinks. They start to obey the rules, the rules of society, the rules of the school, the rules of the company, even unwritten rules that exist ONLY inside their minds. Am I saying that there should be no rules or that we should do whatever we want? No, of course not. But the SIMA Journey invites us to recapture some of that lost spirit of freedom , of daring and risking being myself, that attitude of rule breaking and chance taking . We live in the age of “so-called” AI, even though Phally would insist that true AI does not yet exist. 269 AI gives us tremendous opportunities, access to knowledge and logic that would have been impossible a few short years ago. Regrettably, along with all the advantages of AI, it brings a tremendous opportunity to stop being yourself . What do I mean? You can use AI to write reports, emails, essays, speeches, slide presentations and so on, as you all know well. Sometimes it is a great way to save time and reduce unnecessary effort . But it removes your creativity from the process, as well. AI can create a speech on, for example, digital twin technology, in minutes, with real-world examples, technical details and logic that we could not achieve in several hours of speech preparation. But that speech will lack creativity and positivity . It will lack the spark of originality. It will lack “you” . It may be a great speech, a meaningful speech but not really, your speech. A lot of people are worried about losing their jobs and being replaced by AI , needless to say. Please don’t get me wrong. I am not saying that we should not use AI for repetitive and menial tasks or when we are on a tight schedule. It can be a helpful tool for writing and speaking 270

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
searchIndex.text: but if we use AI exclsuively and ultimately lose our own creative voice , we have already been replaced by AI even if we still have our jobs. Are you leveraging the power of AI to be more effective and productive? Or is AI getting ready to replace you and are you helping AI in that process? Think about it like this. AI levels the field. You may be an expert in quantum mechanics with a PhD and years of experience. I know absolutely nothing about that field. But thanks to AI, I can formulate a speech on quantum mechanics just as accurate and in-depth and detailed as you can . So, how does an expert keep her or his competitive edge in an age when technology makes everyone an “instant expert?” You keep ahead of the curve as long as you bring your creativity, your positivity and yourself to the process. AI can never do that and AI-based “so-called” experts can never do that, either. Are you taking the necessary steps to stay ahead of the AI curve? Is your creativity making you indispensable or is your AI dependency making you dispensable? AI can take the pressure off workers and students. Again, obviously, at times, this is necessary and useful. But for most people to be truly successful, 271 they need to turn the pressure on, not take the pressure off. Are you reducing the pressure on yourself when you need to be increasing the volume? Recently, Phally gave a major speech on cybersecurity. By his own admission, this is not a favorite subject of his. The topic is technical and abstract, well outside of his comfort zone. Phally could have chosen to speak on another topic. He could have asked someone else to make the speech. No one would have criticized either decision. But he chose to give the speech himself on that topic. Outside the comfort zone. Putting the pressure on himself. Forcing himself to be himself. Forcing himself to face his weaknesses. Phally gives the example of a caterpillar. Crawling across the tree, eating leaves. Comfortable. Peaceful. And yet, the caterpillar has not reached his potential yet. One day, the caterpillar will enter a transformation, a period of metamorphosis. Violent, radical change. Absolute disruption. But at the end of the process, that caterpillar will fly in the sky as a butterfly. The pressure, the violent change, the radical revolutionary transformation, it is not comfortable and relaxing. At times, it may be disturbing and distasteful and displeasurable BUT you must go through it, if you WANT TO FLY. 272

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
searchIndex.text: Are you ready to go through the challenge, the discomfort and even the suffering, of radical transformation? Are you satisfied with crawling OR do you insist on flying? 273 274 272

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
searchIndex.text: “If you want to change the world, start with yourself.” -Mahatma Gandhi, Indian political and spiritual leader You have a story , a unique story, a story that belongs only to you and no one else in the world. You are the only you in history. Believe in your story, Understand your story, Accept your story, failures as well as success. You also have an ideology , your unique ideology, an ideology that no one else can copy because your ideology is in many ways a result of your unique story. Treasure your ideology, protect your ideology and follow your ideology without hesitation. By the same token, you have a methodology , a unique and distinct way to try to achieve your goals and plans, 279 your way to turn your dreams into reality. Like the old song, “You do it your way.” But quite unlike your story or your ideology, you can and should change your methodology based on results and data. If you try something and it works, keep going. If you try something and it does not work, feel free to change gears. The only caveat is that sometimes it takes time for a methodology to really work, So please be careful not to change your methodology too quickly. Give it time and space but if your methodology is simply not working, it must be changed. VP.Start has never changed its ideology and never will. VP.Start’s story is what it is and obviously, the past cannot be changed. On the other hand, VP.Start changes its methodology flexibly and frequently. As the saying goes, “Fail fast. Fail often. Fail safely.” Have you found the methodology that works for you to achieve the goals that you want to achieve? If not, are you looking for new strategies and methodologies? Either way, how do you determine if your methodology is working or not? 280

searchIndex.title: Chapter 12 SIMA Ideology Innovators Become Themselves “Just be yourself
Chapter 1 SIMA Methodology: Changing Plans on the Unchanging SIMA Journey “Innovation survives only when people believe in their ideas
searchIndex.text: Chapter 1 SIMA Methodology: Changing Plans on the Unchanging SIMA Journey “Innovation survives only when people believe in their ideas.” - Levo League, Carrer Networking Platform The management team was getting ready to welcome an important visitor. A first time visitor to the the Sen Sok Valley Campus. A dignitary. A diplomat. The Secretary General of ASEAN. He could only grant them a 30 minute visit. VP.Start was determined to make sure that the time was well spent. The management team thought about the dress code, the seat arrangements, the menu items, the proper way to address the distinguished visitor. Of course. Nothing wrong with politeness and respect. Decorum and diplomacy. However, Phally struck a slightly different note. Politeness, yes. Respect, of course. Protocol, certainly. Excessive humility, absolutely not. Do you believe in your innovations and value them above all else? 283 Do you respect your ideas and respect yourself enough to consistently defend your ideas? Whenever? Wherever? With whomsoever? Phally wanted to make sure that his team was crystal clear that they were not coming to the ASEAN Secretariat to plead for support or to beg for connections or to humbly request assistance. Innovators don’t plead. They lead. VP.Start had a simple message for ASEAN. They stated that they had solutions that could accelerate grid modernization and create a greener, more equitable and more reliable power system across the entire ASEAN region, in countries both large and small, countries heavily and sparsely populated, in countries of mountains and islands, in countries with calm weather and those with extreme weather events, In countries both affluent and impoverished. All the incredible diversity of the ASEAN region. VP.Start has plans that could benefit ASEAN in many areas that are challenging to ASEAN now, such as extending the grid into remote, rural areas, providing affordable electricity across the region, integrating energy systems more effectively between different countries when geopolitically possible, 284

searchIndex.title: Chapter 1 SIMA Methodology: Changing Plans on the Unchanging SIMA Journey “Innovation survives only when people believe in their ideas
searchIndex.text: advancing renewable integration, accelerating smart grid adoption and promoting regional energy independence. Above all, making the ASEAN region more holistically sustainable. Across all sectors. All countries. All challenges. Forging an ASEAN that is a bankable place for outside investment. Do your solutions and creative ideas align with felt and experienced needs in your target market? Do you have the persuasive voice and persuasive evidence to publicize your ideas persuasively ? But from the methodological perspective, even more importantly than showcasing all the advantages that VP.Start brought to the ASEAN table, VP.Start needed to show clearly that they would not customize their vision and their SIMA Journey. For anyone. Not for ASEAN. Not for the UN. Not for a Climate Fund. Not for SIlicon Valley. Not for anyone, anywhere, anytime, any place. The details, the strategy, the day-to-day plans, these were all open to negotiations, points to be hashed out in various meetings along the way. 285 On the other hand, the vision was not allowed to be changed. The Journey must always keep going to the same destination. Many powerful companies started by true innovators with incredibly creative solutions have gone astray when they decided to change their vision, to revise their journey and to alter their destination. They tried to please their customers or satisfy the regulators or keep up with the competitors or follow the trendsetters or reduce the intense pressure of being innovative. Whatever the reason, if an organization changes its vision, it will shift immediately from growth to maintenance. Innovation brings growth. Customization brings maintenance of the status quo. EVERY TIME. WITHOUT EXCEPTION. Are you seeking growth or seeking to maintain the status quo? Growth is not easy. Innovation is not easy. Are you up to the challenge? Let’s be honest. It is a lot easier to customize than to innovate. Innovation is not some crazy scientist walking around in circles until amazing ideas suddenly appear. 286

searchIndex.title: Chapter 1 SIMA Methodology: Changing Plans on the Unchanging SIMA Journey “Innovation survives only when people believe in their ideas
searchIndex.text: Innovation is hard work. It takes time. And, it takes boldness. Sometimes even the closest allies, the strongest supporters and the internal team, themselves, will start to doubt the Journey. This is human nature. At VP.Start, the methodology is very clear. If you FBR (feel, believe and remember) the SIMA Journey and if you believe wholeheartedly in the destination, you will be rewarded for your sacrifice. If you stop believing , you are welcome to leave at any time, no questions asked and no criticism leveled. After all, everyone has their own journey and if your personal journey ceases to align with the SIMA Journey , it would cruel and also pointless to try to make you stay.
