This is the methodology that informs all other SIMA methodologies. No compromise on the big picture. This is why VP.Start can welcome foreign dignitaries, international ambassadors, leaders of multinational organizations, top government officials, international utility directors, leaders in the education field, such as university presidents and a whole host of VIPs without feeling nervous or humble. 287 As Phally put it, “If Elon Musk walked on to the Sen Sok Valley Campus and offered VP.Start US$1T to change their vision, we would politely say, “No, thank you.” What would you do if you were offered a massive amount of money to alter or discard your idea? Would you “take the money and run?” On the other hand, if anyone has ideas on how to achieve the vision, accelerate the SIMA Journey and arrive at the destination more efficiently, those ideas are welcomed. Whether they come from a tech CEO , an online TED Talk , an intern or new recruit at VP.Start or a random statement by a tuk tuk driver or security guard, it doesn’t matter. Great ideas are great ideas wherever they come from. Interestingly, non-experts often have the best ideas because they are freed from all of the suppositions and assumptions that might slow down the so-called “tech experts”. They don’t enough to know that they don’t know enough. They are not afraid to say any idea, no matter how crazy. And every once in a while, the crazy idea is the one that provides the solution . As Confucius, the ancient Chinese philosopher said, “If I happen to be walking with two other men, they will both serve as my teacher. 288

searchIndex.title: Chapter 1 SIMA Methodology: Changing Plans on the Unchanging SIMA Journey “Innovation survives only when people believe in their ideas
searchIndex.text: I will learn from the good ideas and good character of one and I will learn from the bad ideas and weak character of the other.” Similarly, Phally makes a point of spending time with “ordinary” non-tech savvy people. He loves to listen to the lessons of the monks . He loves to spend time with children . Inspiration can come from anywhere if you have a vision set in stone. Innovators are always gaining new inspiration from a variety of locations and scenarios. Are you ALWAYS ready to learn, to grow and to find new ways to be inspired? One of the greatest challenges for any innovator is to clearly express the vision and the destination. It is not at all surprising that sometimes even the most senior members of the internal team seem to briefly lose the vision and wander off from the journey. Phally never criticizes his team in this situation. It is a normal development. Phally criticizes himself for not making the SIMA Journey clear enough. He rededicates himself to advancing the Journey, showing the direction, pointing to the destination and raising his voice powerfully. You have amazing innovations and powerful ideas. No doubt about that. But, are you expressing those ideas clearly, forcefully and persuasively? Do your friends, supporters and stakeholders occasionally “lose your vision”? 289 Often Phally spends time alone, at his home or at the pagoda or in nature, communing and communicating with himself. Making sure that he is still on the right track, still headed towards the destination. If others get off the track, he can help get then back to the right path. Conversely, if Phally gets off the track, the SIMA Journey will be lost. For an innovative founder and CEO, there is no greater challenge and no higher responsibility than keeping yourself on course. How do you make sure that you have not “lost” your own vision? How do you reconfirm that you are still headed on the right track to theright destination? The most powerful SIMA methodology is the simplest. Know the destination. Change the methodology as often as necessary but never, never, never change the destination. Are you clear about the journey and destination of your innovative ideas? Does your support team REALLY understand that journey and destination? Are you making sure that you are not deviating from your journey and destination? Are you changing the details while staying faithful to your journey and destination? 290

searchIndex.title: Chapter 2 The SIMA Methodology The Negative Sales Pitch “ Your customers don’t care about you
searchIndex.text: If you can answer YES to all of these questions, you will complete your journey and reach your destination . WITHOUT A DOUBT. Chapter 2 The SIMA Methodology The Negative Sales Pitch “ Your customers don’t care about you. They don’t care about your product or service. They care about themselves, their dreams, their goals.” -Steve Jobs A key part of any business methodology is sales and marketing. Pretty hard to dispute that perspective. So, what is the best way to pitch your idea, your product, your service, your company? You probably think that the best way to sell a product or pitch an idea is to bring up all the advantages that accrue from using the product. Not exactly an outside the box approach. Or perhaps, you think that best way to market a service or promote an idea is to understand your customers deeply, build a deep rapport, 291 tap into their wants and desires and give them solutions that meet their requests . This too is hardly an innovative strategy. You might think that the best way to publicize your products is to mention the potential problems that your product can help them overcome. Another reasonable, if ordinary plan. You might even consider resorting to testimonials from satisfied customers or famous celebrities. Been there, seen that. Many, many, many times. These are all common sense approaches to pitching that have been used successfully for a long, long time. They have statistics and a track record and clearly defined outcomes. And Phally rejects them all . What is your “go to” strategy of pitching when you really need to make a sale? As a matter of fact, Phally views pitching in the opposite way of most people. I suppose that is not surprising. He sees almost everything the opposite way of most people ! He does not see pitching as seeking customers, investors, collaborative partners, stakeholders. He sees pitching as providing an opportunity that only a few will be wise enough to take advantage of. No persuasion. No tactics. No sales strategies. The product had better sell itself because Phally sure isn’t going to sell it. 292

searchIndex.title: Chapter 2 The SIMA Methodology The Negative Sales Pitch “ Your customers don’t care about you
searchIndex.text: Do your ideas and innovations and creative solutions sell themselves? If they do not, why don’t they? It is audacious and bold. You might even say it is crazy. You would not be the first one to say so. Some have definitely called it “crazy”. They may well be right. But it is so counter intuitive and so creatively unexpected that it works. The sales figures for VP.Start keep growing year by year. And the traction is clear cut, towards further increasing and accelerating growth. Not bad for a company that “refuses” to sell its products or compromise on the VP.Start vision. Would you ever turn down a potential customer for any reason? What are you afraid of? In one recent meeting, some potential customers requested Smart IoT sensors for their factory. They wanted it modified their way according to their specifications. CEO Phally politely but firmly declined. Innovators do not compromise, do not customize, do not change for others. Why not? Because the moment you start changing your innovations to suit the preferences of the customers and not your own ideals, you cease to be an innovative company and become a product manufacturer, selling products and fighting competitors. VP.Start adamantly refuses to go down that road. 293 In another meeting, some bankers came with possible loan opportunities. Possible investment options. But they said that were some red flags slowing them down. They needed and demanded assets, collateral, balance statements, and the adoption of more conventional management strategies, more traditional sales and marketing, more incremental growth and more measured plans. CEO Phally said that he had no intention of changing any of those things. The bankers and investors said that they would be back later to discuss the situation further. CEO Phally made it clear that no return visit was needed and that they would not be welcomed again. He said that for VP.Start, banks that don’t see opportunities have the biggest red flags. They did not fathom the SIMA Journey so any investments or loans that they might provide, in the long run, would be a burden, not a blessing. Rather than recognizing the amazing opportunity they had to work with VP.Start, they valued their own regulatory frameworks and bank policies. Phally knew well that accepting money from banks so that they could gain major ROI was something that VP.Start could provide, but would not provide to “red flag” banking services. VP.Start wants customers and investors and partners that are in the SIMA Journey for the long haul. There is no point to short term collaborations. Limited partnerships. 294

searchIndex.title: Chapter 2 The SIMA Methodology The Negative Sales Pitch “ Your customers don’t care about you
searchIndex.text: They take too much time and effort . They provide too few positive outcomes . Better to spend more time to build long-lasting relationships with customers based on understanding and shared goals. Because, down the road, there will surely be times when things are not smooth. Short term investors and stakeholders will run away. Long term supporters , on the other hand, know the destination so they will stay the course. As Phally has frequently said, “If you cannot suffer a loss positively, you will never be able to turn a profit.” If you view each customer, each investor, each OEM, each stakeholder and supporter as a trusted partner, whether they provide a great amount of revenue or only a little, you will see soon that the goal is building relationships based on a mutual journey. How do you view your potential customers, investors, partners and supporters? Just as important, how do they think that you view them? For anyone who does not share the goals or see the value of the SIMA Journey, there is no need to become a customer or investor or collaborator. Not because VP.Start is angry. Not because CEO Phally is arrogant. Not because the investors are stupid or unwise. Not because the customers are insignificant and unworthy. But because there is too little time to spend it all on persuading the 295 uninterested. There is a revolution to achieve . There is a journey to continue . There is a world to change . Let those who see the goal clearly, join the journey. If you don’t see it clearly even after we make our pitch, there are no hard feelings, no ill will, but we simply don’t have time for you. Does it seem like a harsh attitude? I suppose it is in some ways. But I don’t think that the point of the “Negative Sales Pitch” is to belittle people or discourage them. Remember, the goal is so big and the time is so short . We welcome anyone who helps us accelerate our journey. On the other hand, without any malice or negative feelings, anyone who decelerates our journey MUST be avoided. Not because there is anything wrong with them BUT because our SIMA Journey is about changing the world. No time for delays, disruptions, distractions. Picture this. At a party held on the deck of a hotel swimming pool, someone drinks too much, slips and falls into the water. 296

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Methodology Smart Teamwork Comes from a SIMA Smart Team “Coming together is a beginning
searchIndex.text: They don’t know how to swim. They will soon be drowned if no one helps them. Do you stand on the edge of the pool and discuss why this person should have been more careful and drunk less? Do you have a negotiation about who should jump in and save the person? Do you host an impromptu conference with a panel discussion on water safety strategies? Do you schedule a meeting to determine the causes of this situation so it can be avoided in the future? I think not. I hope not. I think you will ignore everyone else and jump in the pool to save the person in danger. What if the world is in danger? What if our earth is unsustainable in its current form? What if the planet needs solutions to rescue it? VP.Start is a company that ignores all the bystanders and observers and jumps in to provide solutions for a better future for everyone. Our world is in danger. Will your innovations and solutions make the world a better place? If your answer is “NO” , are you dreams really worth pursuing? If your answer is “YES” , why are you hesitating? We need your innovative solutions NOW ! 297 Chapter 3 The SIMA Methodology Smart Teamwork Comes from a SIMA Smart Team “Coming together is a beginning. Keeping together is progress. Working together is success.” -Henry Ford, Inventor and CEO of Ford Motor Company There are no smart cities without smart citizens. There are no smart homes without smart homeowners. In the same way, there is no smart teamwork without a smart team . A SIMA Smart team. Put in a different way, Wise companies have an effective and well-planned out methodology. 298

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Methodology Smart Teamwork Comes from a SIMA Smart Team “Coming together is a beginning
searchIndex.text: Wiser companies implement that methodology effectively and consistently. The wisest companies implement that methodology with teamwork from a smart team. This is the SIMA Methodology level. At VP.Start, value is given to every member of the team. Not because this is a feel good strategy but Because every team member is essential. A company is only as strong as its weakest team member. On the other hand, a company with unbreakable teamwork is a strong company, indeed. As you promote your ideas and solutions, do you value every member of your team? Do you implement your methodology consistently, efficiently and with unflinching teamwork? In this chapter, we are going to change the format and break the rules a bit. After all, that is what revolutionary companies love to do. We are going to look at some interview results from randomly selected workers across VP.Start. From all departments. All rankings. All different years of experience and heterogeneous areas of expertise. Sokleap is working in the Accounting and Finance Department where she has worked for 9 months. She moved on from a previous job at a retailer where she worked in a similar capacity. She found her previous place of employment “messy” and her work unsatisfying. 299 A friend told her of VP.Start and she was excited to work for a Cambodian CEO. She was impressed by his ideas as well. On an average work day, Sokleap is involved in managing expenses, collecting fees and arranging financing and budgeting for frequent VP.Start business trips. In the future, she hopes reduce unnecessary steps in the work process, automate routine tasks where possible and eliminate or shrink paperwork, by promoting more software-based digital solutions In other words, only 9 months into her VP.Start career, she is already focused on improving the work environment and making innovative changes. This is a constant among all the team member that I interviewed. Are you ready to “hit the ground running” to move your ideas forward? Or are you intending to wait for that “better day” that will never come? Kim Chhean has been working in the Accounting and Finance Department for 5 years already. She first learned about VP.Start as a university when a professor mentioned the company as a rapidly developing tech firm with a Cambodian CEO. Both aspects appealed to her greatly. Her job focus is cost control and especially working with suppliers of the raw materials that VP.Start uses to create its amazingly innovative solutions. She also sees opportunities to increase automation, reduce paperwork and 300

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Methodology Smart Teamwork Comes from a SIMA Smart Team “Coming together is a beginning
searchIndex.text: streamline operations in her department through adoption of online techniques. Are you always looking for ways to streamline processes? Great ideas can be lost due to inefficient operational procedures. Bousong is in the Hardware Modeling Division where he has worked for three years. He initially learned about VP.Start through social media posts by the CEO and management team. He was interested in the solutions presented online and the big picture thinking as well. He felt that this company suited his skill set nicely. Currently, he is working in monitoring teamwork in his areas and helping his team accomplish their tasks when they have some issues. Talking with him briefly, it is clear how much he cares for his team and for the solutions. In the future, he would like to play a role in both technical and commercial growth of the company and he envisions himself possibly working in a management role. Like many of the young team members of VP.Start, he is both humble and ambitious. Do you have the right balance of humility and ambition? Do you envision a much brighter and bigger future for yourself ? Don’t expect to achieve anything that you cannot imagine and foresee! Panha works in the Production Department, as he has for five years already. Panha learned about VP.Start during a college visit to the campus. He works on quality control and product assembly and testing, 301 using circuit board testing to check on functionality of products. He works in a very time-sensitive part of the company, and faces a lot of pressure and deadlines. In the future, he sees himself working closely with OEM partners for inspections and he hopes to share his experiences with young members of the team. Are you excited to share your experiences with team members or do you see them as potential rivals? Are you able to handle stressful situations effectively? Phearun is a member of the R&D 2 Team as he has been for the past 4 years. He learned about VP.Start when he saw some social media posts about home automation products that he found attractive. He is currently working as a web developer, specifically as a front-end web designer and his goal for the future is to create a universal web platform that can be used by all team members across the company for greater communication and collaboration. Are you enthused to communicate and collaborate more effectively and efficiently? Are you building the framework to make such communication and collaboration possible? Kahnchana is in the R&D Team 1 with the Application and Design Team where she has worked for 8 months. She learned about VP.Start when she was doing some job hunting through LinkedIn. She was impressed with the hardware solutions of VP.Start and sent in a CV, not expecting to be selected. An ordinary for her includes designing mobile app configuration for some 302

searchIndex.title: Chapter 3 The SIMA Methodology Smart Teamwork Comes from a SIMA Smart Team “Coming together is a beginning
searchIndex.text: of the DRC solutions to increase their connectivity and ability to interface with hardware. Her goal is to become “more than she is now”, including reaching a senior grade in the company. Her pride in her work is obvious and undeniable. Are you looking to reach a higher “grade” with your innovative ideas? In addition to amazing ideas, do you have undeniably obvious pride in your work? Seng works in the Embedded System Design section as he has for the last 4 years. He mentioned that a large part of his skills were learned “on the job” as there weren’t at that time, many schools focused on these technical areas. Seng first learned about VP.Start from Facebook posts that explored the DRC series. He sent an online application to the HR and was surprised to be accepted. He is currently working on the internal programming of the DRC-010, gradually moving away from his earlier role as an IoT programmer. He pictures himself playing a role in the international development of VP.Start in the future. Often times, innovators shift roles over time and move into completely new areas. Are you ready to be flexible enough to make the change when the situation necessitates it? These interviews revealed several things that seemed consistent. Many team members, including quite new members, handled a variety of tasks. 303 But no one seemed unhappy or stressed about that. Many team members were attracted to VP.Start by social media posts or by the fact that the CEO is from Cambodia. I personally don’t see this as racism or nationalism but a desire to build up their own country. Many team members had transitioned over time from one role to a different one. Sometimes a very different one. Many team members, including younger ones, foresaw a future where they were helping to raise up a new generation, the new Angkorian generation perhaps, of young Cambodian tech professionals. Finally, one thing that they all shared was their love of the company work atmosphere. This atmosphere is, according to them, unique and at times, a little odd. But extremely friendly and familiar. Mistakes were quickly forgiven. Disputes are quickly forgotten and help is freely given. I wonder if I am too old to apply for a job there, haha! What is the atmosphere that you are creating for people who work on your innovative ideas with you? Please never take your team for granted. 304

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Methodology A Day in the Life of a SIMA Engineer “Engineers like to solve problems
searchIndex.text: Chapter 4 The SIMA Methodology A Day in the Life of a SIMA Engineer “Engineers like to solve problems. If there are no problems handily available, they will create their own problems.” -Scott Adams, Author and Cartoonist of “Dilbert” On a busy street, the street stalls and shops are lined up. A coffee stand. A fried noodle shop. A sImple roadside auto repair place. Shoes pilled on a tarp on the sidewalk. And a shop selling beverages from a cart of a motorcycle. A very ordinary scene on a very typical street in Phnom Pehn. Almost stereotypical. Behind the mobile drink “shop”, there is a thick, metal fence. Locked. Behind the fence, there is a small, yellow building, made up of cinder blocks, looking like an off-limits, discontinued public restroom. Unlock and open the doors to this shed, and you will suddenly see a huge medium voltage transformer, an array of electric lines, gears, connections, monitoring systems, grid infrastructure, power cords submerged in water, breakers and other aspects of a functioning substation. Hidden in plain sight. 305 There is an entire “world” of grid infrastructure , beneath the streets, or above our heads or behind this shop or that home. Forests of electricity poles connecting us all to electricity without us even noticing . The strange thing about the electric grid is that we all rely on it every day. But we rarely notice it . When we turn up the temperature of our AC, when we fire up our laptop, when we heat up some coffee, when we wash up with heated water, when we light up our house, we are grid users. But how often do you and I actually think about what is going on behind the scenes? If you are like most people and like me, to be honest, we usually don’t think about the grid EXCEPT when there is an outage . When the power is down and our frustration is up , we notice the power grid. We complain to our friends and family about the unreliable grid service, while day after day, we have been taking advantage of reliable electricity without much of a second thought. When people take advantage of your innovative ideas, do they notice you? Is it your goal for people to notice your solutions or enjoy your solutions without noticing? 306

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Methodology A Day in the Life of a SIMA Engineer “Engineers like to solve problems
searchIndex.text: At midnight, often in bad weather, on weekends, during Khmer New Year, engineers are always working , keeping the power flowing. As a matter of fact, the times that we enjoy the most, weddings, celebrations, festivals, are often the times when electrical engineers are working the hardest, making sure that our good times and happiness are not interrupted by power issues. Similar to the substation hidden behind the drink stand, engineers are often hidden, unseen. In fact, the best engineers are the ones that work so well that we never notice them . Think about a sports match, say a football game. Is it a good game if we notice the referee frequently and question their decisions? NO. The best football match is the one where we hardly notice that the referees were there at all. If you go to hear a speech, do you want to notice the translator? NO. In the best speeches, the translator works so effortlessly that we forget that they are translating. Do we want to notice the engineers and operators of the grid? NO. NOT AT ALL. 307 We want them to work so well and the grid to be so reliable and efficient that we forget that they are even there . This is the goal that VP.Start is striving for, the SIMA methodology that we are promoting. Are your solutions so effective and your operations so seamless that consumers often forget that they are using your product? How do you intend to attain that level of trustworthiness? Two VP.Start engineers park the company car on the narrow sidewalk. They slip behind the drink shop, unlock the gates and enter the substation. Sometimes for repairs, sometimes for monitoring, sometimes for upgrades, sometimes for installation of DRC equipment to manage grid data. If it is a simple installation, they might be in and out in 15 minutes or so . If it is a complicated repair operation, they might need to spend half a day in the crowded and humid conditions of the substation room. Some days, they are off to distant provinces, leaving early in the morning and spending most of the day on the road. Other days, they visit local Phnom Penh metropolitan substations, 308

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Methodology A Day in the Life of a SIMA Engineer “Engineers like to solve problems
searchIndex.text: often visiting a number of substations on the same day. Still, other times they are in conferences and communication, online or at the headquarters, with main operators, support staff from the EDC and other stakeholders coordinating their actions to increase efficiency and reduce unnecessary trips , which generate unnecessary carbon emissions. Are you promoting maximum efficiency in your solutions? Are you able to maintain your innovations successfully WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY reducing your carbon footprint? Safety is crucial, to state the blindingly obvious, whether working on a medium voltage transformer in a sweaty substation or at the top an electrical pole making adjustments or making repairs to an auto recloser beneath the burning midday sun . And yet, speed is also essential. These two are in continuous fluctuation, tension. How do we achieve maximum safety while maintaining maximum speed of operations? In some ways, a SIMA engineer is not particularly different from an electrical engineer for any company. And yet, at the deepest point, there is a fundamental difference. The engineers of the SIMA Journey are not just working for a paycheck, working for a living wage, not just maintaining the grid, 309 not just fixing problems and repairing equipment and monitoring operational performance. There is nothing wrong with any of those things, needless to point out. But, if that was all that motivated our engineers and technicians, they would be exactly the same as other engineers everywhere. What is the motivation that keeps your innovations moving forward? That keeps your dreams moving forward? That keeps you moving forward? The difference is the Big Picture. SIMA electrical engineers see the overarching view, they see long-term, they envision the future. They don’t maintain. They upgrade. They don’t repair. They solve problems before they happen. They don’t gather data only to know the current state of the grid. They gather data to garner actionable insights that they can apply for better decision making. They don’t forget tomorrow. They build tomorrow TODAY. Do your solutions and innovative ideas help you to envision the Big Picture? Do these innovative solutions do the same for user and customers of your ideas? Does the mindset of the engineer really matter? If they have skills, talents, experience and expertise, 310

searchIndex.title: Chapter 4 The SIMA Methodology A Day in the Life of a SIMA Engineer “Engineers like to solve problems
searchIndex.text: isn’t that enough? In the normal working world, YES. In the SIMA Methodology, NO. The SIMA Methodology is never just a plan or strategy. It is a way of thinking, a way of living, a way of creating the future. Think about it like this. A lot of people study English all over the world but very few achieve the level of English that they want to reach. Why? What is the problem? Are they lazy? Are they stupid? Are they unwilling to work hard? Usually no! The problem typically is that they don’t have clear enough goals for their English development. Yes, they want to speak English well. OK, But what does that mean? Order coffee in English? Chat about the weather or music in English? Run a business meeting in English? Pitch a product in English? Write a proposal for grant funding in compelling English? If you don’t have clear goals and you do not envision what success looks like, you will not achieve a satisfactory outcome. 311 On the other hand, the clearer your goals are, the easier it becomes to make a realistic plan to accomplish your objectives. Our SIMA engineers have a very powerful vision of the sustainable future that they are working to attain. While they may be working in a small substation on “ordinary” maintenance and monitoring tasks, they are able to see how these actions fit into the bigger, more enormous picture of a sustainable energy future MADE IN CAMBODIA and MADE FOR THE WORLD. As the astronaut, Neil Armstrong said when he stepped on the moon, “One small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.” Each small step that our engineers take day by day, in the heat and the rain, in the dark of the night, whenever and wherever and for whatever reason, they know that this is part of a giant leap for mankind. The revolution of transformation. The sustainable future. As you develop your innovative ideas, how clear are you about your goals? How certainly can you envision the Big Picture that you are striving to attain? Can you share that Big Picture with others effectively and concisely? 312

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Methodology Branding is Everything and Everything is Branding 313 Let’s take a closer look at branding, SIMA-style
searchIndex.text: “Products are made in a factory but brands are created in the mind.” -Walter Landor, pioneering brand designer and consultant Building a brand is hardly a unique methodology of VP.Start. Companies all over the world strive to build their brand, maintain their image and market their products. And yet, in the SIMA Journey, we take a radically innovative approach to brand building. After all…. How could a revolutionary company have a conventional brand? How could a radically transformative firm opt for traditional marketing practices? How could we burnish our image as innovators unless the image we create is innovative? What is your methodology of branding your ideas, your company and yourself ? According to data and reliable metrics, are your branding approaches succeeding? VP.Start follows the SIMA Branding Methodology and it causes us to reject some typical branding practices . At the same time, the SIMA Methodology leads VP.Start to adopt some unorthodox strategies . Chapter 5 The SIMA Methodology Branding is Everything and Everything is Branding 313 Let’s take a closer look at branding, SIMA-style. First, what are the brand building techniques that the SIMA Methodology avoids? One is relying on influencers and celebrities to promote their products. Influencers, podcasters and other online figures have expressed interest in promoting VP.Start and its solutions for payment, from time to time. The VP.Start answer is unequivocal and always the same. Thank you, but no thank you. We welcome word of mouth exposure but we will not pay for it. Don’t get the wrong idea. We are not opposed to podcasts per se. For instance, Phally has appeared on a CarCam podcast by a major influencer in the car racing community. Instead of the usual podcast, introducing the latest racecars and engines, the podcaster decided to dedicate an episode to the ecosolutions of VP.Start after a visit to the Sen Sok Valley Campus. Much appreciated exposure to a new audience. But there was no reciprocal arrangement and no financial reimbursement. After all, if you pay enough, you can get some influencers and celebrities to endorse or recommend almost anything . Needless to say, this is a common practice across a wide variety of industries and economic domains. 314

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Methodology Branding is Everything and Everything is Branding 313 Let’s take a closer look at branding, SIMA-style
searchIndex.text: But from the SIMA Methodology perspective, this is unethical . Companies that employ this strategy are trying to use the influence of influencers, the celebrity of celebrities and the fame of the famous to convince, persuade or coerce people into buying a product whether they really need it or not. This is not a customer-first methodology. For many companies, this is a popular and wise strategy. For VP.Start, it is completely unacceptable. Are you committed to branding ethically? Will you reject branding strategies that take advantage of the consumer? Do you realize that how you do branding is a major part of your branding? Another common practice is Search Engine Optimization for increased visibility. There are ethical and less ethical ways to do this. Ethical practices might include improving website architecture and posting updated information regularly online in various forums and formats. Less ethical practices might include misleading labeling and click baiting , using false or inaccurate tags in online content to promote access DESPITE the content , not because of it. Similarly, paying a search engine for better placement would fall into the somewhat unethical approach category from a SIMA standpoint. Are you determined to represent your ideas and content fairly and avoid misleading labeling that might draw more responses 315 but would do it in an unethical and inaccurate way? Do you want to be branded as “tricky” and “dirty” or “clean” and “honest”? VP.Start’s approach is much more organic, “word of mouth” marketing . Nowadays, fewer people trust what they see online and the influence of influencers is becoming diluted as well. On the other hand, the power of a recommendation from a trusted friend or colleague who has nothing to gain from recommending VP.Start’s solutions is at an absolute premium . Think about it. Are you more likely to drink coffee from a coffee shop that is recommended by a famous football player who has probably never been in the coffee shop and is definitely getting paid by the coffee shop to recommend the coffee shop ? Or are you more likely to listen to the recommendation of your co-worker who really loves coffee and recommends a coffee shop where he or she is a regular customer? While some will be swayed by the football player, surely, VP.Start puts its energy into the co-worker. VP.Start actually does not want you to be a customer if you are becoming a customer for the wrong reasons. 316

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Methodology Branding is Everything and Everything is Branding 313 Let’s take a closer look at branding, SIMA-style
searchIndex.text: Radical? Yes. Crazy? Maybe. Ethical? To a fault. If you are able to garner customers who misunderstand your products or who are influenced to buy your innovative solutions by celebrity promoters who have never used your product, will you embrace these customers or will your turn them away? Which do you value more, one sales or your long-term reputation? So, in a similar vein, VP.Start does not search out podcasts to appear on or forums to appear at or journals to appear in . As Phally puts it, “We don’t go to the world. The world comes to us.” This really does sound like a crazy strategy for an upcoming young company but incredibly, it seems to really work. The CEO is on podcasts and at forums FREQUENTLY even though he NEVER approaches them. Some of the biggest speeches to the biggest audiences were given at conferences where Phally was requested as the keynote speaker. Conferences and forums that VP.Start had never even heard of. Lucky? Good timing? Maybe occasionally but surely not time after time after time. Why does this happen? If you ask Phally, it is simple. 317 We tell our story. The product sells itself. We don’t tell what our product can do. We tell why we made the product . We don’t tell you why you need the product. We are not salespeople. We tell you who were are and what we believe because we are storytellers . People will pay a lot of money to go to see a good storyteller. Not many people will pay to see a salesperson, even a world-class one, I dare say! In terms of branding, have you decided to become a salesperson or a storyteller? For you personally, do you prefer meeting storytellers or salespeople? How do you think your potential customers and stakeholders feel about this choice? One strategy that is essential to the SIMA Branding Methodology is purpose-driven Brand Identity . We don’t just go beyond telling about the products that we sell; at times, we don’t bother to even mention what we sell at all. The customers have to ask us! And they do! We focus on our core values , mission and brand mindset. These are what attract loyal customers. Our brand’s identity. Our brand’s mindset. Our brand’s purpose. 318

searchIndex.title: Chapter 5 The SIMA Methodology Branding is Everything and Everything is Branding 313 Let’s take a closer look at branding, SIMA-style
searchIndex.text: And if these attributes don’t attract customers, we don’t think that it is time to change our strategy. Instead, we think that it is time to upgrade our voice to tell our story and our perspectives better. If that still fails, we probably didn’t want them as a customer anyway. No anger. No regret. Tell our truth and accept the outcome. Are you ready to tell your “truth”, upgrade your persuasion and storytelling but refuse to change your basic strategy, even if some customers walk away? Do you have enough confidence in your branding to let some sales opportunities slip by? In other words, “branding is everything because everything is branding.” Most observers would agree that the greatest branding success in tech and maybe in business, is Apple. People want to buy Apple products for many reasons but most of them come back to FBR (how the Apple brand makes them f eel, b elieve and r emember). Apple doesn’t spend a lot of time explaining its features and technology and internal workings to the general public. If they did, they would become just a good brand or a quality brand. Since they do NOT, they become an iconic brand , an unforgettable brand, 319 a “must have” brand. Branding can make or break a company . A reputation takes years and years to build but can be lost in an instant . In the SIMA Methodology, there is nothing more powerful than branding BUT true branding comes from who you really are and what you really believe and the people and ideas that you really value. Otherwise, branding is like a fake ID that people use to hide their true identity. That’s why “branding is everything” but even more importantly, “everything is branding.” Every action you take , every decision you make , every rule you break , every morning you wake , you are continuously branding. You are either building your branding or tearing it down, but you are always, always branding . That’s why we need to mention VP.Start’s most peculiar type of branding. VP.Start frequently holds workshops and forums aimed at university and high school students. Building the brand. Burnishing the reputation. One notably strange condition, however. 320

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Methodology Innovators Love Collaboration “Great things in business are never done by one person; they are done by a team of people
searchIndex.text: These students are not able to become customers, not at this point. Too young to buy their own IoT devices. Unlikely to participate in the SIMA City Initiatives or SIMA Smart Grid modernization. What is the purpose of building up branding to those who are not potential customers or investors? This comes back to the meaning of branding. The purpose is surprisingly simple: Branding is what we do, not because we want to acquire and keep customers, not because we want to persuade investors, not because we want to impress potential collaborative partners, not because we want to amaze government stakeholders, but because , simply, that is who we are. Branding is not a gimmick. Branding is not a strategic plan. Branding is not a high pressure sales technique. Branding is VP.Start being itself, the team being themselves, us being ourselves . At the end of the day, branding, true branding, is about being yourself. Your authentic self. Your imperfect self. Your vulnerable self. Are you brave enough to “become your own branding” without gimmicks, strategies or pressure? Respect to you, if that is your decision! 321 Chapter 6 The SIMA Methodology Innovators Love Collaboration “Great things in business are never done by one person; they are done by a team of people.” -Steve Jobs “When you need to innovate, you need collaboration.” -Marissa Mayer, former CEO of Yahoo! Let me tell you a contradiction . In traditional Asian spiritual thought, contradictions can often lead us to deeper truths. First, a true innovator and founder MUST stand alone. Simultaneously, innovation requires teamwork and collaboration. How can both of these be true at the same time? The SIMA Methodology rests on individuality AND partnering, isolation AND connection, learning from others AND ignoring others. This is not an easy concept to grasp. This is not an easy methodology to implement. But the SIMA Journey does not go forward without it. Let’s break this down a bit. First, an innovator must stand alone. A founder must be true to his vision even though at times, his own team doesn’t understand it. The team may love the founder’s vision and they will FBR (feel, believe and remember) the vision but 322

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Methodology Innovators Love Collaboration “Great things in business are never done by one person; they are done by a team of people
searchIndex.text: they won’t be able to really completely fathom the vision. That is not a problem, not really. The innovator must spend time alone, with himself, quietly. Before an important conference, Steve Jobs would famously often “disappear” for a few weeks, leaving others in charge with instructions to disturb him only in case of emergency. Similarly, Phally often “disappears”, spending time in nature or with underprivileged kids or especially, at the pagoda. His management team knows that his time alone is often more productive than his time in the office so they give him ample space to be himself. By himself. With himself. No distractions. No disruptions. No disturbances. If you want to become an innovator, you must find time to be “with yourself ” Are you ready to find time to spend with yourself in the midst of your busy schedule? It will not be easy to find that time, to be sure, but will you proactively set aside that time? Do you value yourself, your time and your ideas enough to remove all interruptions? While an innovator must be alone with her or his thoughts and must adamantly refuse to copy or imitate others, innovation requires collaboration. Innovators love collaboration. 323 Innovation grows through collaboration. Collaboration springs from a mindset. The detailed contracts and legal frameworks, the MoUs and joint ventures that make up the legal side of collaboration will never work unless all the parties involved have a collaborative mindset . VP.Start values, emphasizes and prioritizes teamwork and collaborative partnership. Why? Do you have a collaborative mindset? Are you always looking for opportunities to work with others? Do you see teamwork and partnership as key pillars of your methodology? Innovation never thrives ALONE. First of all, no one person has all the answers. Einstein did not. Professor Richard Feynman did not. Stephen Hawkins did not. Neither did Alan Turing . Steve Jobs did not and CEO Phally does not either. To state the blindingly obvious. If you don’t have all the answers, you need to work with others. When done properly , this does not weaken your ideas, it makes them stronger . Do you have all the answers? Do you even know all the questions? If not, wouldn’t it be wise to collaborate with people who are strong in areas that you are particularly weak in? 324

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Methodology Innovators Love Collaboration “Great things in business are never done by one person; they are done by a team of people
searchIndex.text: VP.Start does not try to do everything , handle every aspect of every business operation, micromanage every detail and process. VP.Start has no desire to become an enormous conglomerate, a slow-moving behemoth with a massive workforce and monstrous campus . VP.Start intentionally chooses to remain agile and flexible , quickly able to respond to changes in the tech sector. Do you need to micromanage every detail of your operation? Do you need to constantly oversee every aspect of your innovative solutions? People who cannot let go and delegate and outsource are defeated by their own limitations. Without exception. VP.Start is wisely building partnerships and relationships with OEMs and outsourcing parts of the sustainability system, such as aspects that include: construction of infrastructure, manufacturing of IoT equipment and building an AI support structure for the SIMA Journey. VP.Start is not an expert company in construction. VP.Start is not an expert company in manufacturing. VP.Start is not an expert company in AI Data Center building. VP.Start could try to master all of those areas, I suppose, but they choose to focus on innovation and ideas . Sometimes the greatest superpower that a company or an innovator can have is the ability to see their own limitations. What are some areas where your skills and talents are limited? What are some parts of your innovative dream that you should delegate to others? What are the core aspects that you MUST keep for yourself? 325 Are you clear on the distinction between the core aspects and the outsourceable parts of your innovation? The overarching sustainability system has an almost infinite number of components, from renewable energy integration to EV adoption, from AI infusion to telecommunication implementation, from data storage to energy storage to battery storage. It would be unwise for VP.Start to try to master all of these components. Completely impossible and completely unnecessary. There are already powerful companies working in each of these areas. VP.Start intends to keep its focus on its big picture missions and delegate these myriad of smaller detail aspects of the sustainability system to others. If you want to become an innovator, you must keep your methodology focused on the big picture . Do you feel like your methodology has a clear, big picture focus? What aspects of your methodology would you do well to change to better align with your ideas? Of course, while collaboration and delegation are important methodological approaches, OEMs and other potential partners need to be selected and screened carefully based on their skills , their research and development abilities and their capabilities to complete work in a timely fashion at a high level of quality. VP.Start is constantly ascertaining whether or not its OEM partners are providing work of sufficient quality. After all, VP.Start’s name and brand are on the solutions. If the manufacturing, testing, quality control or after service are subpar, customer and users will not blame the OEMs. 326

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Methodology Innovators Love Collaboration “Great things in business are never done by one person; they are done by a team of people
searchIndex.text: The blame will fall on VP.Start. As, of course, it should. When you delegate and outsource, you take on more risk. But VP.Start has always made the decision to embrace risk over inflexibility , delegation over excessive workload and creative big picture thinking over micromanagement. VP.Start chooses business, not busyness. Every time. Collaboration, delegation and outsourcing always involve risks. Are you ready to embrace the risks if they help you become more agile and flexible? If you are truly open to collaboration, if you are truly in possession of a win-win mindset, if you are truly willing to make sure that your partner benefits as much as you do, you don’t need to search for partners. In VP.Start’s experience, MoUs with government ministries, educational institutions, international organizations and fellow industrial associations have been signed when these heterogeneous stakeholders sought out the Sen Sok Valley Campus. We don’t search for partners. Partners search for us. Innovative companies are always like that. One especially unusual example occurred recently 327 when two companies, SNKRP, a local, Cambodian construction and manufacturing company and Huawei, the Chinese tech conglomerate, met for informal collaboration talks. Two companies meeting to discuss potential areas of collaboration is not so out of the ordinary. A fairly common business scenario. However, what makes the situation unique is that they met and discussed and negotiated under the auspices of VP.Start at the SIMA Journey Annex on the VP.Start campus. Why would two unrelated companies meet together at VP.Start? First of all, VP.Start has close relations with both companies , which is especially interesting in the case of Huawei, since it was VP.Start’s ecosolutions that replaced those of Huawei with the EDC. You might reasonably expect that Huawei would harbor less than kind feelings towards a rival, but in this case, things are quite different. Huawei feels respect for VP.Start, camaraderie and a willingness to work together. SNKRP, on the other hand, is a company founded by a long-time friend of Phally who Phally considers something of a mentor or teacher. So, VP.Start brought the two companies together, not because it would benefit VP.Start directly, or even indirectly , but because the collaboration of these two parties would help further sustainability in Cambodia. True innovators and truly innovative companies love collaboration and foster collaboration even when that collaboration does not include themselves directly or indirectly. True innovators seek a better future and 328

searchIndex.title: Chapter 6 The SIMA Methodology Innovators Love Collaboration “Great things in business are never done by one person; they are done by a team of people
searchIndex.text: are not so concerned about how that better future is achieved . Phally and the VP.Start team provided a location, logistical support and professional guidance to help a collaboration move forward. A collaboration between two OTHER companies . Are you willing to support collaboration for the good of innovation, even when you are not directly involved in that collaboration? Do you embrace progress whether you are directly involved or not? This is the advanced stage of the true innovator. Are you up to the challenge? The most powerful collaboration, by far, for VP.Start, is its close relationship with the EDC. The utility has been willing to adopt the DRC and other IoT solutions on very favorable terms, helping VP.Start overcome its lack of outside investment support. VP.Start has sent teams, often spearheaded by Phally, himself, to give training sessions and workshops at all 16 local headquarters of the EDC, to make sure that the solutions are being used to maximum efficiency. This is an essential part of the collaborative mindset and methodology. Reciprocity. For VP.Start, collaboration is always a two-way street. EDC provides feasible, doable financial terms. VP.Start provides extensive training. Everyone benefits. VP.Start would never want to enter into a relationship where they provide all the benefits to the other party. Obviously. But by the same token, 329 VP.Start would not be willing to receive benefits from their partner if they could not provide any. Mutually beneficial. Win-win. In the near future, the VP.Start team will travel to China and shortly thereafter, Japan and South Korea, in search of more collaborative OEM partners . Once again, let me remind you that collaboration is not a business plan. It is not a strategy. It is not approach to gain value capture. It is a methodology based on a mindset . A mindset that says, “We need help from others. We do not know everything. We can provide help to others. We know some things that others do not know. We do not need to do everything. We can delegate and outsource. We are stronger together. We grow faster together.” The SIMA Journey moves forward together. The time has come to make a choice. Do you want to be a true innovator? Are you willing to adopt a collaborative mindset? The SIMA Journey advances. Are you ready to participate? 330

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Methodology Predicting the Future with Digital Twins “Trying to predict the future is like trying to drive down a country road at night with no lights while looking out the back window
searchIndex.text: Chapter 7 The SIMA Methodology Predicting the Future with Digital Twins “Trying to predict the future is like trying to drive down a country road at night with no lights while looking out the back window.” -Peter Drucker, Investor and Futurist Digital twin technology is an important part of the SIMA Methodology. A core component. A mission critical element. Many people would consider digital twinning to be a cutting edge, state of the art technology. Phally would disagree. According to him, digital twinning is as old as human life on earth and maybe much older than that. Why does Phally say that? Digital twinning is simply taking data and making predictions based on the data . How effectively do you use data in your daily life? What does that suggest to you about how effectively you use data in your innovations? For example, as I get ready to go outside in the morning, I look out and see that it is a cloudy, overcast day. I grab my umbrella. 331 Why do I do that? I am making a prediction based on the available, limited data. I am creating a mental digital twin. However, let me ask you, when it is cloudy, does it always rain? Of course not. I might take the umbrella needlessly. I don’t have enough data, enough actionable intelligence, to make a highly accurate prediction. But I could opt to get the weather forecast from an online app, based on data gathered from IoT devices. I could acquire more data , better data, more thoroughly tested data. Now my data is much more reliable and accurate…but still not perfect. For example, the app might tell me that there is a 75% chance of rain. I will probably take my umbrella in that case But I realize that there is still a 25% chance that it will not rain. This example shows the fundamental ideas of the digital twin. Gathering more and more accurate data. Taking into account more and more factors . Covering more and more of the big picture. Building a more and more high-fidelity replica. But…. never achieving absolute identicality. And since that is the case, always striving to further upgrade and become more and more accurate. In an endless loop. Do your innovative solutions and products continually leverage more data? Are they in a constant stage of upgrading and approaching greater fidelity? 332

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Methodology Predicting the Future with Digital Twins “Trying to predict the future is like trying to drive down a country road at night with no lights while looking out the back window
searchIndex.text: You can think of digital twin technology as answering two questions: How do we make predictions more accurately? How do we continuously upgrade the data that we base our predicitons on? VP.Start is aggressively moving to integrate digital twin technology into every aspect of the SIMA Journey, all five missions: the SIMA Smart Grid, the SIMA Smart City, the SIMA Home, the SIMA Universal Connectivity Network app and SIMA Big Data. The more accurate the predictions, the better the results. The faster the data is collected and upgraded, the more accurate the predictions. The more DRC devices deployed, the faster data is collected and upgraded. This is a positive cycle that benefits everyone. Are you determined to introduce data-driven digital twin concepts into every aspect of your ideas? In the case of the SIMA Smart Grid, digital twins are used to create a digital replica of the entire grid architecture. This is an indispensable step in the methodology of SIMA grid modernization. First of all, digital twins monitor every aspect of the electricity network from massive power generation plants and BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) complexes down to small components like individual substations and smart meters. Everything placed into one digital model for easy visualization and management. Bottlenecks can be recognized and alleviated instantly. Battery storage systems can be charged and discharged with maximum efficiency. Supply and demand can be varied instantly to reduce volatility and outage frequency and duration can be shrunk dramatically. 333 Everything based on data accumulated and updated by DRC series IoT sensors and meters instantly and continuously. Secondly, digital twins can be used powerfully for predictive maintenance of equipment. Conventionally, infrastructure and grid equipment has an arbitrary lifespan . At the end of a fixed time period, infrastructure must be replaced. Automatically. After all, who has enough time to monitor every component of infrastructure. Twinning changes everything. Digital twin technology monitors the data that shows functionality and efficiency of the equipment. As long as the equipment is functioning well, it is kept in service. As data shows the onset of potential issues, the equipment is replaced BEFORE it fails . Less unnecessary replacement. Less equipment failure. Better outcomes. On the third hand, if I had three hands , digital twins allow operators to test out scenarios on the grid that would be expensive and dangerous to test in the real world. Cyberattacks. Severe weather events. Excessive peak demand situations. Physical line breaks and equipment failures. Digital twins allow operators to find the best solutions 334

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Methodology Predicting the Future with Digital Twins “Trying to predict the future is like trying to drive down a country road at night with no lights while looking out the back window
searchIndex.text: to problems that might occur , so they can try to make sure that these predicaments never do occur , or if they do, there is a plan in hand for them to be mitigated effortlessly. On more major benefit of digital twin technology is effective integration of renewables into the grid. Renewables are important for a sustainable, carbon footprint reducing SIMA future and yet, renewables present considerable challenges when they are integrated into the power network. Intermittency. Unreliability. Weaker power generation. Digital twins take these factors into account with data, data, data. Weather data. Power Generation data. Demand data. Battery storage data. Conventional fossil fuel generation data. Big Data. Harnessed by AI capabilities. Are your solutions leveraging Big Data and DIgital Twins to their maximum efficiency? Taking digital twin technology to the next level, 335 we can create a digital twin of an entire city, an “urban brain”, if you will, a replica that is based on all gathered IoT data converged into one digital twin. Moving urban planning from guesswork and assumptions to data-based predictions. Moving the SIMA City Initiatives from imagination to reality. Digital twinning can improve traffic systems and mobility. You simply cannot have a smart city without mobility. Digital twins can be used to test infrastructure like bridges and new road construction safely. To optimize recycling systems, waste collection and storage . To upgrade emergency prediction and management such as flood preparedness and response. To enhance sustainable urbanization and population growth. The SIMA City Digital Twin combines three key parts: data collection by IoT devices, visualization and mapping on the UCN app and intelligent application of the acquired actionable insights for augmented urban outcomes. Creating a replica of the city so we can recreate a better original city. Digital twin technology also comes into play in SIMA Smart Home Automation. Digital twin technology moves home automation from individual, disconnected, siloed appliances to an overarching replica of the entire digital home . The entire energy footprint of a home is monitored digitally. This can be used for smart shedding , a process where autonomous raising or lowering of smart curtains based on real-time temperature and weather data can lead to greatly reduced household energy costs. 336

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Methodology Predicting the Future with Digital Twins “Trying to predict the future is like trying to drive down a country road at night with no lights while looking out the back window
searchIndex.text: Similar to monitoring grid infrastructure, individual appliances can be monitored by data to determine lifespan and degradation. No unnecessary replacements, no unexpected appliance failures. Proactive warnings to alert us to imminent appliance and gadget failure to avoid emergencies and reduce waste. For example, if a refrigerator fails unexpectedly, a lot of food could be lost. If the failure could be predicted and the refrigerator replaced BEFORE problems occur, waste is greatly reduced . Thanks to the digital twin, these inconvenient scenarios can be avoided. Similar protections can be afforded to water and electricity systems that are monitored by IoT devices and fed into the personal home digital twin. This, of course, can be applied to offices, shops, restaurants, businesses, factories, schools, hospitals and so on and so on . A digital version of your home to improve the quality of your life in your own physical home. Digital twins can improve grid operations, urban experiences and home automation. How are digital twin technologies 337 improving the experiences of the customers of your innovative products? The UCN takes all that digital twin data and brings it into visualization . One significant problem of digital twins is that they are digital. And we are not. While a digital twin inhabits the artificial world , so to speak, we live in the physical, material world. So when the digital twin creates benefits and insights and actionable intelligence in the virtual world, we need to find a way to bring that into the tangible world, our world. That is one of the functions of the UCN. AlienCheck connects us to our IoT-infused devices, our IoT managed cities and our IoT monitored and operated smart grid. In other words, AlienCheck puts us in contact with the variety of SIMA digital twins, but in a way that we can understand. You see, digital twins speak the language of data, the language of coding, the language of the digital future. Unless we are data analysts or data scientists, we are probably not very fluent in digital language. You can think of the UCN as a translator that helps us communicate with the IoT devices and by extension, the digital twins, themselves, while enabling them to get in touch with us as well. Our SIMA digital twin methodology brings about the interface of man and machine, natural and artificial, digital and physical. 338

searchIndex.title: Chapter 7 The SIMA Methodology Predicting the Future with Digital Twins “Trying to predict the future is like trying to drive down a country road at night with no lights while looking out the back window
searchIndex.text: Our final mission, SIMA Big Data , absolutely depends on digital twin technology. We follow three main processes: acquire data, simulate scenarios with data and apply data. As we acquire data , we are building the skeleton of the digital twin. A digital twin requires copious amounts of data, clean, accurate data, continuous data, a wide variety of data. But a skeleton is not going to walk very far. As we start to use this data in simulations, we are putting the flesh and muscle onto the bones of the digital twin. We make millions upon millions of simulations with slight variations, all performed virtually simultaneously , until we find the simulation that best fits the data. But a skeleton covered with skin and muscles is still not alive . When we start to apply the data into real-world tests and pilots in the SIMA Grid, SIMA City and SIMA Home, the digital twin roars to life. But, of course, tests have results an they are not always exactly what we might have expected or hoped for. This creates a new wave of data rushing back to fortify the skeleton, starting the process again. Upgrading. Endlessly. Relentlessly. Unflinchingly. This brings us back to the digital twin mindset. The two questions. How do we make predictions more accurately? 339 How do we continuously upgrade the data that we based our predicitons on? Every loop in our amazing cycle of upgrading brings us a step closer to perfect accuracy. Absolute identicality . A digital twin in the true meaning of the word “twin. ” A step closer and yet, perfection remains elusive. A 100% identical replica remains an unreachable goal. At VP.Start, this effort to access the inaccessible, this bold approach to the unapproachable, this attempt to reach the unreachable, it moves us forward. After all, we seek a true sustainability system for a sustainable world. This, too, is an attempt to reach the unreachable. Is a sustainable world even possible? Maybe no. Will we achieve a sustainable world in our lifetimes? Probably no. Is it going to be easy to get there? Absolutely no. Will we stop striving and trying to achieve a sustainable future? Definitely no. Some tasks are challenging. Others are truly daunting. And a few tasks are unreachable. Do your solutions and innovative ideas take us closer and closer to the unreachable ideal? Do you leverage data-driven and digital twin technology in a way to improve outcomes? 340

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Methodology The SIMA Journey is Green “The best way to achieve a green revolution is to have innovative, greenable ideas
searchIndex.text: Chapter 8 The SIMA Methodology The SIMA Journey is Green “The best way to achieve a green revolution is to have innovative, greenable ideas.” -CEO Phally Nowadays everybody is talking about green . Green energy. Green solutions. Green products. Green technology. Green strategies. Green investment in green companies. A green planet with a green future. Unfortunately, the one “green” that you rarely hear about is “green ideas” . At VP.Start, we insist that you can never achieve any methodology without having ideas first. No green ideas? No green methodology. No green methodology? No green future. Ideas always come first. With your innovative solutions, do ideas always come first? Are your green products and green services built on the foundation of green ideas? You might not think that VP.Start is a green company. We don’t manufacture solar panels or wind turbines. We don’t invest in renewable energy generation. We are not involved in lobbying the government for more environmental 341 legislation. We don’t do research and development of green, carbon-friendly strategies. Not directly. But, we at VP.Start are clear on one key point. The best green solutions are solutions that make the grid and power generation more efficient and less wasteful . Renewable energy is not going to be very useful if the power system is full of leakages and outages, waste and faults, power losses and inefficient storage. Wasted energy hurts the environment even if that energy was generated “greenly” . As a matter of fact, it is better to have conventional power generation with fossil fuels when losses and waste are kept to the bare minimum than to have solar and wind generated power that is overwhelmingly wasted and mishandled . Do your solutions do more harm than good? Do your ideas keep losses, waste and inefficiencies to the bare minimum? Furthermore, green energy solutions that are highly effective but prohibitively expensive , are not really effective at all. Governments and industries will not adopt solutions, no matter how great they are, if they are excessively expensive. SIMA Green ideas require grid efficiency and require it to be affordable. 342

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Methodology The SIMA Journey is Green “The best way to achieve a green revolution is to have innovative, greenable ideas
searchIndex.text: Are your ideas both amazingly innovative and affordable? Many solutions have one or the other but very few have both. The VP.Start mindset is sustainability-driven . Let me reiterate. The SIMA mindset is sustainability-driven. The SIMA Journey has one destination : a sustainability system for a sustainable future for our planet. Reducing our carbon footprint and protecting the environment are important in their own right but they are just components of the overarching sustainability system. So, how can the SIMA Smart grid modernization solutions make the grid and the overall power system greener? The greenest energy is the energy that we never have to generate in the first place. Let me give you an example. When electricity travels long distances on the transmission lines, some power is lost as heat. These “line losses” force greater generation of energy than is really used. The data-driven digital twin-infused SIMA grid solutions can recognize these losses in the data. This, in turn, can lead to actionable intelligence for preventative maintenance such as upgrading the materials of certain portion of the transmission line network. Reducing losses and waste. Sustainable. Further more, data can indicate cases 343 where using High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) is advantageous over conventional High Voltage Alternating Current (HVAC). HVAC changes directions frequently whereas HVDC flows in one direction only. In the case of long distance transmission lines, HVDC use can reduce friction and diminish energy losses and leakages. This is especially useful when renewable energy sources like wind turbines or solar farms are in remote areas, as is often the case. It is also absolutely necessary for underwater cables in island nations like the Philippines. The data-driven solutions of the SIMA Journey can indicate when these special measures need to be taken and, on the other hand, when more conventional approaches are sufficient. In this way, the DRC series reduces the cost of unnecessary distribution line changes while simultaneously reducing wasted energy when transmission line upgrades are needed. With Big Data in hand, we can choose highly accurately where to make changes and where not to make them. A greener future based on grid modernization technology. 344

searchIndex.title: Chapter 8 The SIMA Methodology The SIMA Journey is Green “The best way to achieve a green revolution is to have innovative, greenable ideas
searchIndex.text: Do your innovations solve problems of waste and problems of cost simultaneously? Another way in which SIMA Smart grid solutions can promote a greenable tomorrow are in terms of promoting the Electrification “of Everything” (EoE). Electric buses. Electric trains. Electric vehicles. Electric subways. Electrification of the entire transportation infrastructure. This electrification can greatly reduce fossil fuel usage , carbon emissions, pollution and promote renewables integration . But it can only succeed, if the grid is resilient enough to handle the added demand of EV charging stations. To facilitate meeting this increased demand, the SIMA Smart Grid anticipates peak demand by predictive data analysis and staggers charging to reduce excess consumption at any one time. For one example, most electric buses and vehicles charge at night which puts a strain on grid capacity . Data-driven solutions spread out the charging while preparing the required excess energy. A resilient battery storage system that can be efficiently integrated into the system as needed is mission critical to this overall spreading and shedding strategy . Based on the data-driven solutions of VP.Start, this process becomes possible. Every new advancement, such as EV adoption or renewables integration, 345 brings new challenges. Are your solutions adaptable enough to face the challenges, not just current ones, but those of the future, as well? Another issue on the road to a more greenable economic future is how to cope with increasingly extreme climate events. Climate change is causing more severe weather development worldwide, including increased wildfires, storms and unprecedented heat waves . In addition to being harmful to nature and people directly, these events have a negative impact on the electric grid and grid infrastructure that must be mitigated by a resilient grid that has self-healing capabilities . For instance, the IoT sensors deployed by VP.Start can instantly recognize a line that has fallen due to environmental factors or a line that has been compromised or damaged due to various extreme weather events. Automatically, within milliseconds, the power flow can be rerouted to avoid the damaged section , which can be isolated and subsequently repaired, either remotely or in person, depending on the damage. No loss of service. No loss of energy. No waste. That is the methodology of VP.Start . Problems will happen. More often, more seriously and of more duration. Do your innovative solutions take these problems into account? Do they leverage problems as opportunities for systemic growth and advancement? Intermittent renewable power generation requires the data-driven 346

searchIndex.title: Chapter 9 The SIMA Methodology A Deep Dive Into the LMS System “ Your power transformer is not aging in isolation
searchIndex.text: VP.Start is a company based on “Innovation through Technology” . “Innovation” means the amazing, outside the box, creative ideas, the dreams that form the vision of the SIMA Journey. On the other hand, “Technology” means the detailed plans and projects, equipment and gadgets, the hardware and the software, that make these dreams come true. While we tend to glorify the Big Picture ideas and honor the sweeping vision and respect the impossible dreams, we cannot forget the engineering technology that makes those ideas, vision and dreams come to life. Do you have the technology in hand to back up your innovative ideas ? Do you have the innovation in hand to give meaning to your technology ? One of the the key components of the grid, whether conventional grid or smart grid, are the transformers . If you believe in transformation, as Phally does, You need powerful, effective, hardworking transformers. Transformers are used to raise voltage or lower voltage as needed. When energy is generated in a power plant, it is at a very high voltage. This voltage is maintained as the electricity travels long distances on the transmission lines. This is necessary because electricity traveling at a high voltage will have less leakage from the power lines because of facing less resistance. 349 However, high voltage cannot be delivered to a standard house or shop. It would create an explosion. Therefore, we need transformers. Transformers are required to reduce the voltage to safe levels : medium voltage for large businesses, factories, hospitals and the like, low voltage for distribution to individual houses. When transformers are working effectively, The SIMA Smart grid runs smoothly, outages are diminished and energy loss is kept to a bare minimum . When the transformers are ineffective, outages increase, leakages become more frequent and infrastructure degradation accelerates significantly . When transformers fail, this can cause major, lengthy outages , costly and time consuming repairs and equipment damage or failure . So, it goes without saying that transformer proactive maintenance and preventive monitoring by means of data analysis is absolutely essential. It is at this point that the LMS System comes into play. What systems do you have in place to make sure that the key components of your innovations: Do not fail? Work effectively? Are maintained preventatively and proactively? The LMS System (Low Voltage Management System) is an integrated 350

Furthermore, it is indispensable in reducing outages and power failures . LMS utilization can lead to dramatic reductions in CAPEX (Capital Expenditures) , in other words, the upfront costs of building and installing infrastructure while SIMULTANEOUSLY decreasing significantly OPEX (Operational Expenditures) , the cost to operate and maintain infrastructure. Finally, LMS adoption can enable better SIMA Smart Grid operations for greater data-driven loss reductions and more digitized asset management by the EDC. In layman’s terms, cost savings, waste reduction, greater efficiency. Yes, SUSTAINABILITY. The SIMA Methodology practices involved here are critical to notice. Don’t let the Methodology get lost in the technical details of the previous paragraph. Simply stated, we solve problems! But invariably, solving problems creates new ones . ALWAYS! Think about it this way: How many car accidents were there 300 years ago ? How many traffic jams were there 300 years ago ? How many parking issues? 351 Drunk driving? Speeding? Dangerous driving? Similarly, issues of electric grid functions and operation and efficiency did not exist when there was no electric grid. In other words, each new development, each new advancement, each new technology , creates problems that did not exist before. Remember, nuclear weapons were never a problem BEFORE nuclear energy was discovered. The SIMA Methodology comes in 3 steps: 1) Solve “old” problems, 2) Discover the “new” problems that arise with these solutions and Solve these “new” problems (which, of course, creates more “new” problems). In an endless creative loop. What problems do your solutions create? Do you have solutions to the problems created by your solutions? Do you have the mindset required to continuously solve “new” problems as they arise?
